ten: BICYCLE AND OTHER RUDIMENTARY VEHICLE DRIVERS
mo_ta: The people covered by Article 9: drivers of bicycles, motorized bicycles, and other rudimentary vehicles
The people operating bicycles, motorized bicycles, or other rudimentary vehicles; Article 9, Clause 1 sets penalties for drivers who commit the listed riding-abreast violations.
A person operating a bicycle, included among the drivers subject to the listed road-traffic penalties.
People operating bicycles who are subject to the traffic rules and fines described in Article 9.
BICYCLE OPERATORS are people operating bicycles who are subject to the traffic rules and penalties set out in Article 9, including the penalties in Clause 2, if they commit the specified violation.

A road traffic violation under Article 9 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, committed when a bicycle, motorized bicycle, or cyclo carries more people than permitted. The stated fine is from 100,000 to 200,000 Vietnamese đồng.

id: bicycle riding abreast in groups of three or more
ten: BICYCLE RIDING ABREAST IN GROUPS OF THREE OR MORE
mo_ta: A traffic violation described in Article 9, Clause 1 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP: operating bicycles or motorized bicycles abreast in a group of at least three vehicles.

id: bicycle, motor-assisted bicycle, and other rudimentary-vehicle operators
ten: BICYCLE, MOTOR-ASSISTED BICYCLE, AND OTHER RUDIMENTARY-VEHICLE OPERATORS
mo_ta: The category of road users covered by Article 9, Clause 3 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, including operators who swerve or weave, or chase one another on the road.
A curved section of road where the driver's view is obstructed, where making a U-turn is prohibited under Article 15.

**BLOOD ALCOHOL LIMIT VIOLATION** is a road traffic violation involving the operation of a bicycle, motorized bicycle, or other rudimentary vehicle with a blood alcohol concentration above 50 mg and up to 80 mg per 100 ml of blood. The violation is described in Article 9, Clause 3 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP.
The preservation and transfer of a blood sample to a testing facility when the healthcare facility is unable to conduct the required tests.
Testing a vehicle operator’s blood for alcohol, drugs, or other stimulants after a road traffic accident.
The event of entering a ferry, during which pedestrians board before road vehicles, which proceed according to the traffic controller’s directions.
Examination of bodies directly connected to a road traffic accident
BORDER GATE is a border-crossing location where vehicles may be transferred to or from a warehouse, port, or store. A police post or police station may also operate or be situated there.

id: border gates under the ministry of national defence’s management
ten: BORDER GATES UNDER THE MINISTRY OF NATIONAL DEFENCE’S MANAGEMENT
mo_ta: Border gates under the Ministry of National Defence’s jurisdiction, where it organizes exit and entry inspections and controls and carries out border procedures.
Police posts at border gates and in export-processing zones whose chiefs may impose administrative sanctions for specified road traffic violations within their assigned functions and duties.
A police station serving a border gate or export processing zone; its chief is listed among the officials authorized to apply specified remedial measures.

id: border-gate or export-processing-zone police post chief
ten: BORDER-GATE OR EXPORT-PROCESSING-ZONE POLICE POST CHIEF
mo_ta: The chief of a police post at a border gate or export processing zone, authorized within assigned duties to impose administrative sanctions for specified road traffic order and safety violations.
A police station located at a border gate or in an export processing zone; its chief is granted authority under Article 41 to sanction specified road-traffic violations.

id: border-gate or export-processing-zone police station chief
ten: BORDER-GATE OR EXPORT-PROCESSING-ZONE POLICE STATION CHIEF
mo_ta: The **BORDER-GATE OR EXPORT-PROCESSING-ZONE POLICE STATION CHIEF** is the head of a police station located at a border gate or in an export-processing zone. Under Article 41 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, the chief may, within the functions and duties assigned to the station, impose administrative penalties for specified violations involving road-traffic order and safety. Article 43, Clause 3, authorizes the chief to impose fines of up to 2,500,000 Vietnamese đồng and to seize objects or vehicles used in administrative violations when their value does not exceed 5,000,000 đồng.
A police post at a border gate whose chief is granted authority to impose specified administrative sanctions under the decree.
The head of a police post at a border gate, authorized under Article 41 to impose administrative sanctions for specified road traffic violations within the assigned scope of duties.

The BORDER-GATE POLICE STATION’s chief is authorized under Articles 41 and 43, including Article 43, Clause 3, to impose administrative penalties for specified road-traffic violations relating to traffic order and safety, within the chief’s assigned functions and duties.

The BORDER-GATE POLICE STATION CHIEF is the official who heads a police station at a border gate. Under Article 43 of the decree, the chief is authorized to impose penalties and apply specified remedial measures.
Police stations at border gates whose chiefs are authorized, within assigned duties, to impose administrative penalties for specified road traffic violations.
A type of dependent enterprise unit listed in the text.
A branch of a credit institution, mentioned in connection with the receipt accompanying a certified copy of a vehicle registration certificate.

BREATH ALCOHOL LIMIT VIOLATION refers to a road traffic violation involving operation of a vehicle with a breath alcohol concentration above 0.25 mg and up to 0.4 mg per liter of breath. Under Article 9, Clause 3 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, this includes operating a bicycle, motorized bicycle, or other rudimentary vehicle while over that limit.

BRIDGE is a structure built over or across an obstacle. Under Article 15 and the stated traffic rules, vehicles may not make U-turns on a bridge unless an applicable exception permits it. Parking on a bridge is also prohibited when it obstructs traffic.
**BRIDGE APPROACH** refers to the area at the beginning, entrance, or end of a bridge. Under Article 15, making a U-turn there is prohibited unless an applicable exception allows it.
Damage to a bridge or road caused by a driver’s administrative violation.
Road infrastructure identified in the decree as potentially damaged by covered administrative violations and subject to restoration.
Infrastructure that may be damaged by the specified transport violation.
The burial of a deceased person following a road traffic accident, arranged by the commune-level People's Committee after the competent state agency consents.

BUS STATIONS are facilities where road users may be required to observe, slow down, or stop to ensure safety. They are also places where road inspectors may conduct inspections and checks under the applicable provisions.
A BUS-ONLY ROAD is a road or lane reserved for bus traffic. Stopping and parking are prohibited on it under the cited provisions.
The commercial activity of dealing in signal-emitting devices for priority vehicles, which must satisfy legally prescribed security and public-order conditions.
BÀI KIỂM TRA is the examination addressed in Article 6. The article sets out its content, method, timing, and structure, as well as the criteria for achieving a satisfactory result.

id: bồi dưỡng, kiểm tra và cấp chứng chỉ
ten: BỒI DƯỠNG, KIỂM TRA VÀ CẤP CHỨNG CHỈ
mo_ta: The activity of providing road-traffic-law instruction, testing participants, and issuing certificates to those who achieve a passing result.

BỘ CÔNG AN (BCA) is Vietnam’s Ministry of Public Security. The “BCA” designation appears in references to Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA and Circular 105/2026/TT-BCA; the minister is identified as the issuer of Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA. The Traffic Police Department operates under the Ministry and is associated with the dossier-submission channel. The Ministry is also responsible for receiving reports of difficulties or obstacles arising during implementation of the circulars and providing timely guidance. Relevant authorities are to notify its traffic police agency of authorized movements by oversized, overweight, or tracked vehicles.
Bộ Công an (the Ministry of Public Security) is identified by the “BCA” designation in the circular number 65/2024/TT-BCA.

BỘ GIAO THÔNG VẬN TẢI (Vietnam’s Ministry of Transport), abbreviated BGTVT in official circular designations and numbers, assigns expressways to designated agencies for management. The Ministry also built and manages the database of inspections for motor vehicles and specialized motorcycles, and receives information and data collected by vehicle journey-monitoring devices.
The Ministry of Construction, whose minister may establish an inspection team whose head is identified in Article 44 as having sanctioning authority.

id: bộ, ngành và cơ quan ở trung ương
ten: BỘ, NGÀNH VÀ CƠ QUAN Ở TRUNG ƯƠNG
mo_ta: The central-level ministries, sectors, and agencies whose eligible vehicles may be registered with the Traffic Police Department for permits for priority-vehicle signal equipment.

A theoretical legal-knowledge examination for applicants holding a C1 driving licence. It lasts 22 minutes and consists of 35 multiple-choice questions worth one point each, including one critical question. A score of at least 32 out of 35 is required, but an incorrect answer to the critical question results in failure.
A person holding a C1-class driving licence who takes the legal-knowledge test described in the text.

The **cancellation of the auction result** applies when the winning bidder dies within the prescribed period before completing the required vehicle-registration steps. The descriptions identify two relevant deadlines: death within 12 months without registering the vehicle to attach the plate, and death within 30 days before receiving the confirmation decision. The applicable deadline depends on the stage or rule governing the case.
The process of comparing an examinee’s identity documents or available electronic identity information with the details in the examination application.
A test candidate whose result does not meet the requirements and who may register for a retake.
People taking the theoretical legal knowledge examination described in the text.

id: car breakdown at a road-rail level crossing
ten: CAR BREAKDOWN AT A ROAD-RAIL LEVEL CROSSING
mo_ta: A car becoming damaged or disabled at a level crossing where a road intersects a railway.

A **CAR DRIVER** is a person operating a car who may be subject to penalties for violating transportation regulations. The specified violations include transporting oversized or overweight cargo, addressed in Article 22; transporting certain dangerous goods through tunnels at least 100 metres long, addressed in Article 23; and the transportation-rule violation described in Article 24. For oversized or overweight cargo violations, the driver may receive a penalty and have points deducted from their driving licence.
An auction of a car vehicle license plate, for which the starting price must be at least 40 million đồng.

Auctions of automobile license plates. Article 89 provides transitional rules for auctions conducted before Law 36/2024/QH15 took effect, directing some cases to continue under Resolution 73/2022/QH15.
The falsification of a car’s distance-indicator reading, which the text identifies as requiring corrective adjustment.

An individual who owns the car in a vehicle combination. If the car owner is not also the owner of the towed trailer or semi-trailer, the car owner may nevertheless be treated as the vehicle owner for sanctions concerning violations involving that trailer or semi-trailer.

People learning to drive cars who, while participating in road traffic, must practice in a training vehicle on a designated training route under the supervision of a driving instructor or driving test examiner
The required practice activity for people learning to drive cars, conducted in a training vehicle on a designated training route under supervision
The car-driving examination, conducted in a test vehicle on a designated test route under supervision
People taking a car-driving test who, while participating in road traffic, must use a test vehicle on a designated test route under the supervision of a driving instructor or driving test examiner
A designated route on which people taking a car-driving test must use a test vehicle while participating in road traffic
A designated route on which people learning to drive cars must practice in a training vehicle while participating in road traffic

An organization that owns the car in a vehicle combination. If the organization is not also the owner of the towed trailer or semi-trailer, it may nevertheless be treated as the vehicle owner for sanctions concerning violations involving that trailer or semi-trailer.
A required remedial action to bring a vehicle’s cargo body into compliance with current regulations before the vehicle is used on the road.
An event in which cargo falls or spills onto a railway crossing or shared railway bridge and cannot immediately be cleared from the railway safety area.

**CARGO OVERLOAD VIOLATION** refers to operating a truck, tractor, trailer, semi-trailer, or similar goods-transport vehicle with a load exceeding the permitted carrying capacity recorded in its inspection certificate. The descriptions give conflicting thresholds: one specifies an excess of more than 30% and up to 50%, while the other specifies an excess of more than 150%. The precise threshold therefore cannot be determined from the provided information.

A traffic violation involving driving a truck, tractor, or similar goods-transport vehicle with a load exceeding the permitted amount recorded in its inspection certificate. The cited provision applies when the excess is over 10% up to 30%, or, for liquid-tank vehicles, over 20% up to 30%; it carries a fine of 800,000 to 1,000,000 Vietnamese dong.

id: cargo vehicle overloading above the permitted limit
ten: CARGO VEHICLE OVERLOADING ABOVE THE PERMITTED LIMIT
mo_ta: A violation in which a truck, tractor, or similar goods-transport vehicle carries cargo exceeding its permitted payload, as recorded in the vehicle’s technical safety and environmental protection inspection certificate, by more than 50% and up to 100%. The text specifies a fine of 5,000,000 to 7,000,000 Vietnamese đồng for this violation.

id: cargo vehicle overloading by more than 30% and up to 50%
ten: CARGO VEHICLE OVERLOADING BY MORE THAN 30% AND UP TO 50%
mo_ta: A road traffic violation described in Article 21: operating a cargo vehicle, including a truck or tractor with a trailer, carrying a load more than 30% and up to 50% above its permitted carrying capacity.

Violations of road traffic order and safety regulations by drivers of trucks, tractors, and similar vehicles used to transport goods. The provision states that an applicable violation is subject to a fine of 800,000 to 1,000,000 Vietnamese dong and concerns deduction of driving-license points; the specific violations are not listed in the excerpt.
CARGO-SECURING VIOLATIONS are breaches of regulations governing the securement of transported goods, as referenced in Article 12.
Operating a vehicle for commercial cargo transport without a journey-monitoring device, with a device that does not function during road use, or with falsified device data.
A violation of regulations on ensuring road traffic order and safety by a driver operating a truck, tractor, or similar vehicle used to transport goods.
Drivers of trucks, tractors, and similar vehicles used to transport goods; the text describes penalties applicable to them for specified violations.
The act of carrying people in the bed of a cargo truck, which the cited provision permits for members of the People's Armed Forces traveling to perform urgent duties.

A violation committed when a driver fails to latch or securely close the rear or side door of a cargo vehicle while it is moving. The text specifies a fine of 600,000 to 800,000 Vietnamese dong for this conduct.

A violation of road-traffic order and safety rules committed by a driver of a truck, tractor with a trailer or semi-trailer, or similar vehicle transporting goods. The particular conduct referenced in Clause 7 is not specified in the text.
Violations of road-traffic order and safety requirements by drivers of trucks, tractors, and similar vehicles used to transport goods, including vehicles towing trailers or semi-trailers.
A prohibited conduct listed in Article 12, Clause 5: carrying a bulky object while being carried on a motorcycle, motorbike, or similar vehicle.

id: carrying a bulky object while being carried
ten: CARRYING A BULKY OBJECT WHILE BEING CARRIED
mo_ta: A road-traffic violation in which a passenger being carried on a bicycle or electric bicycle carries a bulky object.

id: carrying a passenger not listed on the passenger list
ten: CARRYING A PASSENGER NOT LISTED ON THE PASSENGER LIST
mo_ta: A traffic violation in which a driver carries a passenger whose name does not appear on the required passenger list.

id: carrying a passenger on a towed vehicle
ten: CARRYING A PASSENGER ON A TOWED VEHICLE
mo_ta: A road traffic violation described in the decree: carrying a passenger on a towed vehicle, other than the person operating it.

id: carrying a passenger while using an umbrella
ten: CARRYING A PASSENGER WHILE USING AN UMBRELLA
mo_ta: A road-traffic violation in which a motorcycle or similar vehicle driver carries a passenger who is using an umbrella. Article 7 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP sets a fine of 200,000 to 400,000 Vietnamese dong for this conduct.

id: carrying a passenger who uses an umbrella
ten: CARRYING A PASSENGER WHO USES AN UMBRELLA
mo_ta: A road traffic violation committed when a bicycle or motor-driven bicycle rider carries a passenger who uses an umbrella.

id: carrying bulky objects that obstruct traffic
ten: CARRYING BULKY OBJECTS THAT OBSTRUCT TRAFFIC
mo_ta: A pedestrian traffic violation described in Article 10, Clause 2 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. The conduct is punishable by a fine of 400,000 to 600,000 Vietnamese dong.

id: carrying cargo beyond the vehicle bed’s width
ten: CARRYING CARGO BEYOND THE VEHICLE BED’S WIDTH
mo_ta: A road-traffic violation involving cargo extending beyond the width of the vehicle bed, including the width of an attached trailer or semi-trailer.

id: carrying cargo more than 10% beyond the vehicle’s front or rear
ten: CARRYING CARGO MORE THAN 10% BEYOND THE VEHICLE’S FRONT OR REAR
mo_ta: A road-traffic violation involving cargo extending beyond the front or rear of a vehicle, including an attached trailer or semi-trailer, by more than 10% of the vehicle’s designed overall length.

id: carrying cargo on top of a vehicle bed
ten: CARRYING CARGO ON TOP OF A VEHICLE BED
mo_ta: A road-traffic violation involving carrying goods on the roof or top of a truck or similar goods-transport vehicle’s bed.

id: carrying cargo over the permitted weight by more than 50% up to 100%
ten: CARRYING CARGO OVER THE PERMITTED WEIGHT BY MORE THAN 50% UP TO 100%
mo_ta: A traffic violation involving a truck, tractor, or similar cargo vehicle carrying a load more than 50% and up to 100% above the permitted payload recorded in its technical safety and environmental protection inspection certificate.

id: carrying luggage or goods above the vehicle's permitted load
ten: CARRYING LUGGAGE OR GOODS ABOVE THE VEHICLE'S PERMITTED LOAD
mo_ta: A transport violation described in Article 36, clause 2, as carrying luggage or goods in excess of the vehicle's permitted load.

id: carrying luggage or goods beyond a vehicle’s designed load capacity
ten: CARRYING LUGGAGE OR GOODS BEYOND A VEHICLE’S DESIGNED LOAD CAPACITY
mo_ta: A traffic violation involving carrying luggage or goods in a vehicle in excess of its designed load capacity. The text states that this violation is subject to a fine of 1,000,000 to 2,000,000 Vietnamese đồng.

**CARRYING MORE PASSENGERS THAN PERMITTED** is a road traffic violation in which a vehicle carries more people than its permitted capacity. The applicable penalty depends on the vehicle type and the provision governing the offence. The descriptions cite fines of **1,000,000–2,000,000 Vietnamese đồng under Article 28**, and, for passenger cars or other covered vehicles, **400,000–600,000 đồng for each excess passenger**, capped at **75,000,000 đồng**, except for violations covered by Clause 4 of that article. Article 32 is also described as setting per-person fines and maximum total fines for vehicle owners. These amounts therefore reflect different cited provisions or circumstances rather than one uniform penalty.

id: carrying more people than permitted in a vehicle cab
ten: CARRYING MORE PEOPLE THAN PERMITTED IN A VEHICLE CAB
mo_ta: A road traffic violation described in the text: a vehicle driver carries more people in the cab than regulations allow. The text states this is punishable by a fine of 600,000 to 800,000 Vietnamese đồng.

id: carrying more than the permitted capacity
ten: CARRYING MORE THAN THE PERMITTED CAPACITY
mo_ta: The prohibited practice of carrying more passengers or baggage and goods than the permitted limits allow

A traffic violation involving carrying luggage or goods that exceed the vehicle’s outer dimensions. Under Article 20, Clause 3 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, it is punishable by a fine of 600,000 to 800,000 Vietnamese dong.

id: carrying passengers above the permitted capacity
ten: CARRYING PASSENGERS ABOVE THE PERMITTED CAPACITY
mo_ta: A vehicle-occupancy violation involving carrying more people than the vehicle is permitted to carry; the decree sets fines for each person over the limit.

id: carrying passengers illegally in a vehicle bed
ten: CARRYING PASSENGERS ILLEGALLY IN A VEHICLE BED
mo_ta: A road traffic violation in which a driver carries passengers in a vehicle bed contrary to regulations. The text states that it is punishable by a fine of 4,000,000 to 6,000,000 Vietnamese dong.

id: carrying passengers not named on the passenger list
ten: CARRYING PASSENGERS NOT NAMED ON THE PASSENGER LIST
mo_ta: A violation in which a contract-based passenger transport vehicle carries a person whose name is not on the passenger list. The decree sets a fine of 1,000,000 to 2,000,000 Vietnamese đồng for this violation.

id: carrying passengers not on the contract list
ten: CARRYING PASSENGERS NOT ON THE CONTRACT LIST
mo_ta: “CARRYING PASSENGERS NOT ON THE CONTRACT LIST” is a violation in which a passenger-transport vehicle picks up or carries a person whose name does not appear on the passenger list for the signed contract.

id: carrying passengers on a vehicle roof
ten: CARRYING PASSENGERS ON A VEHICLE ROOF
mo_ta: A road traffic violation in which a driver carries passengers on the roof of a vehicle. The text states that it is punishable by a fine of 4,000,000 to 6,000,000 Vietnamese dong.

id: carrying people in cargo truck beds
ten: CARRYING PEOPLE IN CARGO TRUCK BEDS
mo_ta: The activity regulated by Article 28, Clause 1 of Law 36/2024/QH15, which permits carrying people in the bed of a cargo truck only in specified circumstances.

id: carrying people on a vehicle roof or in its luggage compartment
ten: CARRYING PEOPLE ON A VEHICLE ROOF OR IN ITS LUGGAGE COMPARTMENT
mo_ta: A traffic violation described in Article 20 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, involving carrying people on the roof of a passenger vehicle or in its luggage compartment

id: carrying people or goods on a practice driving vehicle in violation of regulations
ten: CARRYING PEOPLE OR GOODS ON A PRACTICE DRIVING VEHICLE IN VIOLATION OF REGULATIONS
mo_ta: A violation committed by a practical driving instructor who carries people or goods on a driver-training vehicle contrary to regulations. Article 39, Clause 1 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP provides for a fine of 2,000,000 to 3,000,000 Vietnamese dong.

id: carrying three or more people on a vehicle
ten: CARRYING THREE OR MORE PEOPLE ON A VEHICLE
mo_ta: A traffic violation described in Article 7 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP: carrying at least three passengers on a vehicle. The text states that this violation is punishable by a fine of 600,000 to 800,000 Vietnamese đồng.

id: carrying two people on a motorcycle
ten: CARRYING TWO PEOPLE ON A MOTORCYCLE
mo_ta: A road-traffic violation under Article 7 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, involving a motorcycle, moped, or similar vehicle carrying two people, subject to a fine of 400,000 to 600,000 Vietnamese đồng. The stated exceptions are transporting a sick person for emergency care, a child under 12, an elderly or disabled person, or escorting a person who has violated the law.

**CARRYING UNLISTED PASSENGERS** is a violation in which a driver providing passenger transport under a signed contract picks up or carries passengers whose names do not appear on the required passenger list.

id: case showing signs of a crime
ten: CASE SHOWING SIGNS OF A CRIME
mo_ta: A circumstance excluded from the ordinary transfer procedure for handling invalid or improperly issued documents.
Central-level agencies responsible for organizing implementation of Decree 184/2025/ND-CP
The median strip in the middle of a divided road, whose occupation for specified purposes is prohibited by the cited provision.
This category refers to ministries, departments, and agencies at the central level whose eligible entities may receive permits to use signal devices on priority vehicles.
The ministries, sectors, and agencies at central level whose vehicles are among those covered when their plates are registered with the Traffic Police Department.

Centrally governed cities are cities directly administered by the central government. Under the decree, the chairpersons of their People’s Committees are responsible for implementing it, and their police traffic divisions are included among the authorities covered by Article 23.
A **centrally governed city** is governed directly by the central government. Its Chief Inspector is also covered by the authority described in the text.
Police authorities of cities directly under the central government whose traffic police divisions are responsible for the permit actions described in Article 23.

id: centrally governed city traffic command center
ten: CENTRALLY GOVERNED CITY TRAFFIC COMMAND CENTER
mo_ta: A traffic command center for a centrally governed city, included within the traffic command center system.
Police agencies of centrally governed municipalities whose traffic police departments are identified as competent authorities for examining knowledge of laws on road traffic order and safety.
Cities administered directly by the central government, whose People's Committee chairpersons are responsible for implementing the decree
People seeking a certificate in road traffic law knowledge who may register with a qualified driver-training establishment.
An authority responsible for exchanging or reissuing certificates related to road-traffic legal-knowledge training.
The process of exchanging or reissuing a certificate, including its date and the responsible authority.
The process of issuing a certificate after the required test, with the issuance date and certificate number recorded.

id: certificate issuance for road-traffic legal knowledge
ten: CERTIFICATE ISSUANCE FOR ROAD-TRAFFIC LEGAL KNOWLEDGE
mo_ta: Issuance of certificates confirming road-traffic legal knowledge for operators of specialized motorcycles, as described in Article 63 of Law 36/2024/QH15.
A test whose result determines whether a certificate can be issued.

id: certification of motor vehicles or parts
ten: CERTIFICATION OF MOTOR VEHICLES OR PARTS
mo_ta: The certification activity for which false records or documents may be used or supplied.

id: certification of technical safety and environmental protection quality
ten: CERTIFICATION OF TECHNICAL SAFETY AND ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION QUALITY
mo_ta: The certification process for the technical safety quality and environmental protection of covered vehicles and vehicle parts, with procedures prescribed by the relevant ministers for items under their ministries’ management
The certification activity carried out by establishments for motor vehicles, specialized motorcycles, and motor vehicle parts.

id: chairperson of the commune-level people's committee
ten: CHAIRPERSON OF THE COMMUNE-LEVEL PEOPLE'S COMMITTEE
mo_ta: The Chairperson of the Commune-Level People’s Committee is the official who leads the committee. The descriptions identify this office-holder as having authority to impose administrative sanctions, apply the remedial measures specified in Article 3, Clause 3, points a and b, as provided under Article 42, Clause 1, and confiscate objects and vehicles involved in administrative violations.

id: chairperson of the commune-level people’s committee
ten: CHAIRPERSON OF THE COMMUNE-LEVEL PEOPLE’S COMMITTEE
mo_ta: The officeholder who, under Article 42, Clause 1, of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP, is authorized to impose fines of up to 5,000,000 Vietnamese dong.

id: chairperson of the district-level people's committee
ten: CHAIRPERSON OF THE DISTRICT-LEVEL PEOPLE'S COMMITTEE
mo_ta: The Chairperson of the District-Level People’s Committee leads the committee and has administrative enforcement powers under Clause 2 of Article 42 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. These powers include imposing fines of up to 37,500,000 Vietnamese đồng, confiscating exhibits and vehicles used in administrative violations, and issuing administrative penalty decisions for violations involving the deduction of driving-licence points.
The officeholder who has authority to impose sanctions on behalf of a People's Committee; the text specifically mentions the chairperson of a district-level committee

id: chairperson of the people's committee at district level
ten: CHAIRPERSON OF THE PEOPLE'S COMMITTEE AT DISTRICT LEVEL
mo_ta: The district-level committee's chairperson, identified by office rather than by personal name, is authorized under Article 42, Clause 2 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP to revoke the right to use licenses or professional certificates for a fixed period, or to suspend activities for a fixed period.

id: chairperson of the provincial people's committee
ten: CHAIRPERSON OF THE PROVINCIAL PEOPLE'S COMMITTEE
mo_ta: The Chairperson of the Provincial People’s Committee is the official who leads a provincial-level People’s Committee. Under the decree, the officeholder is authorized to apply the remedial measures specified in Clause 3 of Article 3 and to confiscate objects and vehicles used in administrative violations.

id: chairperson of the provincial people’s committee
ten: CHAIRPERSON OF THE PROVINCIAL PEOPLE’S COMMITTEE
mo_ta: The official who chairs a provincial-level People’s Committee; the text states that this role has authority to impose sanctions.

id: chairperson of the provincial-level people's committee
ten: CHAIRPERSON OF THE PROVINCIAL-LEVEL PEOPLE'S COMMITTEE
mo_ta: The **Chairperson of the Provincial-Level People’s Committee** is the official who presides over a provincial-level People’s Committee. The officeholder is not identified by name in the provided descriptions. Under Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, the Chairperson has specified administrative-enforcement powers, including applying the remedial measures provided for in Clause 3, Article 3; exercising penalty authority under Article 42(3); and confiscating exhibits and vehicles involved in administrative violations under Article 42(2). The Chairperson may also issue an administrative penalty decision for a violation involving the deduction of driving-licence points.

id: chairperson of the provincial-level people’s committee
ten: CHAIRPERSON OF THE PROVINCIAL-LEVEL PEOPLE’S COMMITTEE
mo_ta: The office-holder authorized to revoke the right to use permits or professional certificates for a fixed period, or to suspend activities for a fixed period
The office-holders who lead People's Committees at different administrative levels and are addressed in Article 42 as having sanctioning authority.

id: chairpersons of people's committees at all levels
ten: CHAIRPERSONS OF PEOPLE'S COMMITTEES AT ALL LEVELS
mo_ta: Chairpersons of People’s Committees at all levels are the officials who lead People’s Committees across Vietnam’s administrative hierarchy. Article 42 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP sets out their authority to impose administrative sanctions for violations within the decree and within the management scope of their localities. It addresses the powers of chairpersons at different levels, including specific provisions for district-level chairpersons and for provincial-level chairpersons. The article also specifies that commune-level chairpersons may apply certain remedial measures.

id: chairpersons of people’s committees at all administrative levels
ten: CHAIRPERSONS OF PEOPLE’S COMMITTEES AT ALL ADMINISTRATIVE LEVELS
mo_ta: The officeholders whose administrative-sanctioning powers are addressed in Article 42 of the decree, including the commune-level chairperson.

id: chairpersons of people’s committees at all levels
ten: CHAIRPERSONS OF PEOPLE’S COMMITTEES AT ALL LEVELS
mo_ta: Chairpersons of People’s Committees at all levels are the officials who lead People’s Committees at their respective administrative levels. Article 42 addresses their authority to impose sanctions, with Clause 2 specifying the sanctioning authority of provincial-level chairpersons.

id: chairpersons of provincial and centrally governed municipal people's committees
ten: CHAIRPERSONS OF PROVINCIAL AND CENTRALLY GOVERNED MUNICIPAL PEOPLE'S COMMITTEES
mo_ta: Officials who chair provincial or centrally governed municipal People's Committees and are responsible for implementing the decree.

id: chairpersons of provincial and centrally run city people's committees
ten: CHAIRPERSONS OF PROVINCIAL AND CENTRALLY RUN CITY PEOPLE'S COMMITTEES
mo_ta: The chairpersons of provincial and centrally run city People's Committees, identified as responsible for implementing Decree 151/2024/ND-CP

A change to the content or information in a document that was previously approved, which is addressed by the described application procedure.

id: chasing each other on the road

The act of observing the front, rear, and side where a vehicle door will open before opening it, to determine whether it is safe.

id: chief inspector of a province or centrally governed city
ten: CHIEF INSPECTOR OF A PROVINCE OR CENTRALLY GOVERNED CITY

id: chief inspector of a province or centrally-run city

id: chief inspector of the department of transport

id: chief inspector of the ministry of transport
ten: CHIEF INSPECTOR OF THE MINISTRY OF TRANSPORT
mo_ta: The Chief Inspector of the Ministry of Transport is the official who heads the Ministry’s inspectorate. Under Article 44, Clause 4, the Chief Inspector is authorized to impose penalties and apply the remedial measures specified in Article 3, Clause 3.

The district police official responsible for entering driving-licence point-deduction data into the relevant database when the district-level People's Committee chairperson issues the administrative penalty decision.
The Chief of District-Level Police is the official who heads a district-level police unit. Article 43(4) lists the chief as having authority to impose administrative sanctions.
A violation involving requirements for equipment that records images of preschool children or students on a vehicle, described in Article 27, point b, clause 3.
A child under 10 years old and under 1.35 meters tall who is carried in the same row of seats as the driver.

People responsible for managing children during transportation, whom educational institutions must instruct in the required safety procedures
A violation involving equipment on a vehicle that warns of or prevents children being left behind, described in Article 26, point b, clause 6.

The violation described in the decree: carrying a child under 10 years old and under 1.35 meters tall in the same row as the driver, except in a car with only one row of seats, or failing to use an appropriate child safety device.
The required corrective action of providing compliant seats in vehicles for preschool children and primary school students.

Children are among the groups whose participation in road traffic is addressed by Article 30 of Law 36/2024/QH15, including under clause 2. The law provides for their road use to be accommodated and regulated. Children enrolled in preschool educational institutions are intended recipients of education on road traffic law and safety, including how to wear a helmet correctly, to strengthen their self-protection and awareness of complying with traffic rules. Children are also the people the described safety device is designed to protect while they are sitting or lying in a car.

id: children under 10 years old and under 1.35 meters
ten: CHILDREN UNDER 10 YEARS OLD AND UNDER 1.35 METERS
mo_ta: Children who are under 10 years old and shorter than 1.35 meters; the law specifies seating and safety-device rules when they are transported in a car.
Children younger than seven years old, identified as people who should be helped when crossing a road.
Children younger than seven years old; the text states they must be accompanied by an adult when crossing a road.

id: chánh thanh tra tỉnh, thành phố trực thuộc trung ương
ten: CHÁNH THANH TRA TỈNH, THÀNH PHỐ TRỰC THUỘC TRUNG ƯƠNG
mo_ta: The chief inspector of a province or centrally governed city, who may impose fines of up to 52,500,000 đồng under the stated conditions.

CHÍNH PHỦ (the Government of Vietnam) sets the conditions that automotive driver-training establishments must meet and establishes the regulations under which vehicle inspection establishments are organized and operate. It also issues detailed rules for implementing Article 51 on ensuring road traffic order and safety when road vehicles transport dangerous goods. CHÍNH PHỦ is identified as the issuing authority of Decree No. 10/2020/NĐ-CP, Decree No. 47/2022/NĐ-CP, and Decree No. 41/2024/NĐ-CP.
An owner of a motor vehicle, referred to in the article heading as a party with responsibilities under Article 43.
An owner of a special-use motorcycle, identified in Article 43’s heading as a party whose responsibilities are addressed.

A Vietnamese legal instrument issued by the Minister of Transport on May 12, 2023, amending and supplementing provisions of circulars concerning the management, exploitation, use, maintenance, and protection of roads.

CIRCULAR 105/2026/TT-BCA is a Vietnamese Ministry of Public Security circular that amends and supplements rules for legal-knowledge tests on road traffic order and safety, including tests taken to restore points on a driver’s license. Its provisions address test content and methods, timing, questions, duration, passing results, and the restoration of license points.

Article 5 provides an appendix of forms for use in these tests. Article 6 sets out the circular’s entry into force and transitional provisions: tests held after it takes effect must follow its requirements, while Clause 3 continues specified testing rules from earlier circulars until June 30, 2027. Article 7 assigns the Director of the Traffic Police Department responsibility for directing, inspecting, and urging implementation.

Circular 13/2025/TT-BCA is a Vietnamese Ministry of Public Security circular that amends and supplements point a, clause 1, Article 6 of Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA. Its Article 6 contains testing provisions referenced by Circular 105/2026/TT-BCA, whose transitional rules keep those provisions in effect through June 30, 2027. Article 14 sets out implementation provisions, assigns the Director of the Traffic Police Department responsibility for overseeing implementation, and identifies the parties responsible for carrying it out.
A Vietnamese legal instrument issued by the Minister of Transport on August 29, 2019, concerning speed limits and safe distances for motor vehicles and specialized motorcycles in road traffic.

CIRCULAR 38/2024/TT-BGTVT is a Vietnamese Ministry of Transport regulation on vehicle operating speeds and safe distances on roads. Article 3 defines terms including “operating speed” (a vehicle’s speed while participating in road traffic), “one-way road,” “payload” (the permitted cargo mass recorded in specified technical-safety and environmental-protection certificates), “road in a densely populated area,” and the safe distance between vehicles.

Article 4 sets out the principles drivers must follow for operating speeds and safe distances. Where relevant signs are absent, drivers are directed to apply Articles 6, 7, 8 and 11. Article 5 addresses road design speeds, including the basis for determining rural-road design speeds and the design speeds used to calculate expressway technical criteria.

Article 6 establishes maximum permitted speeds for motor vehicles on roads other than expressways, with limits differentiated by road configuration and provisions addressing roads outside populated areas. Article 8 sets maximum speeds for four-wheel motorized passenger and cargo vehicles on non-expressway roads; passenger vehicles are limited to 30 km/h when operated within the permitted area and time. Article 9 sets maximum and minimum speeds for motor vehicles and specialized motorcycles on expressways: the maximum is 120 km/h, and the minimum is generally 60 km/h. Where an expressway’s design speed is 60 km/h, the minimum is determined by the approved traffic organization plan. The article also requires speed-limit signs.

Article 10 governs how permitted operating speeds are determined and how speed signs are installed, including requirements for sign placement. Article 11 sets safe-distance rules. On clear, dry, level roads, required distances depend on vehicle speed; below 60 km/h, drivers must maintain a distance appropriate to traffic conditions.

Under Article 12, the circular takes effect on January 1, 2025. It replaces Circular 31/2019/TT-BGTVT and Article 15 of Circular 06/2023/TT-BGTVT.

**CIRCULAR 65/2024/TT-BCA** is a circular issued by Vietnam’s Ministry of Public Security establishing requirements and procedures for testing drivers’ legal knowledge of road traffic order and safety, particularly for drivers whose driving-license points have been fully deducted and who must pass a test to restore points.

Article 5 sets requirements for the conditions, facilities, and equipment needed to organize the tests. Article 6 specifies the test requirements, including the content and method of assessment, duration, question structure, results, and passing requirements. Clause 3 addresses the theoretical test’s timing, questions, and pass criteria; point (a) of clause 1 was amended and supplemented by Circular 13/2025/TT-BCA. Provisions of Article 6 are also referenced by Circular 105/2026/TT-BCA, whose transitional rule keeps the specified testing provisions in effect through June 30, 2027.

Article 7 governs registration for and organization of the road-traffic-law knowledge examination, including retesting. Article 8 sets out the responsibilities of competent authorities conducting examinations, including publicly posting study materials on the electronic information portal under their management.

Article 11 addresses implementation responsibilities. It assigns the Traffic Police Department’s director responsibility for researching, developing, administering, maintaining, and upgrading software used for the tests, and for reporting that work to Ministry leadership. It also assigns responsibilities to directors of provincial and centrally governed municipal police. The circular provides for reporting difficulties and requesting guidance during implementation.

A circular whose Article 6 addresses effectiveness and transitional provisions. It establishes that specified provisions of Circular No. 65/2024/TT-BCA cease to be effective when this circular takes effect.

A circular dated 28 February 2025 that amends and supplements provisions in circulars concerning road, railway, and inland-waterway traffic order and safety. Its Article 6 amended and supplemented a simulated legal-knowledge testing provision.
A circular whose Article 6 provisions identified in Circular No. 105/2026/TT-BCA cease to be effective when the latter circular takes effect.
A mobile application for citizens, managed and operated by Vietnam’s Ministry of Public Security, through which relevant changes are to be reported.
A city-level traffic command center, listed as a component of the traffic command center system in Article 75.

Civil servants are government employees or public officials who perform official duties or tasks and are authorized under the relevant decree or provision to prepare and make records of administrative violations.
The urgent mobilization of civilians, civilian vehicles, and equipment, including the people using or operating them, authorized by Article 68 for specified public-protection purposes.
People who may be mobilized by traffic police in urgent circumstances under the law.

Road segments classified as Class IV, identified in the text as among the roads outside populated areas that may have adverse conditions and traffic-safety risks.
Road segments classified as Class V, identified in the text as among the roads outside populated areas that may have adverse conditions and traffic-safety risks.
Road segments classified as Class VI, identified in the text as among the roads outside populated areas that may have adverse conditions and traffic-safety risks.

“CLAUSE 1” refers to several different provisions, depending on the article. Clause 1 of Article 52 defines oversized vehicles as motor vehicles or specialized motor vehicles whose overall dimensions exceed the limits permitted by national technical regulations for motor vehicles. Clause 1 of Article 43 authorizes on-duty People’s Public Security officers to impose fines of up to 7,500,000 Vietnamese dong. Clause 1 of Article 45 requires automobile passenger transport to follow its registered schedule and route, except in cases of force majeure. Clause 1 of Article 57 describes driving-licence categories and the vehicles permitted under Category C.
The clause specifying a fine of 400,000 to 600,000 VND for listed vehicle-condition violations.
The provision referenced in Clause 6 as defining conduct that results in a two-point deduction from the driver’s license.

The first clause of Article 29 sets the rule that a motor vehicle may tow only one other motor vehicle or specialized motorcycle when the towed vehicle cannot move under its own power, subject to the stated exception and safety requirements
The first clause of Article 33, cited in the excerpt among the provisions specifying violations subject to the penalty authority described.
The first clause of Article 34, cited as one of the provisions whose violations require excess or oversized cargo to be removed.
Clause 1 of Article 35 sets the conditions that intelligent transport vehicles must satisfy.

Clause 1 of Article 38 is described as addressing vehicle and license-plate matters. It specifies an act whose repetition may result in confiscation of the vehicle operated by the person responsible, though the act itself is not identified in the descriptions. It is also described as allowing the winner of a vehicle license-plate auction to transfer, exchange, give away, or bequeath the vehicle associated with the auction-winning plate. These descriptions appear to concern different aspects of the clause, and the available information does not clarify how they relate.

A provision referenced by Article 40, Clause 3, under which motor vehicle inspectors may be penalized. The number of inspectors penalized under this clause within the specified period can trigger a fine for a testing or certification facility.

The first clause of Article 50 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, which specifies how driving-licence points are deducted when a person is sanctioned for multiple qualifying administrative violations in the same instance.
The first clause of Article 51 identifies the authority responsible for restoring driving-license points.

id: clause 1 of article 54 of the law on road traffic order and safety
ten: CLAUSE 1 OF ARTICLE 54 OF THE LAW ON ROAD TRAFFIC ORDER AND SAFETY
mo_ta: Provision defining which vehicles are eligible for road rescue, as referenced by the penalty rule

Clause 1 of Article 56 sets driver-eligibility requirements for cars, motorized four-wheeled passenger vehicles, motorized four-wheeled goods vehicles, and similar vehicles. Drivers must meet the applicable legal age and health requirements and hold a valid driving licence appropriate to the vehicle. The clause provides an exception for certain moped drivers.
The first clause of Article 7, which sets a fine of 200,000 to 400,000 Vietnamese dong for specified road traffic violations.
The clause of Article 8 that establishes a fine of 400,000–600,000 VND for specified conduct by a driver of a specialized motorcycle.

CLAUSE 10 provides that drivers who commit the specified violations face supplementary penalties in addition to a monetary fine, including the loss of six points from their driving licences. The descriptions cite different articles—Article 13 and Article 20—for this provision, so its article reference is unclear.
A provision stating that, in addition to the applicable penalty, a driver who commits the specified violation has points deducted from their driver’s license.
The clause that prescribes a fine of 18,000,000 to 22,000,000 Vietnamese dong for specified container-securing violations during transport.
A provision referenced by Article 7 whose specified traffic violations result in a 10-point deduction from the driver’s license.
A clause of Article 13 that provides for corrective measures in addition to penalties for the violations it references.
A provision stating that drivers who commit the specified violations are subject to corrective measures in addition to penalties.
A referenced category of violation that triggers the corrective measures described in Clause 13.
A provision setting a fine of 30,000,000 to 40,000,000 Vietnamese dong for specified serious violations, including driving with alcohol levels above the stated limits.
A provision specifying vehicle confiscation for drivers who commit any of the listed dangerous operating acts.

CLAUSE 12 of Article 32 provides for fines against individuals and organizations that own specified vehicles and violate regulations on operating smart traffic vehicles on roads, including by unlawfully installing or using devices that alter license plates.
A provision of Article 6 cited as covering an administrative violation for which a vehicle may be temporarily seized.

CLAUSE 13 is described in two regulatory contexts: as a clause of Article 26 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP specifying remedial measures for certain road-transport violations, and as Clause 13 of Article 13, which provides for a driver’s-license point deduction when drivers commit specified vehicle-condition violations. The descriptions do not establish whether these references concern the same provision.

Clause 13 of Article 21 provides that drivers who commit an act specified in Clause 9 lose six points from their driving licence. It concerns penalties for violations of road-traffic order and safety rules by drivers of cargo-carrying vehicles.

mo_ta: A provision of Decree No. 10/2020/NĐ-CP that is repealed under Article 38(2) of Decree No. 151/2024/NĐ-CP.
Clause 13 of Article 26 requires individuals and organizations that commit the specified violations to undertake corrective measures in addition to any applicable penalties.

A clause of Article 26 specifying that certain violations by a transport-business individual who directly operates a vehicle result in a two-point driver’s license deduction, in addition to other penalties.
The provision specifying information that is collected from the database on driving tests and driver's license issuance.
A provision setting a fine of 35,000,000 to 37,000,000 dong for individuals who commit the specified violations.

A provision stating that, in addition to other penalties, a person who directly drives a vehicle while conducting transport business and commits the specified violation has six points deducted from their driving licence.

The clause imposing fines of 28–30 million VND on individual vehicle owners and 56–60 million VND on organizational vehicle owners for allowing ineligible drivers to operate specified vehicles in traffic.
A provision of Article 6 cited as covering an administrative violation for which a vehicle may be temporarily seized.
A referenced provision whose specified act triggers an eight-point driver's-license deduction when committed by a vehicle owner directly driving the vehicle.
The cited clause of Article 6 states that, in addition to a fine, drivers who commit specified violations are subject to supplementary penalties.
A provision of Decree 151/2024/ND-CP identifying information that is collected from the database concerning transport business units and vehicle badges.
A provision stating that drivers committing violations specified in Article 6, points a of clause 9, clause 10, and point đ of clause 11 lose 10 points from their driving licenses
Clause 17 of Article 32 requires the confiscation of specified vehicles when their owners commit the listed violations, including the repeat violation described in Point b of Clause 16.
A provision specifying supplementary penalties for certain violations, including suspension of the right to use a vehicle’s operating insignia for one to three months when applicable.

Clause 19 of Article 32 sets out additional corrective measures for individuals and organizations committing specified violations when a vehicle’s body or permitted cargo weight does not comply with current regulations.

A provision requiring individuals and organizations who commit the specified violations to take corrective measures, including installing prescribed rescue equipment and driver or journey-monitoring devices.

“CLAUSE 2” refers to several different legal provisions, rather than one single rule. Depending on the instrument, it may be:

- A subsection of Article 30 setting out requirements for specified groups using roads, including that children under seven be accompanied by an adult when crossing a road.
- Clause 2 of Article 40, providing that a modified vehicle is subject to the service-life rules applicable to it after modification.
- A subsection of Article 17 specifying where priority signal devices must be placed on motorcycles.
- Clause 2 of Article 45, requiring drivers and service personnel on passenger-transport automobiles to ensure luggage and goods are safely arranged and secured.
- Clause 2 of Article 9 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP, setting a fine of VND 150,000–250,000 for the specified traffic violation.

These provisions concern separate traffic-safety and enforcement matters; the relevant article or decree is needed to identify which “CLAUSE 2” applies.
The provision imposes a fine of 400,000 to 600,000 Vietnamese dong on vehicle operators who commit one of the listed violations.
The clause containing rules that people aboard passenger-transport vehicles are required to follow
The clause that specifies a fine of 400,000 to 600,000 Vietnamese đồng for listed traffic violations involving livestock
Clause 2 of Article 13 sets a fine of 400,000 to 600,000 Vietnamese đồng for specified vehicle-condition violations

The subsection of Article 18 that sets out the fine for specified violations of motor-vehicle driver requirements, including driving a motorcycle or similar vehicle without valid compulsory civil liability insurance.
A provision referenced by Article 20 as defining conduct that may result in a four-point deduction from a driver’s license.
A provision referenced in Article 22 whose specified violation results in a four-point driver's-license deduction.
The second clause of Article 33, cited in the excerpt among the provisions specifying violations subject to the penalty authority described.
The second clause of Article 34, cited as one of the provisions whose violations require excess or oversized cargo to be removed.

Clause 2 of Article 38 addresses both repeat violations that may result in confiscation of an operator’s vehicle and restrictions on vehicle license plates won at auction. It provides that winners may not transfer, exchange, give away, or bequeath their winning plates, except as provided in Point c of Clause 1.
The clause specifying a fine of 3,000,000 to 5,000,000 Vietnamese dong for driver-training facilities committing the listed violations.
The clause assigning traffic police authority, within their assigned functions and duties, to penalize violations specified in Articles 6 through 36.
The subsection of Article 41 that specifies traffic police’s authority to penalize violations listed in designated provisions of Article 39.
The clause assigning drivers and onboard service personnel duties to guide, require, and check compliance with the rules cited in Clause 2 of Article 10
The clause referenced as defining the cases in which driving-license points are automatically restored.
The provision cited for driver eligibility requirements applicable to specialized motorcycles.
Clause 21 of Article 32 provides that, in addition to other penalties, a vehicle owner who directly drives the vehicle may have points deducted from their driver’s license for specified violations.
The clause stating that individuals or organizations committing the specified violations may also have driving-license points deducted.

“CLAUSE 3” is a context-dependent reference to the third clause of different articles in road-traffic regulations, rather than one single provision. Depending on the article cited, it may:

- List remedial measures for administrative violations affecting road-traffic order and safety, such as installing compliant equipment, restoring technical functions, or removing unauthorized equipment.
- Require road-vehicle operators to observe and slow down or stop when hazard warnings, obstacles, or specified locations make this necessary for safety.
- Identify violations under Article 13, including those in points a and d, that trigger corrective measures under Clause 11.
- Set the conditions under which overtaking is permitted under Article 14.
- Prescribe a fine of 300,000 to 400,000 VND for specified traffic violations.
- Specify an act under Article 29 that results in a deduction from the operator’s driving licence.
- Set a fine of 5,000,000 to 10,000,000 VND under Article 39 for specified violations, including a driving test center’s failure to retain required records or maintain required conditions.
- State when oversized, overweight, or tracked vehicles may be permitted to travel on public roads under Article 52.
- Establish requirements under Article 55 for specified foreign vehicles to operate in Vietnam.
A provision of Decree 151/2024/ND-CP that specifies the database referred to in Article 13.

The clause specifying a fine of 600,000 to 800,000 Vietnamese đồng for listed violations, including failing to display the vehicle's route or displaying a route that does not match the authorized route.
The clause prescribing a fine of 1,000,000 to 2,000,000 Vietnamese đồng for specified violations involving driver-image recording devices.

Clause 3 of Article 22 imposes a fine of 13,000,000 to 15,000,000 Vietnamese dong for specified violations involving permits to transport oversized or overweight goods. A violation covered by this clause also results in a four-point deduction from the driver’s license.

id: clause 3 of article 26 of decree no. 10/2020/nđ-cp
ten: CLAUSE 3 OF ARTICLE 26 OF DECREE NO. 10/2020/NĐ-CP
mo_ta: A provision of Decree No. 10/2020/NĐ-CP that is repealed under Article 38(2) of Decree No. 151/2024/NĐ-CP.
A provision of Article 28 referenced as defining conduct that results in a six-point driving-license deduction under Clause 4.

Clause 3 of Article 3 specifies remedial measures for administrative violations involving road traffic order and safety. These measures include requirements to install designated monitoring, safety, and rescue equipment in vehicles.

Clause 3 of Article 32 sets fines for individual and organizational owners of motorcycles, mopeds, and similar vehicles who install or use sound or lighting equipment that disrupts road-traffic order and safety. Points a and b of the clause are referenced as provisions covering these sanctionable violations.
The clause specifying a fine of 8,000,000 to 10,000,000 Vietnamese dong for listed road-traffic violations.

Clause 3 of Article 39 prescribes fines of 5,000,000 to 10,000,000 đồng (VND) for specified violations of driver-training and driving-test regulations. These include enrolling students in driver training when they do not meet the required qualifications or lack the necessary documents.
