A commune is a local administrative area. In the Vietnamese administrative context, it corresponds to the “cấp xã” level, which is the level of the People’s Committee referenced in the text. It is also the jurisdictional level associated with a commune-level police chief.
Commune roads within the relevant People’s Committee’s area of management, for which the competent authority decides where to place speed-limit signs.
The commune in which the road traffic accident takes place; its commune-level People's Committee has burial responsibilities under the stated conditions.
The local administrative level referred to in the text when describing the commune-level police chief.
The commune-level tier of Vietnam’s administrative divisions, referenced as the level at which the relevant People’s Committee and chairperson operate.

The **COMMUNE-LEVEL PEOPLE’S COMMITTEE** is a local government body at the commune administrative level. Under Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, its chairperson is authorized to impose certain administrative sanctions, including fines of up to 5,000,000 Vietnamese dong under Clause 1 of Article 42, and to apply the remedial measures specified in Article 3, Clause 3.

The committee also has a role when a fatal road traffic accident occurs in its commune. With consent from the competent state agency, it is responsible for arranging the deceased person’s burial if the person’s identity is unknown, there are no relatives, or the relatives are unable to arrange the burial.

The COMMUNE-LEVEL PEOPLE’S COMMITTEE is a local government body in Vietnam. Under amended Article 42, Clause 1 of the decree, its chairperson is authorized to impose administrative sanctions, including issuing warnings and fines of up to 37,500,000 Vietnamese đồng, suspending permits or activities for a limited period, confiscating violating items or vehicles, and applying specified remedial measures.

The **COMMUNE-LEVEL PEOPLE’S COMMITTEE CHAIRPERSON** is the officeholder who chairs a commune-level People’s Committee. Under Article 42, Clause 1, the chairperson is authorized to impose administrative fines of up to 37,500,000 Vietnamese dong, confiscate evidence and vehicles used in administrative violations when their value does not exceed 10,000,000 Vietnamese dong, and temporarily revoke the right to use licenses or professional certificates or temporarily suspend activities.

**COMMUNE-LEVEL POLICE** are local police authorities whose chiefs have administrative-enforcement powers under Decree 168/2024/ND-CP. Within their assigned functions and duties, commune-level police chiefs may impose specified penalties for road-traffic violations, including fines of up to 37,500,000 đồng, and may apply specified remedial measures. The decree also authorizes them to confiscate exhibits and vehicles involved in administrative violations, as provided in Article 43, Clause 4. The relevant penalty powers are set out in Articles 41 and 43, including Article 43, Clauses 3 and 4.

Commune-level police offices also receive examination applications from people applying through the authority responsible for their place of residence. For valid applications, they provide appointment information in line with published schedules and forward the applications to the Traffic Police Division no later than one working day after receipt.
A commune-level police unit whose chief may impose administrative penalties for specified road traffic violations within the functions and duties assigned to the unit.

The **COMMUNE-LEVEL POLICE CHIEF** is the official who heads a commune-level police force or unit. Within the functions, duties, and scope assigned to the office, the chief may impose administrative sanctions for specified violations involving road-traffic order and safety, including those covered by Article 41 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. The listed sanctions include warnings and fines, and the chief may also apply authorized remedial measures.

The descriptions give different fine limits: one cites a maximum of **37,500,000 đồng**, while Article 43, Clause 3 is cited as setting a maximum of **2,500,000 đồng**. These figures should be understood as applying under different stated legal authorities or contexts; the limit applicable to a particular violation depends on the governing provision.

The chief’s stated enforcement powers also include seizing objects or vehicles used in administrative violations when their value does not exceed **5,000,000 đồng** under Article 43, Clause 3, and confiscating exhibits or vehicles where authorized under Clause 4. The office may further be empowered to revoke temporarily the right to use specified permits or professional certificates, suspend certain activities, and apply the remedial measures specified in Article 3, Clause 3.

The COMPANY-LEVEL MOBILE POLICE UNIT is an unnamed company-level unit of the Mobile Police. Under Article 43, clause 2 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, its head has specified authority to impose administrative penalties, including fines of up to 15,000,000 Vietnamese đồng, and to confiscate exhibits and vehicles involved in administrative violations valued at no more than 30,000,000 đồng.

The commander of a company-level Mobile Police unit, authorized to issue warnings, impose fines up to 15,000,000 đồng, confiscate items or vehicles within the specified value limit, and apply certain remedial measures.
The head of a company-level Mobile Police unit, identified in Article 43 as having sanctioning authority.
Compensation required under law when a person who causes a road traffic accident causes damage.

The compensation process for damage suffered while mobilized civilians, vehicles, or equipment are carrying out their assigned duties. The responsible unit must resolve compensation in accordance with the law.
The official authorized to impose administrative penalties and whose office or organizational unit may receive vehicle owners and relevant parties to resolve a violation case.
The competent agencies and organizations authorized to use and share the road traffic order and safety database.

**Competent authorities** are the public bodies and authorized forces empowered under applicable laws to perform specific road-traffic, vehicle-document, permitting, and enforcement functions. Their responsibilities include issuing orders and plans for patrol and traffic-control activities; issuing vehicle registration certificates and vehicle technical-safety and environmental-protection inspection certificates or labels; and requesting, issuing, or verifying vehicle documents, including through the authority in the country where a foreign motor vehicle is registered. References to documents not issued by an authorized body may concern their use or, where provided, their revocation.

Competent authorities also issue permits for priority-vehicle signal devices and may authorize temporary use of roadways or sidewalks for purposes other than traffic. They may receive applications under administrative-procedure rules, approve international border gates for the temporary import and re-export of foreign vehicles, and test knowledge of road-traffic order and safety laws, making relevant study materials publicly available.

In traffic management, the authorities empowered to address congestion may be asked by traffic police to resolve or prevent it. They may receive police reports and recommendations, and resolve congestion matters referred to them.

For enforcement, competent authorities and functional forces use professional or smart technical equipment to detect violations, direct and control traffic, resolve situations, and handle road-law violations. They are responsible for administrative penalties and related procedures, including cases where a vehicle cannot be stopped immediately after a violation is detected. They may notify vehicle owners and relevant parties, direct them to the office or unit of the official responsible for handling the violation, and seek to identify the driver.

When excess-weight or oversized cargo is found, the relevant authorities or enforcement forces direct how it must be unloaded or removed at the location of the violation. Their instructions may also govern the clearing of rubbish, waste, materials, or goods associated with the violation.

The competent authorities of Vietnam are empowered to authorize foreign agencies and organizations to operate within Vietnam. They also grant permission for the vehicles described in the relevant text to participate in road traffic, specifying the permitted scope, routes, and times.

**COMPETENT AUTHORITY** is a generic term for the public body or government agency legally designated to perform a particular function. It does not identify one single agency: the responsible authority varies according to the applicable law, procedure, and subject matter.

Its functions include issuing, approving, or administering vehicle registration certificates and documents; technical-safety and environmental-protection inspection certificates or stickers; driving licences; vehicle and passenger-vehicle badges; temporary licence plates; circulation and operating permits; and certificates for vehicle or component quality. It may also issue permits for intelligent-transport vehicles, oversized or overweight goods, foreign vehicles circulating in Vietnam, convoys, and the use of signal-emitting devices on priority vehicles. In specified cases, it may authorize passengers to ride in a cargo-truck bed during a procession, prohibit certain vehicle types from entering an area or road, or decide where or when speed-limit or operating-speed signs are placed.

Depending on its designation, the COMPETENT AUTHORITY may receive permit applications and dossiers in person, consult applicants in emergencies, review or reissue permits, approve documents or plans, and explain or return files under transitional procedures. The authority that issued an intelligent-transport-vehicle permit may review replacement or reissuance applications within two working days and provide written reasons if requirements are not met. Authorities may also retain, revoke, recover, or process licences and professional certificates where authorized by law; documents held by an entity lacking recovery authority are transferred to the issuing or another competent authority.

The term also covers bodies responsible for vehicle inspections and for announcing inspection schedules; organizing examinations of road-traffic-order-and-safety knowledge; assigning personnel to receive applications and conduct checks; verifying participants’ identities and application information; and publishing test dates and procedures. Authorities designated under Article 23 of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP receive applications for specified permits, including direct submissions.

Other responsibilities may include approving plans for temporary roadway or sidewalk use and promptly notifying traffic police; authorizing relevant traffic arrangements; requesting information from people at an accident scene; receiving accident and operator information; and receiving police reports when additional forces or vehicles are needed. An authority must also be notified when an issue exceeds an agency’s capacity, jurisdiction, functions, or duties.

The COMPETENT AUTHORITY may be empowered to determine whether a vehicle’s chassis or engine number was unlawfully altered, whether a modification changes the vehicle’s type, or whether a vehicle meets requirements for circulation. The term also refers to bodies that approved relevant programs before a decree took effect, and to the agency responsible for ensuring conditions required for legally prescribed checks and examinations. The specific authority is determined by the governing provision; it is not named where the legislation leaves it unspecified.
A competent Vietnamese authority authorized to issue driving licenses.
An authorized official who prepares administrative violation records and carries out vehicle detention in accordance with the stated rules.

The authority referred to in Clause 3 of Circular 38/2024/TT-BGTVT; the excerpt does not identify it by name. It is responsible for deciding whether to place maximum operating speed signs for vehicle types considered to pose a high traffic-safety risk.

The **COMPETENT EXAMINATION AUTHORITY** is the authorized body responsible for administering or overseeing the examination on laws concerning road traffic order and safety. Applicants select the authority when registering and may submit their registration documents or dossiers to it, including through an online application. For in-person submissions, the authority assigns a staff member to review the dossier and issue an appointment specifying the examination time and location.

The authority publicly announces examination schedules, including the expected time and location of examinations for the following month, and must notify registered examinees if the examination time or location changes. A person who fails may request a retest from the authority that administered the earlier examination or choose another competent authority.

The authority retains a copy of the examination record. It must preserve examination-room surveillance-camera images for at least two years and examination registration records and minutes, in both paper and electronic form, for at least five years.
The competent authority responsible for conducting the legal-knowledge test. It must ensure that the facilities and equipment used for testing are available for its use.

The **COMPETENT ISSUING AUTHORITY** is the authority that previously issued a permit for signaling devices on a priority vehicle or an intelligent transport vehicle operating license. It is responsible for receiving the relevant permit or license when it is subject to revocation and for carrying out the revocation.
A competent authority responsible for checking people’s knowledge of laws on road traffic order and safety.
Authorities that previously issued the relevant approval and are empowered to suspend the activity and refuse further approvals after a violation.

The **COMPETENT LICENSING AUTHORITY** is the government body designated under the applicable regulation or decree to receive applications and issue written approvals, refusals, or permits. Depending on the procedure, it may authorize relevant travel or vehicle arrangements, approve changes to previously submitted information, permit the operation of smart or intelligent transport vehicles, and issue permits for signal-emitting devices on priority vehicles. The applicable rules may not name the authority specifically; applications are sent to the body authorized to handle the relevant licensing matter.

For signal-device permits, the COMPETENT LICENSING AUTHORITY may access supporting documents through a connected shared database and, when it handles an application directly, update permit information in the management database. Where an approval or permit has already been issued, the issuing authority receives required notices of changes to covered arrangements and any prescribed follow-up documents. It may also need to be notified of an incident that delays departure, receive a written report once the incident is resolved, and receive a report on the results of an organized activity.

The COMPETENT LICENSING AUTHORITY may consider proposed changes, refuse approval, or suspend covered activities when violations occur. For intelligent transport vehicles, the authority that issued the operating permit receives it and carries out its revocation when required. The rules also refer separately to competent government bodies responsible for issuing driver’s licenses and vehicle license plates: use of a driver’s license or plates not issued by an authorized body is identified as a violation.

A **COMPETENT MEDICAL FACILITY** is a medical facility authorized to issue a valid health certificate, in paper or electronic form, for a driver or a person registering for an examination. No specific facility is named.
An unnamed government authority empowered to issue international driving permits under the stated rules.
A person authorized to impose penalties and issue a notice concerning resolution of a violation.

The **COMPETENT PERMIT-ISSUING AUTHORITY** is responsible for issuing documents and processing applications for permission to use signal devices on priority vehicles. It is also the authority that issued the smart traffic vehicle operating permit and receives requests to amend or reissue that permit.

A **COMPETENT PERSON** is a person authorized under the applicable rules to handle a violation. They may prepare an administrative violation record against the vehicle owner and proceed with sanctions in accordance with the law, including issuing an administrative sanctioning decision.
The police authority with jurisdiction to handle a reported road traffic accident.

The **COMPETENT ROAD MANAGEMENT AUTHORITY** is the authorized body responsible for issuing circulation permits for vehicles transporting oversized or overweight cargo, including oversized vehicles, overweight vehicles, and tracked vehicles operating on roads. As specified in Clause 3 of Article 10, it also leads and coordinates with the relevant traffic police and district-level People’s Committee to determine the permitted operating speed and arrange for the installation of speed signs.
A person legally authorized to impose administrative penalties, including deprivation of the right to use a driving licence.
A person authorized to impose administrative penalties, issue notices concerning violations, and notify relevant agencies after a violation case is resolved.

The **COMPETENT STATE AGENCY** is a state agency authorized to require the resolution of administrative violation cases involving road traffic order and safety. It also has authority to investigate and resolve road traffic accidents and to consent to the burial of a deceased person.

Competent State Authorities are government bodies with legal authority over the relevant matter. Their responsibilities may include conducting driving tests and handling legal violations or traffic accidents involving foreign visitors or foreign motor vehicles. They may require outstanding violations or incidents to be resolved, and unresolved matters may be grounds for refusing approval. In Vietnam, an authority that previously issued an approval may also suspend the related activity until the violation has been settled.

The **COMPETENT STATE AUTHORITY** is a government agency empowered by the cited law to issue vehicle registration plates, produce them or authorize their production, and require the resolution of administrative violations concerning road traffic order and safety.

The **COMPETENT STATE MANAGEMENT AUTHORITY** is the relevant authorized government agency whose approval driving test centers must obtain before changing or using specified testing software, scoring equipment, or test vehicles. Its approval is also required before centers relocate functional rooms or alter the layout of driving-test courses.

The **COMPETENT TESTING AUTHORITY** is the authorized body responsible for organizing and conducting examinations on knowledge of laws concerning road traffic order and safety. It must have the facilities and equipment required for the examinations available for its use.

The authority announces examination schedules and locations, publicly posting the relevant information on an electronic information portal within its management scope. It receives or processes applications, including requests to retake the examination. After receiving a complete and valid application, it notifies registered candidates of the examination time and location at least two working days in advance, and promptly informs them of any changes.

On the examination day, the authority notifies candidates of the required time and location, checks their documents, and compares their identity information with their applications. When language assistance is needed, it may hire an interpreter for a participant, including a foreign participant who cannot read or write Vietnamese.
The state authorities responsible for handling violations and for suspending previously approved activities until the violation case has been resolved.
Conduct by a driver of a passenger vehicle consisting of competing for or enticing passengers, which is subject to the penalty specified in Clause 6 of Article 20.
Prohibited conduct under Article 9 of Law 36/2024/QH15, involving争争 or competing to obtain passengers.

A **COMPLETED ADMINISTRATIVE VIOLATION** is an administrative violation whose conduct has ended, as distinguished from a continuing violation. Under Article 4 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, its completed status is determined in accordance with administrative-violation law and is relevant to calculating the limitation period for imposing administrative penalties.
A condition documented by evidence that must be satisfied for the issuance of new vehicle registration certificates and license plates.

id: complex security and public-order situation on a road
ten: COMPLEX SECURITY AND PUBLIC-ORDER SITUATION ON A ROAD
mo_ta: A complex security or public-order situation occurring on a road and listed as an unexpected traffic-disrupting situation.

id: compliance with permitted speed and cargo-dimension signage requirements
ten: COMPLIANCE WITH PERMITTED SPEED AND CARGO-DIMENSION SIGNAGE REQUIREMENTS
mo_ta: A required part of transporting oversized or overweight cargo by road: vehicles must travel at the speed specified in their permit and display signs indicating the cargo’s dimensions.
The activity of obeying road signals, addressed by Article 11 of Law 36/2024/QH15.
The subject of Article 11, which concerns compliance with road traffic signals.

id: compliance with speed and distance rules
ten: COMPLIANCE WITH SPEED AND DISTANCE RULES
mo_ta: The subject of Article 12: complying with rules on vehicle speed and the distance between vehicles.

A corrective measure required for certain violations: excess load must be unloaded, or goods exceeding permitted dimensions must be removed, as directed by competent authorities at the place where the violation is detected.

id: conducting an inspection despite refusal conditions
ten: CONDUCTING AN INSPECTION DESPITE REFUSAL CONDITIONS
mo_ta: A violation described in Article 40(2) of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP: an inspection facility inspects a vehicle that falls under a regulatory condition for refusing inspection. The violation is punishable by a fine of 10,000,000 to 15,000,000 Vietnamese dong.

id: conducting licensed activities while deprived of license use
ten: CONDUCTING LICENSED ACTIVITIES WHILE DEPRIVED OF LICENSE USE
mo_ta: Conduct by an individual or organization that continues activities listed in a license or professional practice certificate during a period of deprivation; the text says it is penalized as conduct without the required license or certificate.
Conferences are among the activities that foreign-registered vehicles may enter Vietnam temporarily to attend.
The issuance of a decision confirming that the bidder won the vehicle license plate auction; this decision starts the 12-month period described in the text.

id: confirming bookings outside a signed contract
ten: CONFIRMING BOOKINGS OUTSIDE A SIGNED CONTRACT
mo_ta: A violation involving the use of a car for contract passenger transport to confirm reservations for passengers beyond the terms of the signed contract.

id: confiscation of administrative violation exhibits and means
ten: CONFISCATION OF ADMINISTRATIVE VIOLATION EXHIBITS AND MEANS
mo_ta: An enforcement action that an on-duty People's Public Security officer is authorized to take against exhibits and means involved in an administrative violation when their value does not exceed 15,000,000 đồng

**CONFISCATION OF EVIDENCE AND VEHICLES** is an administrative enforcement action involving the confiscation of evidence or vehicles used in, or otherwise involved in, an administrative violation. The descriptions give conflicting value limits—30,000,000 đồng and 45,000,000 VND—so the applicable ceiling cannot be determined from the information provided.

**CONFISCATION OF EXHIBITS AND VEHICLES** is an administrative penalty involving the confiscation of exhibits and vehicles used in an administrative violation. It is authorized for specified transport-sector officials under Article 44, Clause 4 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP. The descriptions give two value limits—75,000,000 and 105,000,000 Vietnamese đồng—but do not explain how they differ. The applicable limit therefore depends on the relevant provision or official’s authority.

id: confiscation of exhibits and violation vehicles
ten: CONFISCATION OF EXHIBITS AND VIOLATION VEHICLES
mo_ta: An administrative enforcement action that the provision authorizes the chairperson of a provincial-level People's Committee to carry out.

id: confiscation of illegally installed or used priority signaling devices
ten: CONFISCATION OF ILLEGALLY INSTALLED OR USED PRIORITY SIGNALING DEVICES
mo_ta: A supplementary penalty prescribed for the conduct specified in point đ, clause 2 of Article 7: confiscation of a priority-signaling device installed or used contrary to regulations.

id: confiscation of improperly used priority-signal equipment
ten: CONFISCATION OF IMPROPERLY USED PRIORITY-SIGNAL EQUIPMENT
mo_ta: A supplementary penalty requiring the confiscation of priority-signal equipment installed or used contrary to regulations when the specified violation is committed.

id: confiscation of license plates and plate-altering devices
ten: CONFISCATION OF LICENSE PLATES AND PLATE-ALTERING DEVICES
mo_ta: An additional sanction imposed for specified road traffic violations, involving the seizure of license plates and devices used to alter license plates.

id: confiscation of license plates and vehicles
ten: CONFISCATION OF LICENSE PLATES AND VEHICLES
mo_ta: An additional penalty involving the confiscation of license plates and vehicles that were illegally produced or assembled.

CONFISCATION OF OBJECTS AND VEHICLES is an administrative sanction authorized by Article 44. It involves seizing objects and vehicles used in or connected with an administrative violation, provided their value does not exceed 1,000,000 đồng.
The penalty of confiscating a specialized motor vehicle operated in traffic after it was manufactured, assembled, or modified contrary to regulations.
CONFISCATION OF VEHICLE LICENSE PLATE is an additional or supplementary penalty prescribed for violations specified in Article 14, Clause 3, Point a, and Article 16, Clause 2, Point d.

id: confiscation of vehicles used for administrative violations
ten: CONFISCATION OF VEHICLES USED FOR ADMINISTRATIVE VIOLATIONS
mo_ta: A principal administrative sanction in which a vehicle used to commit an administrative violation is confiscated.

id: confiscation of violation evidence and vehicles
ten: CONFISCATION OF VIOLATION EVIDENCE AND VEHICLES
mo_ta: A supplementary administrative penalty involving confiscation of items connected with an administrative violation and vehicles used to commit it, when confiscation is not imposed as the principal penalty.

id: connection and sharing of road traffic data
ten: CONNECTION AND SHARING OF ROAD TRAFFIC DATA
mo_ta: The activity of connecting, sharing, accessing, and using information in the road traffic order and safety database, including coordination with specialized and other databases.

id: construction and management of specialized databases
ten: CONSTRUCTION AND MANAGEMENT OF SPECIALIZED DATABASES
mo_ta: The administrative activity assigned to the Ministry of Transport under Decree 151/2024/ND-CP, Article 10(3), covering the construction and management of specified specialized databases.
The subject of Article 10 of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP: building databases concerning road traffic order and safety, as well as specialized databases.
The activity of building specialized databases, mentioned alongside databases concerning road traffic order and safety in Article 10.

Consular agencies in Vietnam may be involved in road-traffic matters concerning their personnel and vehicles. They may request permission for a foreign vehicle to participate in traffic by issuing a diplomatic note that states the reason for the request. Their vehicles may receive license plates marked “NG,” with a white background, red lettering, and black numbers. Administrative-technical staff of consular agencies may hold official identity cards and use vehicles bearing “CV” plates. Consular agencies are also among the bodies to be notified about legal violations or traffic accidents involving foreign nationals driving foreign motor vehicles, and their personnel or vehicles may themselves be involved in road accidents.

Foreign consular agencies in Vietnam may use diplomatic notes to explain the reasons and purposes for which vehicles participate in Vietnamese traffic. They may also submit diplomatic notes requesting permission for a right-hand-drive car to be used in Vietnam for a non-tourism purpose, stating the reason for the request. The Ministry of Public Security must notify these agencies of the specified incidents.
Foreign consular missions in Vietnam that the Ministry of Public Security must notify about the specified violations, accidents, or incidents
Consular offices in Vietnam that are designated to receive notifications about relevant legal violations, traffic accidents, and vehicle-related incidents involving foreign drivers or vehicles.

id: continuation of testing rules through june 30, 2027
ten: CONTINUATION OF TESTING RULES THROUGH JUNE 30, 2027
mo_ta: The transitional continuation, until the end of June 30, 2027, of specified testing content, methods, timing, structure, and passing-result requirements.

id: continued driving after the resolution deadline
ten: CONTINUED DRIVING AFTER THE RESOLUTION DEADLINE
mo_ta: The conduct of continuing to drive or putting a vehicle into traffic after the stated deadline, without resolving the violation as required. The text says this may be penalized as driving without the required documents.

id: continued implementation of testing provisions through june 30, 2027
ten: CONTINUED IMPLEMENTATION OF TESTING PROVISIONS THROUGH JUNE 30, 2027
mo_ta: A transitional continuation under which specified requirements concerning testing content, methods, timing, structure, and passing results remain in effect until the end of June 30, 2027.

id: continued use of previously issued b1 automatic licenses
ten: CONTINUED USE OF PREVIOUSLY ISSUED B1 AUTOMATIC LICENSES
mo_ta: The continued validity of qualifying B1 automatic driving licenses issued before Law No. 36/2024/QH15 takes effect, provided they have not been exchanged or reissued under the law.

id: continued validity of class c driving licences
ten: CONTINUED VALIDITY OF CLASS C DRIVING LICENCES
mo_ta: The transitional rule allowing qualifying Class C driving licences to remain valid for driving trucks and tractors with a load capacity of 3,500 kg or more, as well as vehicles covered by licence categories B1 and B2, if the licences have not been exchanged or reissued under the law
The continuation of conduct that had previously been suspended, even after a request from a competent authority to resolve the matter; this is listed as a ground for refusing approval.
Continuously revving a vehicle’s engine while participating in road traffic is listed as prohibited conduct under Article 9 of Law 36/2024/QH15.
A road-traffic violation described in Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, Article 8, Clause 3: continuously using a horn or revving the engine.

id: continuous horn use or engine revving
ten: CONTINUOUS HORN USE OR ENGINE REVVING
mo_ta: A traffic violation involving continuously sounding a horn or repeatedly revving the engine.

id: continuous horn use or engine revving in restricted areas
ten: CONTINUOUS HORN USE OR ENGINE REVVING IN RESTRICTED AREAS
mo_ta: A road traffic violation committed by a motorcycle or similar vehicle driver who continuously sounds the horn or revs the engine in a densely populated area or near a medical examination or treatment facility. Under Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, Article 7, Clause 9, the violation is punishable by a fine of 8,000,000 to 10,000,000 Vietnamese đồng, except for priority vehicles performing official duties as prescribed.

A category of violations described in Article 26, Clause 7 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. Examples include operating without the required transport contract or passenger list, lacking access to electronic contract information, altering or using an improper contract, carrying passengers not listed in the contract, picking up or dropping off passengers at specified business premises or fixed locations on streets, and transporting people outside permitted groups in certain school and student transport services. The stated fines are 5,000,000–6,000,000 Vietnamese đồng for individuals and 10,000,000–12,000,000 Vietnamese đồng for transport businesses or support-service organizations.
Violations consisting of failing to sign or terminate a driver-training contract as required, or having the contract signed by someone other than the learner driver
The act of controlling or guiding livestock, addressed in Article 11 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP in connection with road traffic violations.
The 1968 United Nations Convention on Road Traffic, whose participating countries issue the international driving permits referred to in the decree.

id: conversion of another type of car into a passenger car
ten: CONVERSION OF ANOTHER TYPE OF CAR INTO A PASSENGER CAR
mo_ta: A road-traffic violation described in the decree: converting a car of another type into a passenger car.
A convoy accompanied by a traffic-police vehicle; the provision identifies it as having priority at intersections.
A duty involving protection of a convoy.

A road traffic violation in which a person drives a motorcycle, moped, or similar vehicle in a convoy that obstructs traffic without authorization from a competent authority. Under Article 7, Clause 9 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, it is punishable by a fine of 8,000,000 to 10,000,000 Vietnamese dong.

A cooperative is a type of economic organization established under the Law on Cooperatives. In the described road-transport arrangement, an unnamed cooperative registers a transport business using a member’s vehicle. For purposes of penalties under the stated rule, the cooperative is treated as the vehicle’s owner.
A type of economic organization established under the Law on Cooperatives.
A member of a cooperative who owns a vehicle that the cooperative registers for automobile transport business.
A type of economic organization established under the Law on Cooperatives.
Measures applied to individuals and organizations who commit the specified violations, in addition to penalties.

Measures imposed in addition to penalties, requiring violators to provide, update, transmit, store, and manage information and data collected from vehicle monitoring and driver image-recording devices.

A corrective measure under Article 38 requiring a vehicle involved in specified violations to be returned to the special trade-economic zone or international border-gate economic zone where it is registered to operate.

The corresponding violation referenced in Article 26 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP; where a transport-business individual personally drives the vehicle, the text directs that the penalty be imposed under Article 26, point đ, clause 2

The corresponding violation concerning failure to clean a vehicle or remove its danger symbol after dangerous-goods transport has ended, referenced in Article 26, Clause 2, Point e of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP.
COUNTERTERRORISM refers to participation in efforts to prevent or combat terrorism, including police duties focused on countering terrorist threats.
The unspecified country where a foreign motor vehicle is registered and whose competent authority issues the vehicle’s valid inspection certificate or equivalent document.

id: country party to the vienna convention
ten: COUNTRY PARTY TO THE VIENNA CONVENTION
mo_ta: An unspecified country that is a member of the Vienna Convention; the text does not name any particular country.
The coupling or linking of multiple vehicles, including trucks and specialized trailers, to pull or push trailers while transporting oversized or overweight cargo.

A **credit institution** is a financial organization that may hold or retain a vehicle’s original registration certificate, including when the vehicle is mortgaged or held as collateral. Where the institution retains the original certificate, the vehicle’s driver or operator may be required or permitted under the described provisions to carry a certified copy of the registration certificate together with the institution’s original or valid receipt. If the vehicle is held as collateral, the relevant confirmation document may also be required alongside the registration certificate or its certified copy.
CREDIT INSTITUTION BRANCH is referenced in connection with the provision of a valid receipt accompanied by a certified copy of the vehicle registration certificate or documents.

Credit institutions or other financial institutions may retain a vehicle’s original registration certificate. When the original is held by such an institution, the applicable decree provides for the vehicle’s documentation to include an officially certified or authenticated copy of the registration certificate together with the institution’s original receipt. These documents serve as supporting documentation in the circumstances specified by the provision, including when the vehicle participates in traffic or a replacement document is used.
Crimes and violations of law, including violations relating to road-traffic order and safety and other legal violations, which the force is to resolutely combat and prevent
Criminal activity occurring on road traffic routes, which traffic police are tasked with combating and preventing.
The duty to resolutely fight and prevent crime
Activities to prevent and combat crime, cited as a purpose for stopping road traffic vehicles for inspection and control.
Criminal conduct that may be the subject of reports, denunciations, feedback, petitions, or proposals and may provide grounds for stopping a road traffic vehicle under Article 66.
Criminal handling of cases arising from road traffic accidents; the provision calls for recording the number of cases handled criminally.
Investigation and handling under criminal law and criminal procedure law when a road traffic accident shows signs of a criminal offense
The body of law that governs investigation and resolution of road traffic accidents when an accident shows signs of a crime.

A **criminal offense** may be indicated by the circumstances of a road traffic accident. The indication does not by itself establish that an offense occurred; when signs of a criminal offense are present, the accident is investigated and handled under criminal law and criminal procedure law.
The body of law governing criminal proceedings, which applies to investigating and resolving road traffic accidents that show signs of a crime.
Legal prosecution that a person who causes a road traffic accident may face, depending on the nature and severity of the violation.
The activity of crossing by ferry, addressed by Article 23 of Law 36/2024/QH15.

id: crossing a ferry or pontoon bridge
ten: CROSSING A FERRY OR PONTOON BRIDGE
mo_ta: The road-traffic activity addressed by Article 23, Clause 3 of Law 36/2024/QH15. The provision states that motor vehicles and specialized motorcycles leave the ferry before non-motorized vehicles and pedestrians; when boarding, pedestrians go first, followed by road vehicles as directed by the traffic controller.
A road traffic violation in which a motorcycle, moped, or similar vehicle is driven across the fixed divider between roadways.
A road-traffic violation described in Article 8, Clause 6: driving across the fixed median separating two roadways, subject to the stated exceptions.
A pedestrian traffic violation listed in Article 10.
“CROSSING A PONTOON BRIDGE” refers to a road-traffic activity addressed by Article 23 of Law 36/2024/QH15. The article references it alongside crossing by ferry.
The activity of crossing a road; children under seven must have an adult guide them while doing so.

id: crossing a sidewalk to enter a home or agency
ten: CROSSING A SIDEWALK TO ENTER A HOME OR AGENCY
mo_ta: The exception to the sidewalk-driving violation: driving across a sidewalk to enter a home or agency is excluded from the penalty described in the text.
An unnamed railway crossing guard whose signal requires road users to stop.

id: crossing more than one adjacent lane in a single lane change
ten: CROSSING MORE THAN ONE ADJACENT LANE IN A SINGLE LANE CHANGE
mo_ta: A road-traffic violation involving moving across more than one adjacent lane during a single lane change.
A violation involving driving across the fixed divider between two roadways.

id: crossing the road at an unauthorized place
ten: CROSSING THE ROAD AT AN UNAUTHORIZED PLACE
mo_ta: A pedestrian traffic violation listed in Article 10.

id: crossing the road without the required hand signal
ten: CROSSING THE ROAD WITHOUT THE REQUIRED HAND SIGNAL
mo_ta: A pedestrian traffic violation listed in Article 10.
The crossing-control condition in which a guard gives a signal, a red light flashes, a bell rings, or the road barrier moves or is closed.
Public works areas with many people, listed as places where road users must observe, slow down, or stop to ensure safety
Cultural activities are among the activities for which temporary use of a roadway or sidewalk may be permitted, subject to an approved plan.
A curved section of road where visibility is obstructed, identified as a location where U-turns are prohibited.
A road curve where visibility is limited; the text identifies it as a location where overtaking is prohibited.
The customs authority that handles the procedures for temporarily importing or re-exporting a foreign motor vehicle.
The customs procedures that must be completed at the relevant entry or exit border gate under the decree.
The issuance of a customs declaration associated with a vehicle; the database may record the declaration number, date, and issuing authority.
The authority responsible for issuing the customs declaration associated with an imported or exported vehicle; the text does not specify its name.
The customs formalities that foreign motor vehicles and their users must complete in connection with participating in traffic in Vietnam.

Individuals who may cooperate with, collaborate with, or assist state agencies in carrying out duties to ensure road traffic order and safety. The text provides for rewards or compensation and other legal protections for individuals who suffer harm.
Individuals concerned with implementation of the circular; they are responsible for carrying it out and may report difficulties or obstacles.

id: các cơ quan có liên quan
ten: CÁC CƠ QUAN CÓ LIÊN QUAN
mo_ta: Other relevant authorities, not individually named, with which vehicle-monitoring data may be connected and shared in accordance with law.

id: các đơn vị thuộc cơ quan bộ
ten: CÁC ĐƠN VỊ THUỘC CƠ QUAN BỘ
mo_ta: Units subordinate to the ministry-level agency; their heads are responsible for implementing the circular.
The police organization referenced by the police flag listed among the signals for a traffic-police escort vehicle.

id: công an các đơn vị, địa phương
ten: CÔNG AN CÁC ĐƠN VỊ, ĐỊA PHƯƠNG
mo_ta: CÔNG AN CÁC ĐƠN VỊ, ĐỊA PHƯƠNG (police units and local police authorities) are responsible for reporting difficulties and obstacles encountered while implementing the Circular to the Ministry of Public Security through the Traffic Police Department, so that the Ministry can provide guidance.

CÔNG AN CẤP TỈNH (provincial-level police) operates within the People’s Public Security system. Its director is authorized to confiscate exhibits and vehicles used in administrative violations and to apply specified remedial measures.

CÔNG AN NHÂN DÂN, or Vietnam’s People’s Public Security, is the country’s national public security force. Its officials’ authority to impose administrative sanctions is addressed in Article 43 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. Under clause 3, certain officials may impose fines of up to 22,500,000 đồng.
Provincial and municipal police agencies whose directors are responsible for implementing the circular.

id: công an tỉnh, thành phố trực thuộc trung ương
ten: CÔNG AN TỈNH, THÀNH PHỐ TRỰC THUỘC TRUNG ƯƠNG
mo_ta: Provincial and centrally governed municipal police, whose Traffic Police Divisions handle permits for eligible priority vehicles belonging to agencies and organizations.

id: công chức thanh tra sở giao thông vận tải
ten: CÔNG CHỨC THANH TRA SỞ GIAO THÔNG VẬN TẢI
mo_ta: Officials of the Department of Transport inspectorate who, while performing official duties, are authorized to prepare records of violations within the inspectorate’s management area
The ministry-level government agency whose subordinate units are responsible for implementing the circular.

id: cơ quan chức năng của địa phương
ten: CƠ QUAN CHỨC NĂNG CỦA ĐỊA PHƯƠNG
mo_ta: A local competent authority that may submit an opinion requesting review of the operating speed on a road in operation.

id: cơ quan có thẩm quyền cấp giấy phép
ten: CƠ QUAN CÓ THẨM QUYỀN CẤP GIẤY PHÉP
mo_ta: The competent authority that issues permits for the use of priority signal devices.

id: cơ quan có thẩm quyền của nước ngoài
ten: CƠ QUAN CÓ THẨM QUYỀN CỦA NƯỚC NGOÀI
mo_ta: A competent authority of a foreign country that issued the foreign driving license referred to in the provision. No particular authority is named.

id: cơ quan cảnh sát giao thông
ten: CƠ QUAN CẢNH SÁT GIAO THÔNG
mo_ta: The Traffic Police Agency is responsible for developing and organizing the implementation of plans to ensure road traffic order and safety.

id: cơ quan cảnh sát giao thông trên tuyến đường
ten: CƠ QUAN CẢNH SÁT GIAO THÔNG TRÊN TUYẾN ĐƯỜNG
mo_ta: The traffic police agency responsible for maintaining traffic order and safety on the road or road section that a permitted vehicle will travel along. It is to be notified of the vehicle’s movement.

id: cơ quan cấp giấy phép lưu hành
ten: CƠ QUAN CẤP GIẤY PHÉP LƯU HÀNH
mo_ta: The agency that issues permits for the road use of oversized, overweight, or tracked vehicles. It is responsible for immediately notifying the relevant traffic police agencies when such vehicles travel on a road.
State agencies tasked with carrying out duties to ensure road traffic order and safety. The text refers to them as recipients of cooperation, assistance, and support.

id: cơ quan nhà nước có thẩm quyền
ten: CƠ QUAN NHÀ NƯỚC CÓ THẨM QUYỀN
mo_ta: “CƠ QUAN NHÀ NƯỚC CÓ THẨM QUYỀN” (competent state authority) is an authority empowered to issue vehicle license plates; plates not issued by such an authority may not be used. It may also require the resolution of administrative violations involving road-traffic order and safety. Any such requirement must be fulfilled before the vehicle can undergo inspection.

id: cơ quan quản lý đường bộ
ten: CƠ QUAN QUẢN LÝ ĐƯỜNG BỘ
mo_ta: Road management authorities, which are assigned responsibilities within the scope of their duties and powers for addressing factors that endanger road traffic safety.

id: cơ quan quản lý đường bộ có thẩm quyền
ten: CƠ QUAN QUẢN LÝ ĐƯỜNG BỘ CÓ THẨM QUYỀN
mo_ta: The competent road management authority, as defined in Clause 3, leads coordination to consider and decide permitted operating speeds and organize the placement of speed-limit signs.

Agencies and organizations whose eligible priority vehicles fall under the permit responsibilities of provincial and centrally governed municipal Traffic Police Divisions, subject to the stated exceptions.

id: cơ sở dữ liệu về quản lý thời gian điều khiển phương tiện của người lái xe
ten: CƠ SỞ DỮ LIỆU VỀ QUẢN LÝ THỜI GIAN ĐIỀU KHIỂN PHƯƠNG TIỆN CỦA NGƯỜI LÁI XE
mo_ta: A database used to manage the amount of time vehicle drivers spend driving; it is identified as a source from which specified information is collected.

id: cơ sở dữ liệu về sát hạch cấp giấy phép lái xe
ten: CƠ SỞ DỮ LIỆU VỀ SÁT HẠCH CẤP GIẤY PHÉP LÁI XE
mo_ta: A database for driver’s license testing and issuance, identified as a source from which specified information is collected.

id: cơ sở dữ liệu về trật tự, an toàn giao thông đường bộ
ten: CƠ SỞ DỮ LIỆU VỀ TRẬT TỰ, AN TOÀN GIAO THÔNG ĐƯỜNG BỘ
mo_ta: **CƠ SỞ DỮ LIỆU VỀ TRẬT TỰ, AN TOÀN GIAO THÔNG ĐƯỜNG BỘ** is a database concerning road traffic order and safety. Article 12 of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP addresses how information is collected for the database and describes information it contains, including details about vehicle owners and compulsory civil liability insurance.

id: cơ sở dữ liệu về xử lý vi phạm hành chính về trật tự, an toàn giao thông đường bộ
ten: CƠ SỞ DỮ LIỆU VỀ XỬ LÝ VI PHẠM HÀNH CHÍNH VỀ TRẬT TỰ, AN TOÀN GIAO THÔNG ĐƯỜNG BỘ
mo_ta: The database for administrative violations concerning road traffic order and safety. After driving-license points are restored, it automatically sends notification information to the person whose points were restored.

id: cơ sở dữ liệu về đăng kiểm xe cơ giới, xe máy chuyên dùng
ten: CƠ SỞ DỮ LIỆU VỀ ĐĂNG KIỂM XE CƠ GIỚI, XE MÁY CHUYÊN DÙNG
mo_ta: The database of inspections for motor vehicles and specialized motorcycles, identified as a source from which information is collected.
Educational institutions in which legal knowledge about road traffic order and safety is taught, including the specified content for lower secondary school students

id: cơ sở đào tạo lái xe ô tô
ten: CƠ SỞ ĐÀO TẠO LÁI XE Ô TÔ
mo_ta: CƠ SỞ ĐÀO TẠO LÁI XE Ô TÔ are automobile driver-training establishments that must meet conditions prescribed by the Government. They must maintain curricula and lesson plans and deliver training in the required format and according to the prescribed content and program for each driving-licence class. Establishments that meet the relevant qualifications may also provide road-traffic-law training, conduct tests, and issue certificates to those who pass.

id: cơ sở đào tạo người điều khiển xe máy chuyên dùng
ten: CƠ SỞ ĐÀO TẠO NGƯỜI ĐIỀU KHIỂN XE MÁY CHUYÊN DÙNG
mo_ta: Organizations that train operators of specialized motor vehicles and, if qualified, may conduct road-traffic-law training and tests and issue certificates to people who pass.

A vehicle inspection establishment is an organization providing public services that inspects the technical safety and environmental protection of motor vehicles and special-use motorcycles. It is responsible for inspection results and must refuse inspection in specified violation-related circumstances.

CẢNH SÁT CƠ ĐỘNG (Vietnam’s Mobile Police) is a police force authorized under Article 41, paragraph 3, of Decree No. 168/2024/NĐ-CP to penalize specified administrative violations involving road-traffic order and safety, within its assigned functions and duties. The decree provides different sanctioning limits for authorized officials: a Mobile Police commander may impose fines of up to 75,000,000 đồng, while heads of battalion-level Mobile Police units have specified authority to impose fines of up to 22,500,000 đồng.

CẢNH SÁT GIAO THÔNG (the Traffic Police) is responsible for patrol and control duties concerning road traffic order and safety, including organizing traffic control and directing traffic. In carrying out these duties, the force may use systems, vehicles, equipment, data, weapons, and support tools as authorized by law. It also handles legal violations involving oversized or overweight vehicles and tracked vehicles operating on roads, and manages, operates, and uses the nationwide road traffic order and safety database. People and organizations mobilized by the Traffic Police must comply with its decisions and requests. In urgent situations, the on-scene commander may request assistance from foreign organizations or individuals.
