**DECREE 151/2024/ND-CP** is a Vietnamese government decree cited as the legal basis for a broad set of provisions on road traffic order and safety. Its provisions cover education, traffic databases, priority-vehicle signaling equipment, intelligent transport vehicles, journey-monitoring data, and foreign vehicles operating in Vietnam.

Articles 4–8 address road-safety education in educational institutions. They cover legal-knowledge instruction for students at different levels, safe moped-riding guidance for students beginning upper-secondary or vocational education, and the responsibilities of schools, families, and the Ministry of Education and Training.

Articles 9–16 govern the road traffic order and safety database and specialized databases. They set principles for building and managing the databases; describe responsibilities, funding, access, sharing, and use; and provide for collecting and updating information. Article 11 covers records such as vehicle registration and inspection, drivers and licences, training and certificates, driver operating time and health, compulsory civil-liability insurance, administrative violations, foreign vehicles, and vehicles involved in violations. Article 12 specifies collection methods and sources.

Articles 17–23 regulate signal-emitting devices on priority vehicles, including which vehicles may use them, requirements for their signals and technical specifications, permits and application procedures, permit forms and terms, and the authorities responsible for issuing, reissuing, or revoking permits. Use is restricted to authorized vehicles and official duties.

Articles 25 and 25a concern operating permits for intelligent or smart traffic vehicles, including application documents and procedures for issuing, changing, renewing, or reissuing permits. Articles 27–29 address the use, sharing, transmission, management, and storage of data from journey-monitoring and driver-image recording devices. Article 28 requires driver-image recording equipment for specified passenger, tractor, ambulance, and road-rescue vehicles. Article 31 covers assistance, warnings, and safety measures for oversized or overweight vehicles and certain heavy or unusually long loads.

Articles 32–36 regulate foreign motor vehicles and foreign nationals driving in Vietnam. They set vehicle and driver requirements, including inspection documentation, describe approval procedures for foreign vehicles entering Vietnam for tourism and for certain right-hand-drive vehicles, and assign relevant agencies responsibilities for managing these activities. Article 37 provides transitional arrangements for previously approved programs.

The decree also contains provisions on its scope and appendices, entry into force, repeal of specified legal provisions, and implementation responsibilities.
Article 13 of Decree 151/2024/ND-CP sets out requirements for updating information in the road traffic order and safety database.
A provision concerning vehicles equipped with and using priority-vehicle signal devices, including fire engines deployed on firefighting duties.
A provision of Decree 151/2024/ND-CP cited as the rule governing the non-tourism use of right-hand-drive cars in Vietnamese traffic.

Article 33 of Vietnam’s Decree 151/2024/ND-CP sets out approval and application procedures for certain foreign vehicles entering or travelling on roads in Vietnam. It covers foreign vehicles used for non-tourism purposes, including right-hand-drive cars, and explains how changes to approved routes or departure times are handled.

**DECREE 151/2024/NĐ-CP** is a Vietnamese government decree dated November 15, 2024, providing detailed regulations and implementation measures for the Law on Road Traffic Order and Safety. It covers education, traffic-safety data, vehicle equipment and operation, and the participation of foreign vehicles and drivers in traffic in Vietnam.

Articles 4–8 address road-safety legal education across preschool, primary, lower-secondary, upper-secondary, and vocational education. They also provide for safe motorbike-riding instruction for students and assign related responsibilities to education authorities and institutions.

Articles 9–15 establish principles for building, managing, using, connecting, and sharing the road traffic order and safety database and related specialized databases. The database may include information on vehicle registration, ownership, inspection, origin and sales; driver training, licensing, and health examinations; insurance; accidents and traffic-safety recommendations; administrative violations; transport businesses and vehicle badges; and vehicle journeys and driver images. These provisions also address collecting, updating, accessing, and exchanging information, including data from foreign-vehicle and customs databases.

Articles 17–24 regulate signal-emitting equipment on priority vehicles. They cover technical requirements, installation, eligible vehicles and duties, applications and procedures for issuing or replacing permits, reissuance, validity, revocation, and management of the equipment. The decree includes relevant application forms and technical requirements in appendices. It specifies, for example, signals for ambulances responding to emergencies.

The decree also regulates licensing and operation of intelligent or smart transport vehicles, including application documents, licensing authorities, permit replacement or reissuance, and grounds for revocation; the relevant provisions are cited as Articles 25 and 25a in the descriptions. Other provisions address journey-monitoring equipment for specified transport and emergency vehicles, operating conditions for rudimentary vehicles, commercial vehicles transporting students, and safety measures for oversized, overweight, tracked, or exceptionally large or heavy vehicles.

Articles 32–36 govern foreign motor vehicles and foreign drivers in Vietnam. They address vehicle and driver eligibility, registration and licensing, customs and temporary import and re-export procedures, permitted routes and periods of circulation, required documents and insurance, and compliance with Vietnamese traffic laws. They also establish approval procedures and responsibilities for international travel businesses arranging foreign-vehicle tourism and for entities using right-hand-drive vehicles in Vietnam for non-tourism purposes, as well as responsibilities of relevant agencies. The decree’s final provisions include repeal of specified earlier regulations upon its entry into force.
The event in which Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP takes effect on January 1, 2025, as stated in Article 38.
A legal provision specifying the authority to issue, reissue, and revoke permits for using signal devices on priority vehicles, including an exception for military vehicles on emergency missions.

**DECREE 168/2024/ND-CP** (Nghị định 168/2024/NĐ-CP) is a Vietnamese government decree establishing administrative penalties and remedial measures for violations of road-traffic order and safety. Its scope includes road transport and transport-support services, and it identifies the persons and organizations subject to its provisions.

The decree sets out warnings, fines, supplementary penalties, and corrective measures. Depending on the violation, consequences may include deduction of driving-licence points, temporary suspension or revocation of licences, permits, badges, or professional certificates, and confiscation or temporary detention of vehicles and other exhibits. Article 3 addresses principal penalties and remedial measures, including requirements concerning compliant vehicle equipment and the management and transmission of data from journey-monitoring and driver-image-recording devices.

Its substantive provisions cover a wide range of road users and activities. They address drivers of cars and similar vehicles, motorcycles and mopeds, specialized motorcycles, bicycles and other rudimentary vehicles, as well as pedestrians, passengers, vehicle owners, and operators of rescue vehicles. The decree also regulates violations involving passenger and goods transport, dangerous goods, oversized or overweight vehicles, foreign-plated vehicles, vehicles registered in specified economic zones, animal-drawn vehicles, driver training and testing, and motor-vehicle inspection. Many provisions combine fines with driving-licence point deductions; some prescribe additional measures such as vehicle confiscation or suspension of operating insignia.

The decree also establishes administrative procedures and enforcement authority. It covers limitation periods and the distinction between completed and ongoing violations; principles for determining penalties and sanctioning authority; the responsibilities and powers of police, People’s Committee chairpersons, transport officials, and inspectors; and the temporary detention of vehicles and related documents. Article 47 sets procedures for sanctioning vehicle owners and drivers, including cases detected by technical equipment and rules for identifying the driver. Article 50 addresses the principles and procedures for deducting driving-licence points.

Specific provisions set varying fine amounts according to the offence and responsible party, including higher fines for certain transport, inspection, driver-training, and vehicle-overloading violations. The decree also amends provisions of Decree 100/2019/ND-CP and assigns responsibility for implementation to designated agencies and officials.

Article 32 of Vietnam’s Decree 168/2024/ND-CP establishes penalties for vehicle owners who violate road-traffic regulations. It specifies fine ranges for individual and organizational owners of cars, motorized four-wheel passenger and cargo vehicles, specialized vehicles, and similar vehicles, and provides for deductions from driving-license points. The article also provides for the revocation of certain altered, forged, or improperly issued vehicle-registration and inspection documents.

A provision of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP that sets fines for vehicle owners who violate road traffic regulations. For the specified vehicle types, it prescribes fines of VND 4,000,000–6,000,000 for individuals and VND 8,000,000–12,000,000 for organizations.

A provision of Vietnam’s Decree 168/2024/ND-CP concerning penalties for violations of driver-training and driving-test regulations. It fines driving instructors 2,000,000 to 3,000,000 Vietnamese dong for teaching without wearing the prescribed driving-instructor badge.
Article 40 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP concerns penalties for violations of regulations governing the inspection of motor vehicles, specialized-use motorcycles, and motor vehicle parts.
Article 41 of Vietnam’s Decree 168/2024/ND-CP allocates authority to impose administrative penalties for violations concerning road traffic order and safety.

Article 43 of Vietnam’s Decree 168/2024/ND-CP sets out the authority of the People’s Public Security to impose administrative penalties and identifies the officials whose positions confer that authority.
A provision of Vietnam’s Decree 168/2024/ND-CP that specifies which officials have authority to impose administrative penalties.
A provision of Vietnam’s Decree 168/2024/ND-CP concerning procedures and principles for sanctioning vehicle owners and operators who violate road traffic order and safety regulations.

**DECREE 168/2024/NĐ-CP** is a Vietnamese government decree establishing administrative penalties and remedial measures for violations of road-traffic order and safety. It also introduces or governs deductions and restoration of points on driving licences. Its scope covers individuals and organizations, including Vietnamese and foreign parties operating in Vietnam, and addresses road traffic, road transport, transport-support services, vehicle operation and condition, and related regulatory activities.

The decree sets out fines, supplementary sanctions, licence-point deductions, and corrective measures across a broad range of conduct. Its provisions cover drivers of cars and similar vehicles; motorcycles, mopeds and specialized motor vehicles; bicycles and other rudimentary vehicles; pedestrians; vehicle owners; and operators of transport, rescue, inspection, driver-training and testing services. Topics include traffic-rule violations, stopping and parking, roadway and sidewalk use, passenger and cargo transport, oversized or overweight loads, vehicle dimensions and technical condition, licensing and required equipment, vehicle inspection and registration, driver eligibility, environmental requirements, and driver training and testing. Separate provisions address passenger transport involving preschool children and students, dangerous goods, foreign-plated vehicles, and illegal racing.

The decree also regulates procedures and enforcement. It identifies which officials and bodies may impose sanctions, including People’s Committee chairpersons, People’s Public Security personnel, specialized inspectors and other designated officials. It addresses violation records, overlapping violations, cases detected through technical equipment, temporary custody of vehicles and documents, and procedures for deducting and restoring driving-licence points. It also provides for temporary deprivation of the right to use certain licences and certificates, and for measures such as confiscation, suspension of inspection documents, correction of vehicle condition, reinspection, removal of obstructions, installation or repair of required equipment, and recovery of unlawful gains.

The provisions specify a wide range of fines according to the violation and the responsible party; for example, Article 11 includes a fine of 150,000–250,000 đồng for certain violations involving animals or animal-drawn vehicles, while Article 32 sets different owner penalties for individuals and organizations. Article 53 addresses effective dates for specified provisions, and Article 54 contains transitional rules.

A provision of Vietnam’s Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP concerning penalties for people who lead animals or operate animal-drawn vehicles in violation of road traffic rules. It sets a fine of 150,000 to 250,000 Vietnamese dong for allowing an animal onto a road in a way that does not ensure the safety of people or vehicles using the road.

A provision of Vietnam’s Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP concerning fines and driving-license point deductions for motor-vehicle operators who violate vehicle-condition requirements. It sets a fine of 4,000,000 to 6,000,000 Vietnamese đồng for the specified violations.

A legal provision concerning penalties, driving-license point deductions, and remedial measures for drivers of motorcycles, mopeds, and similar vehicles who violate vehicle-condition rules while participating in traffic

Article 16 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP sets out penalties for operators of specialized vehicles who violate vehicle-condition requirements when participating in traffic, including withdrawal of certain improperly issued or mismatched vehicle documents.
A provision of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP concerning penalties and deduction of driving-license points for drivers of passenger cars and similar vehicles who violate rules on traffic order and safety.

A provision of Vietnam’s Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP setting penalties for specified road-transport and transport-support-service violations. It prescribes fines of 6,000,000 to 8,000,000 Vietnamese đồng for organizations and 3,000,000 to 4,000,000 đồng for individuals.

A provision of Vietnam’s Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP concerning penalties and driver’s-license point deductions for violations of road-traffic regulations by vehicle owners. It sets fines of 4,000,000–6,000,000 Vietnamese đồng for individual owners and 8,000,000–12,000,000 đồng for organizational owners of motorcycles, motorbikes, and similar vehicles who commit the specified violation, provided the conduct does not reach the level of criminal prosecution.

A provision of Vietnam’s Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP that sets administrative fines for vehicle owners who violate road-traffic regulations, including penalties for tampering with or falsifying vehicle registration documents when the conduct does not reach the threshold for criminal prosecution. It specifies different fine ranges for individuals and organizations.

A legal provision specifying that passengers who commit listed traffic-order and safety violations, including failing to follow instructions from the driver or onboard service staff, may be fined between 100,000 and 200,000 Vietnamese dong.

Article 7 of Vietnamese Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP sets out fines and driving-license point deductions for road-traffic violations by operators of motorcycles, mopeds, motorbikes, and similar vehicles. The cited provisions include a fine of 400,000 to 600,000 Vietnamese đồng for driving from 5 km/h to less than 10 km/h over the speed limit, and a fine of 1,000,000 to 2,000,000 đồng for certain other listed violations. The specific violations associated with the latter fine are not identified in the excerpts.
A provision of Vietnam’s Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP that sets fines of 300,000 to 400,000 VND for specified road-traffic violations by bicycle, motorized-bicycle, and other rudimentary-vehicle drivers.

DECREE 184/2025/ND-CP is a Vietnamese government decree. Article 28 addresses the decree’s entry into force and implementation, stating that it enters into force on July 1, 2025, and establishing rules for when Article 2 and its corresponding provisions cease to have effect.

DECREE 184/2025/NĐ-CP is a Vietnamese government decree. Article 27 amends and supplements provisions of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP. Article 28 addresses the decree’s entry into force and specifies when Article 2 ceases to have effect.

DECREE 236/2026/ND-CP (also identified as 236/2026/NĐ-CP) is a Vietnamese government decree. Its text refers to Article 4, while Article 16 addresses the supplementation, repeal, or replacement of specified phrases, points, clauses, articles, and attached appendices.

Decree 236/2026/NĐ-CP is a Vietnamese government decree that amends and supplements regulations on road traffic, permits and transport-related procedures. Its provisions address priority-vehicle signal devices, intelligent traffic vehicles, and foreign motor vehicles operating in Vietnam.

Articles 6 and 8 amend rules for installing and managing signal devices on priority vehicles and for issuing or reissuing permits to use them. Article 17 sets transitional rules for administrative-procedure files received or postmarked before the decree takes effect, and for existing permits to use signal devices on priority vehicles. The decree’s text also includes the heading for Article 7 and refers to Article 9, although the available descriptions do not specify their subject matter.

Article 12 adds Article 25a, setting out procedures to issue, exchange, reissue and revoke operating permits for intelligent traffic vehicles. Article 13 amends Article 33, including requirements for approving foreign motor vehicles entering Vietnam for tourism and right-hand-drive cars participating in traffic. Article 15 amends and supplements certain clauses of Article 35.

Article 18 addresses the decree’s entry into force and related implementation matters. It provides for procedures to approve international travel service businesses that organize foreign visitors bringing foreign motor vehicles into Vietnam for tourism, as well as procedures for bringing right-hand-drive cars into Vietnam for non-tourism purposes. It also concerns databases on foreign motor vehicles driven by foreign nationals in Vietnam and on transport businesses and transport-business vehicle insignia. The relevant provisions take effect on 1 July 2027.
The event of Decree 236/2026/NĐ-CP coming into force on July 1, 2026.

Decree 238/2026/ND-CP (Nghị định 238/2026/NĐ-CP) is a Vietnamese government decree that amends and supplements provisions of existing regulations. Article 8 amends specified points and clauses of Article 21; Article 13 amends Article 42, concerning the authority of chairpersons of People’s Committees to impose administrative penalties and remedial measures; and Article 16 amends Clause 2 of Article 46. Article 9 is also referenced in the decree.

The decree addresses rules concerning the transport of construction materials, earth, rocks, waste, bulk goods, and other loads, including cases where loads are not properly covered or materials or water spill onto the road. Article 20 concerns the decree’s entry into force and assigns responsibility for guiding, organizing, and enforcing its implementation.

DECREE 238/2026/NĐ-CP is a Vietnamese government decree amending and supplementing regulations on administrative penalties for road-traffic violations and related matters. Its provisions include amendments to several points of Clause 3, Article 3, and Article 3 also amends point b, clause 8, Article 13 concerning vehicle license plates that are missing, improperly positioned or formatted, unclear, altered, obscured, or made difficult to identify by materials or devices. Article 4 further revises rules on violations involving improper plate placement or formatting and obscured or altered plate information.

The decree also contains provisions on road-traffic penalties in Article 8 and refers to Article 11. Article 15 amends and supplements Article 44, which sets out the administrative sanctioning authority of road and construction officials. Article 18 adds rules governing administrative penalties related to image-recording equipment on certain road-transport vehicles. Article 19 addresses the supplementation, replacement, and repeal of specified phrases, points, clauses, and articles. Article 21 establishes transitional rules for handling administrative violations involving road-traffic order and safety.
The event of Decree 238/2026/NĐ-CP taking effect on August 15, 2026.
A decree of the Government of Vietnam, dated March 7, 2024, regulating the management of road motor vehicles registered abroad and brought into Vietnam for tourism by foreign nationals.
A decree of the Government of Vietnam, dated October 1, 2009, regulating the participation in traffic in Vietnam of right-hand-drive cars registered abroad and owned by foreigners.
The date on which Decree 236/2026/NĐ-CP takes effect; files received by the competent authority or postmarked before this date are covered by the transitional provision.
The event addressed by Article 20, which concerns the entry into force of Decree 238/2026/ND-CP.

id: decree in force when the violation occurred
ten: DECREE IN FORCE WHEN THE VIOLATION OCCURRED
mo_ta: The decree that was in effect at the time the administrative violation was committed; the text specifies that this decree governs the penalty, without naming it.

A Vietnamese government decree dated January 17, 2020, concerning the business and business conditions of road transport by automobile. The text states that specified provisions of this decree are repealed by Decree No. 151/2024/NĐ-CP and that it was amended and supplemented by Decrees No. 47/2022/NĐ-CP and No. 41/2024/NĐ-CP.

DECREE NO. 151/2024/ND-CP is a Vietnamese government decree concerning road traffic order and safety. Article 1 defines its scope, covering when people and vehicles must assist drivers, warn other road users, and take safety measures for oversized, overweight, crawler-track, and exceptionally large or heavy cargo vehicles operating on roads. It also covers journey-monitoring and driver-image recording devices for specified commercial vehicles, permits for intelligent-transport vehicles, and operating conditions for rudimentary vehicles.

The decree addresses several related procedures and responsibilities. Article 12 concerns the collection of information for the road traffic order and safety database. Article 21 sets out procedures for issuing or reissuing permits to use signal-emitting devices on priority vehicles, while Article 22, Clause 2 provides that such permits for vehicles assigned emergency duties expire immediately when the emergency ends. The decree is also cited as the legal basis for procedures to withdraw operating permits for intelligent-transport vehicles.

Other provisions cover road users and vehicle management: Article 5, Clause 1 concerns safe motorbike-riding guidance for students beginning upper-secondary school or vocational education, including recognizing and responding to dangerous situations. Article 30 sets requirements for the exterior paint and identifying signs of vehicles transporting preschool children and pupils. Article 36 specifies the responsibilities of relevant agencies in managing foreign nationals who drive foreign motor vehicles in traffic in Vietnam.

Decree No. 151/2024/NĐ-CP is a Vietnamese government decree addressing road traffic order and safety, related databases, and signaling devices on priority vehicles. Article 11, clause 15, concerns information about foreign motor vehicles driven by foreigners participating in road traffic in Vietnam. Article 12 provides for collecting information for the Road Traffic Order and Road Safety Database, while Article 15 governs management of that database and assigns coordination responsibilities to government bodies.

The decree also sets out rules for signal-emitting devices on priority vehicles. Article 21 addresses procedures for issuing and reissuing permits to use the devices. Under Article 24, agencies and organizations licensed to use them are responsible for their management, installation, and use; the competent authority issues and may revoke permits. Licensed entities must report annually on their management and use of the devices to the authority that issued the permit, before December 15, using Form No. 02d in Appendix II.

Article 38, clause 2, repeals specified provisions, including provisions of Decree No. 10/2020/NĐ-CP. Decree No. 151/2024/NĐ-CP is also cited as the legal basis for provisions on collecting database information and is relevant to administrative procedures referenced in a transitional provision of Decree No. 236/2026/NĐ-CP.

DECREE NO. 168/2024/ND-CP is a Vietnamese government decree that provides the legal basis for administrative penalties for violations of road traffic order and safety in road transport and related support services.

Its provisions address a range of offenses and enforcement measures. Article 13 covers motor-vehicle condition and technical-safety violations, including requirements to install or replace equipment and restore vehicle features or license plates. Article 20 sets penalties and driving-license point deductions for drivers of passenger cars and similar vehicles who breach traffic rules, while Article 22 addresses car drivers transporting oversized or overweight goods. Article 26 establishes penalties and corrective measures for violations involving road transport and transport support services. Article 27 covers drivers of commercial passenger vehicles transporting preschool- or primary-school children, including vehicles used in combination with student pickup and drop-off services. Article 32, Clause 17, provides for vehicle confiscation in specified cases. Articles 41 and 42 address enforcement authority, including the powers of officials authorized to impose certain sanctions and People’s Committee chairpersons at different levels.
A Vietnamese government decree whose Article 2 is scheduled to cease to have effect on 1 March 2027, subject to a possible extension.

A Vietnamese government decree whose Article 19 assigns responsibility for its implementation to ministers, heads of ministerial-level agencies, chairpersons of provincial and centrally governed municipal People's Committees, and other relevant parties.

DECREE NO. 236/2026/NĐ-CP is a Vietnamese government decree that amends and supplements rules concerning road traffic order and safety. Article 5 amends Clause 1 of Article 14 on connections to and sharing of information involving the road traffic order and safety database. Article 14 adds Article 33a, which sets out procedures for approving international travel-service businesses and other organizations or individuals to bring foreign motor vehicles, including right-hand-drive cars, into Vietnam, as well as procedures for amending information in an existing approval. Article 17 establishes transitional rules for administrative-procedure applications received or postmarked before the decree takes effect.
A Vietnamese government decree dated April 16, 2024, that amended and supplemented Decree No. 10/2020/NĐ-CP.
A Vietnamese government decree dated July 19, 2022, that amended and supplemented Decree No. 10/2020/NĐ-CP.

The deduction of driver’s license points is a consequence under Article 24 for covered violations involving vehicles that exceed permitted weight or dimension limits. The decree’s heading refers to this point deduction alongside the fines imposed for such violations.
People whom military vehicles may be assigned to escort.
The departure of a foreign national or foreign motor vehicle later than the time specified in an approval, including delays that cause the maximum permitted stay in Vietnam to be exceeded.

A **densely populated area** is a populated geographic area where roads may have unfavorable operating conditions, such as restricted sightlines or infrastructure close to the edge of the traveled way. In this area, continuous horn use and engine revving by motorcycle and similar-vehicle drivers are prohibited, subject to the stated exception. Horn use is also prohibited between 10 p.m. and 5 a.m. under the cited rule.

Densely populated areas are places with a high concentration of people. Road users must remain alert and slow down or stop when needed to ensure safety. Between 22:00 and 05:00, a vehicle may request to overtake in these areas only by using lights.

id: department for administrative management of social order
ten: DEPARTMENT FOR ADMINISTRATIVE MANAGEMENT OF SOCIAL ORDER
mo_ta: The Department for Administrative Management of Social Order (Cục Cảnh sát quản lý hành chính về trật tự xã hội) is identified in Article 43 as an authority with powers to impose administrative sanctions. Those powers include officials such as the department’s director and chiefs of its professional or specialist divisions. Under Article 43, Clause 6, the director is also authorized to confiscate objects and vehicles used in administrative violations.

id: department for administrative management of social order director
ten: DEPARTMENT FOR ADMINISTRATIVE MANAGEMENT OF SOCIAL ORDER DIRECTOR
mo_ta: The director of the Department for Administrative Management of Social Order, authorized to impose administrative penalties and apply remedial measures under Article 43.

id: department of administrative management of social order
ten: DEPARTMENT OF ADMINISTRATIVE MANAGEMENT OF SOCIAL ORDER
mo_ta: The Department of Administrative Management of Social Order is a department of the People’s Public Security responsible for administrative management of social order. Under Decree 168/2024/ND-CP, its director is authorized to impose specified administrative sanctions, confiscate exhibits and vehicles involved in administrative violations, and apply specified remedial measures. Under Article 43, clause 6, the director may also temporarily revoke permits or professional certificates and temporarily suspend operations. The department’s professional-division heads are also among the officials authorized to impose administrative sanctions.

id: department of administrative management of social order police
ten: DEPARTMENT OF ADMINISTRATIVE MANAGEMENT OF SOCIAL ORDER POLICE
mo_ta: A police department responsible for administrative management of social order; its professional-division heads are listed as having sanctioning authority.

id: department of administrative police for social order
ten: DEPARTMENT OF ADMINISTRATIVE POLICE FOR SOCIAL ORDER
mo_ta: The DEPARTMENT OF ADMINISTRATIVE POLICE FOR SOCIAL ORDER is part of the People’s Public Security and is responsible for administrative policing and maintaining social order. Its director, as well as the heads of its professional divisions, is authorized to impose administrative penalties under Article 43.

The **Department of Construction** (Vietnamese: **Sở Xây dựng**) is a government department whose director is identified in Articles 41 and 44 as an official with authority to impose specified administrative penalties for violations. Under Article 44, including paragraph 2, the director may apply remedial measures and, where authorized, temporarily revoke permits or suspend activities. This authority applies during inspections and is limited to the sanctions specified in the decree. No particular department, locality, or individual director is identified.

id: department of data management, exploitation, processing, operation and digital transformation
ten: DEPARTMENT OF DATA MANAGEMENT, EXPLOITATION, PROCESSING, OPERATION AND DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION
mo_ta: A professional department within the Traffic Police Department responsible for data management and use, processing, operations, and digital transformation.

id: department of guidance and management of conditional security-and-order businesses and seals
ten: DEPARTMENT OF GUIDANCE AND MANAGEMENT OF CONDITIONAL SECURITY-AND-ORDER BUSINESSES AND SEALS
mo_ta: A professional department within the Administrative Police Department for Social Order that guides and manages business sectors subject to security-and-order conditions, as well as seals.

id: department of guidance and management of weapons, explosives, support tools and fireworks
ten: DEPARTMENT OF GUIDANCE AND MANAGEMENT OF WEAPONS, EXPLOSIVES, SUPPORT TOOLS AND FIREWORKS
mo_ta: A professional department within the Administrative Police Department for Social Order that guides and manages weapons, explosives, support tools, and fireworks.

id: department of guidance on road and railway traffic patrol and control
ten: DEPARTMENT OF GUIDANCE ON ROAD AND RAILWAY TRAFFIC PATROL AND CONTROL
mo_ta: A professional department within the Traffic Police Department that guides patrol and control of road and railway traffic.

id: department of guidance on traffic control and escort
ten: DEPARTMENT OF GUIDANCE ON TRAFFIC CONTROL AND ESCORT
mo_ta: A professional department within the Traffic Police Department that guides traffic control and escort operations.

id: department of guidance, propaganda, investigation and resolution of traffic accidents
ten: DEPARTMENT OF GUIDANCE, PROPAGANDA, INVESTIGATION AND RESOLUTION OF TRAFFIC ACCIDENTS
mo_ta: A professional department within the Traffic Police Department, responsible for guidance, communication, investigation, and resolution concerning traffic accidents.

id: department of guidance, registration and inspection of vehicles
ten: DEPARTMENT OF GUIDANCE, REGISTRATION AND INSPECTION OF VEHICLES
mo_ta: A professional department within the Traffic Police Department that guides vehicle registration and inspection.

id: department of guidance, training, testing and driver’s licence management
ten: DEPARTMENT OF GUIDANCE, TRAINING, TESTING AND DRIVER’S LICENCE MANAGEMENT
mo_ta: A professional department within the Traffic Police Department that guides training, testing, and management of driver’s licences.

id: department of military vehicles and transport
ten: DEPARTMENT OF MILITARY VEHICLES AND TRANSPORT
mo_ta: A department of Vietnam’s Ministry of National Defense that issues operating permits for intelligent transport vehicles serving national defense purposes.

id: department of police for administrative management of social order
ten: DEPARTMENT OF POLICE FOR ADMINISTRATIVE MANAGEMENT OF SOCIAL ORDER
mo_ta: The department responsible for police administrative management of social order, whose professional-division heads are listed as having authority to impose penalties.

The Department of Transport is a provincial or municipal government department whose inspectorate may be established depending on the circumstances described in the applicable provision. Where the inspectorate exists, it is referred to as the Department of Transport Inspectorate. The department’s Chief Inspector is authorized under the cited provisions to enforce administrative-violation rules, including imposing fines of up to 37,500,000 đồng and confiscating exhibits and vehicles used in violations, subject to the applicable value limit.

The **DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORT INSPECTORATE** is the inspectorate associated with or operating within a Department of Transport. The cited provisions address situations in which the inspectorate has not been established, including this as a condition relevant to the Chief Inspector’s authority. That authority includes imposing specialized inspection sanctions: the Chief Inspector may revoke, for a fixed period, the right to use permits or professional certificates, or suspend operations for a fixed period.
A unit affiliated with an enterprise; the text lists branches and representative offices as examples.

id: deprivation of the right to use a license or professional practice certificate
ten: DEPRIVATION OF THE RIGHT TO USE A LICENSE OR PROFESSIONAL PRACTICE CERTIFICATE
mo_ta: A time-limited administrative penalty that removes an individual's or organization's right to use a license or professional practice certificate.
Children in preschool, pupils, students, officials, public employees, and workers who are the specified passenger groups for the contract-transport rules described in the text.
A location provided for U-turns through traffic organization, where turning around is permitted under the stated exception.

id: designation of testing and certification establishments
ten: DESIGNATION OF TESTING AND CERTIFICATION ESTABLISHMENTS
mo_ta: The designation of testing and certification establishments, identified as part of the technical safety and environmental protection certification process.

id: destruction or damage of road traffic equipment
ten: DESTRUCTION OR DAMAGE OF ROAD TRAFFIC EQUIPMENT
mo_ta: The prohibited act of destroying, damaging, or rendering ineffective road traffic control or monitoring equipment, including smart devices that assist with traffic command and control.
An administrative violation identified using technical or professional equipment when authorities have not immediately stopped the vehicle.
The process of identifying violations of road traffic order and safety laws and other legal violations.

id: detection, receipt, and handling of road traffic accident reports
ten: DETECTION, RECEIPT, AND HANDLING OF ROAD TRAFFIC ACCIDENT REPORTS
mo_ta: The process addressed by Article 81: detecting, receiving, and handling reports concerning road traffic accidents.

id: detention of vehicles and related items
ten: DETENTION OF VEHICLES AND RELATED ITEMS
mo_ta: A measure listed in the text for investigating and resolving road traffic accidents whose criminal status has not been determined. It involves temporarily retaining vehicles, objects, documents, licenses, and professional certificates belonging to the driver or involved in road traffic.

id: determination and signposting of permitted operating speed
ten: DETERMINATION AND SIGNPOSTING OF PERMITTED OPERATING SPEED
mo_ta: The process of considering and deciding the permitted operating speed for a road section and arranging the installation of speed-limit signs.
The process of determining which authorities are empowered to impose administrative penalties for violations involving road traffic order and safety.

id: determination of human and property damage
ten: DETERMINATION OF HUMAN AND PROPERTY DAMAGE
mo_ta: Determination of harm to people and damage to property caused by a road traffic accident

id: determination of permitted operating speed and installation of speed signs
ten: DETERMINATION OF PERMITTED OPERATING SPEED AND INSTALLATION OF SPEED SIGNS
mo_ta: The procedure described in Article 10: the competent road management authority, coordinating with the route's traffic police and the relevant district-level People's Committee, considers and decides the permitted operating speed and organizes the installation of speed signs in the specified cases.

id: determination of the deprivation period start date
ten: DETERMINATION OF THE DEPRIVATION PERIOD START DATE
mo_ta: The legal determination of when the period of temporary deprivation of the right to use a license or practice certificate begins.

id: development and integration of legal and road-traffic-safety education
ten: DEVELOPMENT AND INTEGRATION OF LEGAL AND ROAD-TRAFFIC-SAFETY EDUCATION
mo_ta: The activity of developing, integrating, and incorporating legal knowledge and road traffic order and safety into teaching at preschool and general education institutions.
DIKE PROTECTION DUTY is an official duty performed by designated vehicles to protect dikes. Vehicles assigned to this duty are eligible to use priority-vehicle signal equipment.
A duty to protect dikes, for which the assigned vehicle is included among priority vehicles.
A duty performed by a vehicle protecting dikes; the text lists such vehicles among those given priority.
Diplomatic agencies whose emblems or identifying symbols are referenced as the kind that may not be imitated on a vehicle.

Diplomatic Missions are foreign diplomatic representative bodies in Vietnam. Their personnel and vehicles may be involved in road traffic accidents in the country. Foreign diplomatic missions may also be notified about legal violations or traffic accidents involving foreign nationals driving foreign motor vehicles.

Foreign diplomatic missions in Vietnam are designated recipients of notifications from the Ministry of Public Security concerning specified legal violations, traffic accidents, and vehicle-related incidents involving foreign drivers or vehicles. They may also submit diplomatic notes requesting permission for a right-hand-drive car to participate in Vietnamese traffic for a non-tourism purpose, with the reason for the request stated.

id: diplomatic note requesting non-tourism vehicle entry
ten: DIPLOMATIC NOTE REQUESTING NON-TOURISM VEHICLE ENTRY
mo_ta: A diplomatic communication that states the reason for requesting permission for a right-hand-drive car to participate in traffic in Vietnam for a non-tourism purpose.

Diplomatic representative agencies in Vietnam may have vehicles registered with “NG” license plates, which feature a white background, red lettering, and black numbers. They may also issue a diplomatic note requesting permission for a foreign vehicle to participate in traffic and explaining the reason for the request. The agencies’ administrative-technical staff may hold official identity cards and use vehicles bearing “CV” license plates.
Foreign diplomatic representative agencies in Vietnam that the Ministry of Public Security must notify about the specified incidents.

id: direct driving by a transport business individual
ten: DIRECT DRIVING BY A TRANSPORT BUSINESS INDIVIDUAL
mo_ta: The circumstance in which an individual engaged in transport business directly operates the vehicle involved in the violation.

id: direct on-scene commander of the traffic police
ten: DIRECT ON-SCENE COMMANDER OF THE TRAFFIC POLICE
mo_ta: The traffic police commander directly in charge at the scene, authorized to mobilize civilian people, vehicles, and equipment in an urgent situation.

id: direct operation of a vehicle by a transport-business individual
ten: DIRECT OPERATION OF A VEHICLE BY A TRANSPORT-BUSINESS INDIVIDUAL
mo_ta: The circumstance in which an individual engaged in transport business personally drives the vehicle associated with the route-information display violation.

id: direct traffic police commander at the scene
ten: DIRECT TRAFFIC POLICE COMMANDER AT THE SCENE
mo_ta: The person who directly commands traffic police at the scene. Under Article 68, this commander may mobilize civilians and civilian vehicles or equipment in urgent circumstances.
A duty of traffic police during road traffic patrol and control, involving directing and controlling road traffic.

id: directly committing a road-traffic violation as a vehicle owner
ten: DIRECTLY COMMITTING A ROAD-TRAFFIC VIOLATION AS A VEHICLE OWNER
mo_ta: The conduct of a vehicle owner personally operating a vehicle and committing the violation specified in Article 21, Clause 2, Point b.

**DIRECTLY COMMITTING A VEHICLE VIOLATION** refers to a vehicle owner personally operating the vehicle and committing a violation specified in point b, paragraph 3, Article 22 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, or point a, clause 4, Article 34.

id: directly committing a vehicle-related traffic violation
ten: DIRECTLY COMMITTING A VEHICLE-RELATED TRAFFIC VIOLATION
mo_ta: Conduct described in the decree in which a vehicle owner directly operates a vehicle and commits a violation specified in Article 21, Clause 8, points a or b.

id: directly operating a vehicle in violation
ten: DIRECTLY OPERATING A VEHICLE IN VIOLATION
mo_ta: The act of a vehicle owner personally operating a vehicle in the manner prohibited by point b, clause 4, Article 34 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP.

id: director general of the vietnam register
ten: DIRECTOR GENERAL OF THE VIETNAM REGISTER
mo_ta: The head of the Vietnam Register, identified in Article 44 as having authority to impose penalties.

id: director general of the vietnam road administration
ten: DIRECTOR GENERAL OF THE VIETNAM ROAD ADMINISTRATION
mo_ta: The Director General of the Vietnam Road Administration is the official who heads the Administration. Under Article 44, the Director General has authority to impose specified administrative penalties and may establish an inspection team or delegation. The head of that team or delegation is also authorized to impose penalties.

id: director of a road management area
ten: DIRECTOR OF A ROAD MANAGEMENT AREA
mo_ta: The official heading a road management area under the Vietnam Road Administration. Article 44 grants this office sanctioning authority, including the power to impose fines up to 37,500,000 đồng and apply other specified administrative measures.

The Director of Provincial-Level Police is the official who leads a provincial-level police authority or unit. Under the cited provisions of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP, the director is authorized to impose administrative sanctions, including fines of up to 75,000,000 Vietnamese dong, and to apply specified remedial measures.

id: director of the department for administrative management of social order
ten: DIRECTOR OF THE DEPARTMENT FOR ADMINISTRATIVE MANAGEMENT OF SOCIAL ORDER
mo_ta: The DIRECTOR OF THE DEPARTMENT FOR ADMINISTRATIVE MANAGEMENT OF SOCIAL ORDER is the official who leads the Department and is authorized under Article 43 to impose sanctions for administrative violations. Under Article 43, Clause 6, the Director may also confiscate objects and vehicles used in such violations.

id: director of the department of administrative management of social order
ten: DIRECTOR OF THE DEPARTMENT OF ADMINISTRATIVE MANAGEMENT OF SOCIAL ORDER
mo_ta: The Director of the Department of Administrative Management of Social Order is the official heading that department. Under Article 43, Clauses 6 and 7 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, the Director is authorized to apply specified remedial measures and to confiscate exhibits and vehicles involved in administrative violations. The Director may also revoke licenses or professional certificates for a fixed period or temporarily suspend activities.

id: director of the department of administrative police for social order
ten: DIRECTOR OF THE DEPARTMENT OF ADMINISTRATIVE POLICE FOR SOCIAL ORDER
mo_ta: The office-holder heading the Department of Administrative Police for Social Order, identified in Article 43 as having authority to impose penalties.

id: director of the department of construction
ten: DIRECTOR OF THE DEPARTMENT OF CONSTRUCTION
mo_ta: The **Director of the Department of Construction** is an unnamed official who heads a Department of Construction; no particular person or department is identified. Under the decree, Article 44 lists the director among officials authorized to impose administrative penalties. This authority includes imposing fines of up to 60,000,000 đồng and applying specified administrative and remedial measures, including those set out in Article 3(3). The director may also temporarily revoke the right to use a permit or temporarily suspend activities. The descriptions additionally refer to Article 41 as a source of the director’s penalty authority.

id: director of the national population data center
ten: DIRECTOR OF THE NATIONAL POPULATION DATA CENTER
mo_ta: The unnamed director of the National Population Data Center, whose position grants authority to impose penalties under Article 43.

id: director of the regional road management area
ten: DIRECTOR OF THE REGIONAL ROAD MANAGEMENT AREA
mo_ta: The Director of the Regional Road Management Area under the Vietnam Road Administration is an official with authority to impose administrative penalties. The role is listed in Article 44 among officials with sanctioning authority.

id: director of the road management area
ten: DIRECTOR OF THE ROAD MANAGEMENT AREA
mo_ta: The Director of the Road Management Area is the official who heads a Road Management Area under the Vietnam Road Administration. The position is recognized in Articles 41 and 44 as having authority to impose administrative penalties. This authority includes imposing fines of up to 37,500,000 đồng, temporarily withdrawing the right to use permits, temporarily suspending activities, and applying the remedial measures specified in Article 3, Clause 3.

id: director of the road management area under the vietnam road administration
ten: DIRECTOR OF THE ROAD MANAGEMENT AREA UNDER THE VIETNAM ROAD ADMINISTRATION
mo_ta: The official leading a road management area under the Vietnam Road Administration, listed among those with sanctioning authority under Article 44.

id: director of the traffic police department
ten: DIRECTOR OF THE TRAFFIC POLICE DEPARTMENT
mo_ta:
The **Director of the Traffic Police Department** is the office-holder heading the department; the role is identified by title, not by personal name. The Director is responsible for directing, monitoring, inspecting, and urging implementation of the relevant circular, and for ensuring consistent guidance at locations where legal-knowledge examinations are held. The position also covers organizing research and the application of science and technology, and managing examinations on legal knowledge concerning road traffic order and safety.

Under Article 43 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, the Director is authorized to impose administrative sanctions and to apply specified remedial measures. The listed powers include confiscating exhibits, objects, and vehicles used in administrative violations, and revoking licences or professional certificates for a fixed period or temporarily suspending activities. The descriptions cite different clauses of Article 43 for some of these powers; taken together, they identify the Director as holding the stated enforcement authorities.

The Director also manages and operates the database on administrative violations involving road traffic order and safety, and is authorized to restore driving-licence points in cases covered by Clause 3 of Article 51, including through automatic restoration where applicable.

The Director of the Vietnam Register is the official who heads the Vietnam Register. Under Article 44, Clause 4, the Director is authorized to exercise the specified sanctioning powers and apply the remedial measures set out in Article 3, Clause 3.

id: director of the vietnam road administration
ten: DIRECTOR OF THE VIETNAM ROAD ADMINISTRATION
mo_ta: The Director of the Vietnam Road Administration is the official who heads the agency and is granted administrative sanctioning authority under Article 44. The Director may impose penalties and apply the remedial measures specified by the relevant provisions. The Director is also authorized to establish an inspection team or delegation. The head of such a team may have separate sanctioning powers under Article 44, including authority to impose fines of up to 60,000,000 đồng and, where specified, apply remedial measures.

id: directors of provincial and centrally governed city police
ten: DIRECTORS OF PROVINCIAL AND CENTRALLY GOVERNED CITY POLICE
mo_ta: Officials who lead provincial and centrally governed city police organizations and are responsible for implementing the circular.

id: directors of provincial and centrally governed municipal police
ten: DIRECTORS OF PROVINCIAL AND CENTRALLY GOVERNED MUNICIPAL POLICE
mo_ta: The Directors of Provincial and Centrally Governed Municipal Police are the officials who head their respective provincial or centrally governed municipal police agencies. They are responsible for organizing mobile checks of road-traffic legal knowledge when the conditions specified in Article 5 are met, and for periodically or exceptionally reporting the results of those checks within their areas of management.

id: directors of provincial and municipal police
ten: DIRECTORS OF PROVINCIAL AND MUNICIPAL POLICE
mo_ta: Directors of police forces in provinces and centrally governed cities, who are responsible for implementing Circular 13/2025/TT-BCA.
Activities to prevent and respond to disasters, cited as a purpose for stopping road traffic vehicles for inspection and control.
Activities to prevent or respond to natural disasters, listed as a circumstance permitting the transport of people in a goods-truck cargo bed.
Operations to address and remedy the effects of a natural disaster.

**Disaster Response** includes operations to address natural-disaster incidents and remediate their consequences. It is a qualifying mission for use of a priority-vehicle signal device, and vehicles performing these duties are listed as priorities.
Response to and recovery from disaster incidents, duties for which priority vehicles use flashing blue lights under the decree.
The act of discharging chemicals or waste in a way that endangers road traffic safety.

id: discharging or spilling hazardous chemicals or waste
ten: DISCHARGING OR SPILLING HAZARDOUS CHEMICALS OR WASTE
mo_ta: The prohibited acts of dumping, discharging, or spilling chemicals or waste in a way that endangers road traffic safety.

id: discovery of a forged permit application
ten: DISCOVERY OF A FORGED PERMIT APPLICATION
mo_ta: The discovery that an application was falsified to obtain an operating permit for a smart transport vehicle; this is a ground for revoking the permit
The point at which an ongoing administrative violation is discovered, which determines which decree applies.

id: discovery or review of a violation
ten: DISCOVERY OR REVIEW OF A VIOLATION
mo_ta: The later discovery of a road-traffic violation or its ongoing consideration for resolution after the conduct has ended.
Activities to prevent the spread of disease, cited as a purpose for stopping road traffic vehicles for inspection and control.
The event of leaving a ferry, during which motor vehicles and specialized motorcycles disembark before non-motorized vehicles and pedestrians.
Prohibited conduct involving disembarking passengers to avoid detection of a vehicle exceeding legally permitted passenger limits.

**DISOBEYING A TRAFFIC SIGNAL** is a road traffic violation in which a vehicle operator fails to obey a traffic signal. Under Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, the fine depends on the vehicle category: Clause 9 of Article 6 provides a fine of 18,000,000 to 20,000,000 Vietnamese đồng for the applicable category, while Clause 7 of Article 8 provides a fine of 6,000,000 to 8,000,000 Vietnamese đồng for another category. These penalties therefore reflect different vehicle classifications rather than a single conflicting fine range.

A road traffic violation consisting of failing to obey commands or instructions from a traffic controller or traffic control officer; the text specifies a fine of 150,000 to 250,000 Vietnamese dong for this conduct.
Causing disorder by taking advantage of a road traffic accident.

id: displaying goods on the central median strip
ten: DISPLAYING GOODS ON THE CENTRAL MEDIAN STRIP
mo_ta: A violation consisting of occupying the central median strip to display goods.

id: disrupting order at a road traffic accident
ten: DISRUPTING ORDER AT A ROAD TRAFFIC ACCIDENT
mo_ta: Using an accident as an opportunity to cause disorder, prohibited by Article 9 of Law 36/2024/QH15.

**DRIVER** is a person who operates a road vehicle, including a car or similar vehicle, a motorcycle or moped, a specialized motor vehicle, or a vehicle transporting passengers or goods. The applicable rules require a driver to meet prescribed age and health conditions and hold an applicable, valid driving licence, subject to the stated exception for certain motorcycle drivers. A valid health certificate may also be required in the registration dossier for a road-traffic legal-knowledge examination.

A driver must obey road-traffic rules and may be fined for prohibited maneuvers, an unlawful U-turn, specified conduct connected with a traffic accident, or other listed violations. Penalties may apply when a driver causes an accident or operates a vehicle exceeding the road’s permitted load limit, including the specified case of exceeding it by more than 10% and up to 20%. The rules also specify where a driver may stop or park. During an inspection, the driver may be required to present relevant personal and vehicle documents; failure to do so may result in an administrative violation or penalty. In the described case, that penalty may be avoided by presenting the documents, or qualifying electronic document information, within the stated period.

Drivers must switch off high beams and use low beams in specified circumstances, including when encountering a pedestrian crossing the road. In a road tunnel, if a technical failure or force majeure requires a stop, the driver must move the vehicle to an emergency stopping position. If that is not possible, the driver must activate hazard lights, place a warning sign or light behind the vehicle at a safe distance, and promptly report the situation. When a traffic accident occurs, the driver has specified responsibilities; provisions may also require testing the driver’s blood for alcohol, drugs, or other stimulants.

A driver transporting goods by automobile must follow Article 49 safety rules, including arranging and securing goods neatly and safely and signaling when a load extends beyond the vehicle’s front or rear. A driver of a contract-based passenger transport vehicle must comply with electronic-contract and passenger-list requirements. When driving a car, the driver must follow child passenger-seating and safety-equipment requirements, subject to stated exceptions, and is responsible for the described seating violations. Passengers are required to follow the driver’s instructions concerning traffic order and safety.

The term also appears in rules concerning motorcycle and moped drivers, drivers of specialized vehicles, and the placement of priority signal lights—which is defined from the driver’s perspective, with red on the left and blue on the right. Specified records may include a driver’s name, licence number, driving-time information, image, and vehicle-journey information.

A **DRIVER TESTING CENTER** is an organization or unit that provides driving-test services and may serve as a venue for driver examinations. It must meet conditions prescribed by the Government, comply with national technical standards, and use information-technology equipment. It is also required to promptly share test results and monitoring data with the relevant authorities. Under the cited decree, a center may be fined for specified violations.

Centers that conduct driving tests. The text identifies failure to install the required surveillance cameras, or failure to keep installed cameras operating as required, as violations subject to a VND 20 million to VND 30 million fine.

**Driver training** is the regulated instruction of people seeking to obtain a new driver’s licence or upgrade an existing one. Learners complete training through a driver-training establishment or another permitted training method, following the curriculum for the relevant licence class. The curriculum is one of the criteria that the driving test must match.

Training includes theoretical and practical instruction. Practical instruction is subject to requirements concerning where it is conducted and instructor qualifications. A driver-training establishment must provide training at the location specified in its driver-training licence. Training records may include the training category, course dates and practical-driving distance. The rules also address prescribed training formats and content, safe-driving periods, and standards for motorcycle driver-training facilities.

Article 60 of Law 36/2024/QH15 governs driver education and related requirements, including specialized training for military and police personnel performing specified duties. Training completed before that law takes effect, or still in progress on its effective date, is also recognized as a relevant circumstance under the applicable provisions.

Article 39 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP addresses violations of regulations governing driver training and driving tests, including violations by driver-training institutions. Driver training is therefore both a required pathway for learners seeking licensing and a regulated activity subject to institutional, instructional and enforcement requirements.
A facility responsible for providing training and issuing certificates related to road-traffic legal-knowledge training.

A **DRIVER TRAINING COURSE** is a course recorded by its identifier and name. Its record may include the training period, including opening and closing dates, the practical training distance, the completion result, and the time the course was completed.

A **DRIVER TRAINING ESTABLISHMENT** is a driving school or other facility that provides driver training. Under Article 39 of the cited decree, it may be penalized for violations of driver-training regulations, including training drivers at a location not listed on its driver-training license (Clause 4), failing to retain required records or keeping incomplete records for two or more training courses, and improperly recognizing a learner’s completion of a course or issuing a primary-level or training certificate. The latter violation may incur a fine of 20,000,000 to 30,000,000 Vietnamese dong under Clause 5. The establishment’s identifier and name are also recorded in the relevant database.

**Driver Training Establishments** are driving schools and other organizations that train learner drivers to obtain a new driver’s license or upgrade an existing one. They are among the organizations covered by Clause 2 of Article 2 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP and must operate within the student-enrollment and training capacity specified in their permits.

Under Article 39 of the Decree and related provisions, establishments may be penalized for specified violations, including enrolling students who do not meet required education or safe-driving experience criteria, accepting incomplete application documents, failing to follow prescribed training content, programs, or curricula, breaching training or testing regulations, and violating relevant contract requirements. They may also be fined for interfering with monitoring equipment or falsifying records of theoretical study time or practical driving instruction time and distance.

Penalties depend on the violation and may include fines of VND 3 million to VND 5 million for specified contract-related violations, VND 10 million to VND 20 million for other specified violations, and VND 20 million to VND 30 million for violations identified under Clause 5. An establishment may also be suspended from enrolling students for two to four months for specified violations.

DRIVER TRAINING FACILITIES are driving schools and other organizations that provide driver training. Under Article 39 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, they may be fined VND 10,000,000–20,000,000 for specified violations under Clause 4, or VND 20,000,000–30,000,000 for specified violations under Clause 5. The applicable fine depends on the violation.

A **DRIVER TRAINING FACILITY** is a driving school or other establishment that provides driver training. The decree includes the facility among the information recorded in its database. It violates training regulations if it does not have enough practical driving instructors for the planned use of its training vehicles, and it may be fined 20,000,000 to 30,000,000 Vietnamese đồng for specified violations.

The DRIVER’S LICENSE HOLDER is a person who holds a driver’s license and is eligible, subject to the stated conditions, to exchange it or obtain a reissued license. The holder’s license points have been restored to 12, and the holder is to be informed of that restoration.

DRIVER'S LICENSE ISSUANCE is the act of issuing a driver’s license. It is listed in a provision’s heading alongside license exchange, reissuance, and revocation. A license may be subject to revocation if it was issued contrary to regulations or obtained through deception.

id: driver's license issuance, exchange, reissuance, and revocation
ten: DRIVER'S LICENSE ISSUANCE, EXCHANGE, REISSUANCE, AND REVOCATION
mo_ta: The procedures covered by Article 62 of Law 36/2024/QH15 for issuing, exchanging, reissuing, and revoking driver's licenses.

**DRIVER'S LICENSE POINT DEDUCTION** is an administrative traffic-penalty measure under Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. It deducts points from a driver’s license when the driver commits a violation for which point deduction is prescribed, in addition to any other applicable penalty. The decree addresses the measure across provisions covering various violations and vehicle types, including motorcycles and similar vehicles, cars, goods-transport vehicles, vehicle-condition violations, and illegal racing. Many cited article headings identify point deduction as a possible sanction without specifying the number of points for the particular violation. One stated example is a two-point deduction for conduct specified in Clauses 3 or 4 of Article 17.

Article 50 sets out the procedure: an authorized sanctioning person deducts the prescribed points from the relevant part of an integrated driver’s license. The applicable part is the non-expiring license category for motorcycles and similar vehicles, or the time-limited category for cars and specified four-wheel passenger or cargo vehicles. If the driver has fewer remaining points than the amount to be deducted, all remaining points are deducted. The most recent deduction begins the 12-month period used to determine eligibility for automatic point restoration.

Point deduction is not applied when the same case also involves a violation subject to withdrawal of the right to use the license.

**Driver’s License Point Restoration** is governed by Article 51 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. If a driver’s license has not had all its points deducted and no points have been deducted for 12 months since the most recent deduction, its point balance is automatically restored to 12. This rule also applies while the license is subject to suspension of usage rights.

When all points have been deducted, restoration is handled under Article 51(3). Once the license’s point data has been restored to 12, the person authorized under Article 51(1)(b) informs the license holder.
DRIVER'S LICENSE REISSUANCE is the act of issuing a driver’s license again. Deception used to obtain a reissued license is grounds for revocation.

DRIVER’S LICENSE REVOCATION is the legally specified action under Clause 5, Article 62 of Law 36/2024/QH15. A driver’s license is revoked if it was issued contrary to regulations or if its holder used deception to obtain, exchange, or have it reissued.
A period during which the holder's right to use a driver's license is suspended. The text states that a license under such suspension may still have its points automatically restored.

**DRIVER’S-LICENSE POINT DEDUCTION** is a penalty measure under which points may be deducted from a driver’s license for specified road-traffic violations. The descriptions associate it with provisions concerning vehicle-condition violations under Article 13, dangerous-goods transportation violations by vehicle operators under Article 23, and specified violations by vehicle owners under Article 32 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. Article 21 also references point deduction for vehicle operators, and the measure applies to the described illegal racing-related conduct.

The references do not establish that every violation covered by these provisions results in a deduction. In particular, although Article 13’s heading identifies point deduction as a possible penalty, clause 4 does not specify a deduction for the particular violation it describes.

**DRIVER-IMAGE RECORDING DEVICE VIOLATIONS** are breaches of the rules governing the installation and use of devices that record images of vehicle drivers, as addressed in Article 29 and corresponding provisions of Article 32. They include operating a commercial transport vehicle, tractor unit, or internal transport vehicle without a required device; participating in traffic with a device that is not functioning; and falsifying the device’s recorded data.

DRIVER-IMAGE RECORDING EQUIPMENT VIOLATION is a road-traffic violation involving the operation of a passenger car with at least eight passenger seats, excluding the driver’s seat, for passenger transport when the vehicle lacks required equipment for recording images of the driver, the equipment does not properly record or store data, or data from the equipment has been altered or falsified.
A violation involving operation of a road traffic rescue vehicle without a functioning device that records images of the driver, or altering data recorded by such a device.

A violation involving a passenger-transport or internal-transport vehicle that lacks a required driver-image recording device, has one that does not function while the vehicle is in traffic, or has falsified device data.
The examination and issuance of driver licenses, governed by regulations of the Minister of Public Security.

mo_ta: The effective date under Law 36/2024/QH15 for requirements to install image-recording equipment for drivers of specified passenger vehicles with fewer than eight passenger seats, goods transport vehicles other than tractor trucks, and internal transport vehicles.

A general category of organizations that provide driver training. Under the decree, a facility may be fined for using a training vehicle without a rain-and-sun canopy or without a securely attached seat in the vehicle bed for learners.
People receiving driver training whose theoretical study time and practical driving time and distance are required to be monitored.

A violation occurs if a driving training establishment fails to seat an instructor beside a learner during practical driving or assigns an instructor who does not meet the required standards.

**Drivers** are people who operate vehicles on roads and are subject to the road-traffic rules and any applicable training, guidance, health, and administrative requirements. They must comply with speed limits and safe-distance rules, including the requirements in Article 12, and wear seat belts when driving cars fitted with them. On expressways, they must follow Article 25 of Law No. 36/2024/QH15. Drivers of two- or three-wheeled motorcycles or motorbikes must wear helmets that meet national technical standards and fasten them correctly, as required by Article 33.

Drivers conducting passenger transport must follow the applicable rules and, where required, hold an identification card and carry a transport order or other transport document. Before departure, they must check the vehicle’s safety condition and inform passengers about road safety and emergency evacuation. Passenger-transport drivers may also be required to coordinate with police agencies in duties supporting national security and public order.

Drivers transporting preschool children or students must receive instruction in the required safety procedures for picking up and dropping off those passengers. Educational institutions and transport operators have responsibilities relating to providing or ensuring this instruction.

Depending on the applicable provisions, drivers may be subject to professional training or guidance, periodic health examinations, and experience requirements, including those described in Article 26, clause 7. Their health information may be held in the driver health database or the database covering drivers and specialized motorcycle operators; the Ministry of Health is responsible for building and managing the relevant database.
A category of vehicle drivers subject to the penalties and driving-license point deductions described in Article 17.

id: drivers of automobiles and similar vehicles
ten: DRIVERS OF AUTOMOBILES AND SIMILAR VEHICLES
mo_ta: The drivers subject to the provisions in Article 38, including drivers of automobiles and vehicles similar to automobiles registered to operate in the specified economic zones.

id: drivers of cars and similar vehicles
ten: DRIVERS OF CARS AND SIMILAR VEHICLES
mo_ta: Drivers of Cars and Similar Vehicles are people who operate cars, motorized four-wheeled passenger or cargo vehicles, and vehicles similar to cars that are registered to operate in the specified economic zones. Article 38 addresses this category and establishes penalties and driving-license point deductions for traffic violations.

People who operate commercial vehicles transporting preschool children or students, including vehicles used for student pickup and drop-off. The text makes these drivers subject to the stated penalties for safety violations.
Drivers transporting preschool children or students in commercial vehicles, including vehicles used for transport combined with picking up or dropping off children and students.

id: drivers of environmental sanitation vehicles and waste-carrying cars
ten: DRIVERS OF ENVIRONMENTAL SANITATION VEHICLES AND WASTE-CARRYING CARS
mo_ta: The drivers subject to Article 25 when they violate regulations governing transport activities in urban areas.

id: drivers of motorcycles, mopeds, and similar vehicles
ten: DRIVERS OF MOTORCYCLES, MOPEDS, AND SIMILAR VEHICLES
mo_ta: The drivers addressed by Article 14, who may be subject to penalties, driving-license point deductions, and remedial measures for violating vehicle-condition rules while participating in traffic

Drivers of passenger-carrying vehicles are the people covered by Article 20, including drivers of passenger cars and similar vehicles carrying passengers. They may be penalized under that article for the specified violations.
Drivers of passenger-transport vehicles, who are responsible for guiding, requiring, and checking that people aboard comply with the cited rules
Drivers of cars and similar vehicles registered for operation in special economic-trade zones or international border-gate economic zones, to whom the penalties described in Article 38 apply.

id: drivers of road motor vehicles bearing foreign registration plates
ten: DRIVERS OF ROAD MOTOR VEHICLES BEARING FOREIGN REGISTRATION PLATES
mo_ta: The category of vehicle operators addressed by Article 37 of the decree and subject to its penalties for the specified violations.
A category of vehicle drivers subject to the penalties and driving-license point deductions described in Article 17.

id: drivers of vehicles similar to automobiles
ten: DRIVERS OF VEHICLES SIMILAR TO AUTOMOBILES
mo_ta: Drivers of vehicle types similar to automobiles who are subject to the penalties and driving-license point deductions described in Article 17.

id: drivers whose licence points have all been deducted
ten: DRIVERS WHOSE LICENCE POINTS HAVE ALL BEEN DEDUCTED
mo_ta: A category of people whose driving licences have had all their points deducted; they are eligible to participate in the road traffic law knowledge test.
The exchange of a driver’s licence, for which the decree lists the date and responsible authority.
The issuance of a driver’s licence, for which the decree lists the date, issuing authority, licence category, and validity period.
The authority responsible for issuing, exchanging, or reissuing driving licences; it must check relevant vehicle-violation and violator data before performing those procedures.
The reissuance of a driver’s licence, for which the decree lists the date and responsible authority.
The event in which a driving license becomes damaged and can no longer be used.
The administrative action of exchanging or reissuing a driving license, which is permitted when the license is damaged and no longer usable.

DRIVER’S LICENSE ISSUANCE is the administrative process of granting a driving license. The process may include a theoretical examination using questions to assess an applicant’s knowledge of road traffic law. The term appears alongside the related administrative actions of exchanging, reissuing, and revoking licenses.

id: driver’s license issuance, exchange, or reissuance
ten: DRIVER’S LICENSE ISSUANCE, EXCHANGE, OR REISSUANCE
mo_ta: The process of issuing, exchanging, or reissuing a driver’s license; it is not carried out for a violator identified in the relevant data lookup.
The agency responsible for managing driver’s licenses; it receives examination results when data are not connected and shared.

**DRIVER’S LICENSE POINT DEDUCTION** is an administrative traffic-penalty measure under Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. It involves an authorized official deducting points from a driver’s license when the holder commits a violation covered by the relevant provisions. Depending on the provision, the deduction may apply alongside a monetary fine or other penalties.

The measure is addressed across several articles, including Articles 6, 7, 12, 13, 20, 21, 30, and 32, and in provisions concerning particular vehicle types and operators. Covered cases include specified road-traffic and vehicle-condition violations, as well as violations by drivers of passenger-transport vehicles, cargo trucks, tractors, ambulances, and certain motorized four-wheel vehicles. Article 32 also addresses deductions from the license of a vehicle owner who commits a relevant violation. The exact scope and consequence depend on the applicable provision; some cited excerpts provide only a monetary fine or refer to point deduction in a heading without specifying the deduction.

One stated example appears in Clause 14 of Article 26: a transport-business individual who directly drives a vehicle and commits specified violations has two points deducted, in addition to other applicable penalties. The measure may involve recording the license holder’s details, license information, the points before and after deduction, and relevant timing.

The cited material does not establish a point deduction for every violation mentioned. In particular, it does not specify one for the cited horn or seat-belt violations.

id: driver’s license point deduction under article 7
ten: DRIVER’S LICENSE POINT DEDUCTION UNDER ARTICLE 7
