mo_ta: The deduction of points from a driver’s license, referenced in Article 7’s title as part of the penalties for covered road-traffic violations.

DRIVER’S LICENSE POINT RESTORATION is the process of restoring points to a driver’s license after all points have been deducted. It requires passing a road-traffic legal-knowledge test, and the time at which restoration occurs is recorded.

The formal notification to a citizen that points have been deducted from their driver’s license. It may be delivered in writing, by post, or electronically through the citizen’s registered account on the public service portal or mobile traffic application.

The recording of a deducted-points status for a driver’s license, including an update to the electronic identity card and electronic identification account when the license is represented as a data message.
The administrative action of revoking a driving license, included in the provision’s title alongside issuing, exchanging, and reissuing licenses.
The process of testing and issuing driver’s licenses under regulations of the Minister of Public Security
Training for drivers seeking to upgrade their driving license, including from class D1 to class D2 or class D

**DRIVER’S-LICENSE POINT DEDUCTION** is an administrative penalty addressed in the decree’s title and in Articles 7, 14, 20, 21, 23, and 32. It involves deducting points from a driver’s license for covered road-traffic violations. The provisions concern violations by drivers or operators—including those operating motorcycles, mopeds, similar vehicles, and goods-transport vehicles—and Article 32 addresses covered violations by vehicle owners. The number of points deducted is not specified in the descriptions.
The restoration of points on a driver’s license after the candidate passes the required legal-knowledge test.

A legal-knowledge test on road traffic order and safety that a driver takes to qualify for restoration of driver’s-license points. It is generally a computer-based multiple-choice test, with duration, questions, and passing score corresponding to the relevant driver’s-license class; an unsuccessful candidate may retake it after seven working days.

**DRIVER’S-LICENSE REQUIREMENT VIOLATIONS** include driving a car or specified four-wheeled motor vehicle without a valid, appropriate license. This covers driving without a license; using one that is unsuitable for the vehicle, has no points remaining, was not issued by a competent authority, has been erased or is otherwise no longer valid; and using a license that has been expired for at least one year.

id: driving 10–20 km/h over the speed limit
ten: DRIVING 10–20 KM/H OVER THE SPEED LIMIT
mo_ta: “Driving 10–20 km/h Over the Speed Limit” is a road-traffic violation under Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, involving operation of a vehicle at a speed 10 to 20 km/h above the prescribed limit. The fine depends on the vehicle type: the stated penalty is 4,000,000–6,000,000 Vietnamese đồng for a car, and 800,000–1,000,000 Vietnamese đồng for a motorcycle.

id: driving 20–35 km/h over the speed limit
ten: DRIVING 20–35 KM/H OVER THE SPEED LIMIT
mo_ta: A road traffic violation involving driving a vehicle more than 20 km/h and up to 35 km/h above the prescribed speed limit. Under Clause 6 of Article 6 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, this violation carries a fine of 6,000,000 to 8,000,000 Vietnamese đồng; the article concerns penalties and deduction of driving-license points.

id: driving 5 to less than 10 km/h above the speed limit
ten: DRIVING 5 TO LESS THAN 10 KM/H ABOVE THE SPEED LIMIT
mo_ta: A road traffic violation committed by driving a vehicle 5 km/h to less than 10 km/h faster than the prescribed speed limit.

id: driving 5–10 km/h above the speed limit
ten: DRIVING 5–10 KM/H ABOVE THE SPEED LIMIT
mo_ta: A road traffic violation committed by a driver operating a car or a similar vehicle at least 5 km/h but less than 10 km/h above the prescribed speed limit.

id: driving a car without an operative horn
ten: DRIVING A CAR WITHOUT AN OPERATIVE HORN
mo_ta: A traffic violation involving driving a car without a horn or with a horn that does not work, punishable under Article 13 by a fine of 400,000 to 600,000 VND.

id: driving a commercial motor vehicle without carrying a driving license
ten: DRIVING A COMMERCIAL MOTOR VEHICLE WITHOUT CARRYING A DRIVING LICENSE
mo_ta: A traffic violation described in Article 18(3) of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP: operating a car, a motorized four-wheel passenger vehicle, a motorized four-wheel goods vehicle, or a similar vehicle used for commercial transport without carrying a driving license. The stated fine is 300,000 to 400,000 Vietnamese đồng, except for the conduct specified in Article 18(8)(c).

id: driving a four-wheeled motor vehicle on an expressway
ten: DRIVING A FOUR-WHEELED MOTOR VEHICLE ON AN EXPRESSWAY
mo_ta: A traffic violation under Decree 168/2024/ND-CP, Article 6, involving a driver taking a four-wheeled motorized passenger vehicle or cargo vehicle onto an expressway. The stated fine is 12,000,000 to 14,000,000 Vietnamese dong.

id: driving a goods-transport vehicle without a required valid badge
ten: DRIVING A GOODS-TRANSPORT VEHICLE WITHOUT A REQUIRED VALID BADGE
mo_ta: A violation described in Article 21: operating a vehicle that is required to display a badge without one, with an expired badge, or with a badge not issued by a competent authority. The stated fine is 5,000,000 to 7,000,000 Vietnamese đồng.

id: driving a passenger vehicle without the required passenger list
ten: DRIVING A PASSENGER VEHICLE WITHOUT THE REQUIRED PASSENGER LIST
mo_ta: A traffic violation consisting of driving a passenger vehicle without the passenger list required by regulations. The cited provision specifies a fine of 1,000,000 to 2,000,000 Vietnamese dong for this violation.

id: driving a right-hand-drive car without required support
ten: DRIVING A RIGHT-HAND-DRIVE CAR WITHOUT REQUIRED SUPPORT
mo_ta: A traffic violation described in Clause 4 of Article 37: driving a right-hand-drive car in traffic without traveling in a convoy and without the required people or vehicles to provide support and traffic guidance.

id: driving a school-transport vehicle without the required paint color
ten: DRIVING A SCHOOL-TRANSPORT VEHICLE WITHOUT THE REQUIRED PAINT COLOR
mo_ta: A violation in which a driver operates a commercial vehicle transporting preschool children or students without the paint color required by regulation.

id: driving a tracked vehicle on a road
ten: DRIVING A TRACKED VEHICLE ON A ROAD
mo_ta: “DRIVING A TRACKED VEHICLE ON A ROAD” refers to operating or circulating a tracked vehicle on a road, conduct addressed by the provision’s heading and Article 34. The article also includes passenger cars within its scope.

id: driving a truck with non-compliant cargo-body dimensions
ten: DRIVING A TRUCK WITH NON-COMPLIANT CARGO-BODY DIMENSIONS
mo_ta: A traffic violation involving driving a truck, including one towing a trailer or semi-trailer, whose cargo-body dimensions do not match the technical specifications recorded in its inspection certificate for technical safety and environmental protection. The stated fine is 2,000,000 to 3,000,000 VND.

id: driving a vehicle exceeding weight or dimension limits
ten: DRIVING A VEHICLE EXCEEDING WEIGHT OR DIMENSION LIMITS
mo_ta: The operation on public roads of a vehicle exceeding prescribed weight or dimension limits, including an overloaded vehicle or a tracked vehicle.

id: driving a vehicle on a sidewalk
ten: DRIVING A VEHICLE ON A SIDEWALK
mo_ta: A road traffic violation involving driving a vehicle on a sidewalk, except when crossing the sidewalk to enter a home or agency. The cited provision sets a fine of 6,000,000 to 8,000,000 Vietnamese dong for this conduct.

id: driving a vehicle that exceeds permitted road weight limits by more than 50%
ten: DRIVING A VEHICLE THAT EXCEEDS PERMITTED ROAD WEIGHT LIMITS BY MORE THAN 50%
mo_ta: A road-traffic violation involving a vehicle whose total weight or axle load, including cargo and passengers, exceeds the road's permitted load by more than 50%. Under Clause 5 of Article 34 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, it is punishable by a fine of 40,000,000 to 50,000,000 Vietnamese đồng, except when the vehicle has a valid circulation permit.

id: driving a vehicle with an expired inspection certificate
ten: DRIVING A VEHICLE WITH AN EXPIRED INSPECTION CERTIFICATE
mo_ta: A road traffic violation involving a motor vehicle or specialized motor vehicle whose required technical safety and environmental protection inspection certificate or sticker has expired by less than one month. Under Article 32, paragraph 9, the stated fines are 4,000,000–6,000,000 VND for individuals and 8,000,000–12,000,000 VND for organizations.

id: driving a vehicle with insufficient or noncompliant tires
ten: DRIVING A VEHICLE WITH INSUFFICIENT OR NONCOMPLIANT TIRES
mo_ta: A traffic violation involving driving a covered vehicle without all required tires, with tires of an incorrect size, or with tires that fail technical standards. The rule also applies to trailers and semi-trailers.

id: driving a vehicle with noncompliant equipment in traffic
ten: DRIVING A VEHICLE WITH NONCOMPLIANT EQUIPMENT IN TRAFFIC
mo_ta: Operating a motorcycle, moped, or similar vehicle in traffic when it fails to meet the required vehicle-equipment conditions.

id: driving a vehicle without a required license plate
ten: DRIVING A VEHICLE WITHOUT A REQUIRED LICENSE PLATE
mo_ta: A traffic violation described in Article 13: driving a car, trailer, or semi-trailer without a license plate when that vehicle is required to have one. The specified fine is 10,000,000 to 12,000,000 Vietnamese dong.

id: driving a vehicle without an effective windshield
ten: DRIVING A VEHICLE WITHOUT AN EFFECTIVE WINDSHIELD
mo_ta: A vehicle-condition violation involving driving a vehicle without a windshield, or with a broken windshield that does not function, when the vehicle is designed to have one. The text sets a fine of 200,000 to 400,000 Vietnamese dong for this violation.

id: driving against prohibited or one-way traffic
ten: DRIVING AGAINST PROHIBITED OR ONE-WAY TRAFFIC
mo_ta: Entering a road marked as prohibited for the vehicle, or driving against the direction of a one-way road or a road marked “No Entry in This Direction,” and causing a traffic accident.

id: driving against the direction of traffic
ten: DRIVING AGAINST THE DIRECTION OF TRAFFIC
mo_ta: A road-traffic violation involving driving against the direction of a one-way street or on a road marked as prohibiting travel in that direction. The text excludes certain priority vehicles performing emergency duties.

id: driving against traffic on an expressway
ten: DRIVING AGAINST TRAFFIC ON AN EXPRESSWAY
mo_ta: **DRIVING AGAINST TRAFFIC ON AN EXPRESSWAY** is a road traffic violation in which a driver travels against the direction of traffic on an expressway. The descriptions cite different fines: 18,000,000–20,000,000 Vietnamese đồng and 30,000,000–40,000,000 Vietnamese đồng. These amounts cannot be reconciled without knowing which decree or version applies; the 30,000,000–40,000,000 đồng range is stated to exclude priority vehicles performing emergency duties as prescribed.

id: driving an overloaded vehicle on a road
ten: DRIVING AN OVERLOADED VEHICLE ON A ROAD
mo_ta: A road-traffic violation covered by the provision’s heading, involving a driver operating a vehicle whose load exceeds the permitted weight.

id: driving below the minimum permitted speed
ten: DRIVING BELOW THE MINIMUM PERMITTED SPEED
mo_ta: A road traffic violation in which a driver operates a vehicle below the minimum speed on a road section where a minimum speed is prescribed. Article 8, clause 3 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP provides for a fine of 800,000 to 1,000,000 Vietnamese dong for this violation.

“DRIVING BELOW THE MINIMUM SPEED” is a road-traffic violation in which a driver operates a vehicle below the minimum speed prescribed for a road section. The stated fine for the driver is 800,000 to 1,000,000 Vietnamese đồng.

id: driving below the speed of other traffic without using the right lane
ten: DRIVING BELOW THE SPEED OF OTHER TRAFFIC WITHOUT USING THE RIGHT LANE
mo_ta: A road traffic violation committed by driving slower than other vehicles traveling in the same direction without moving into the right-hand lane, except when those other vehicles are exceeding the speed limit.

id: driving beyond temporary registration or operating limits
ten: DRIVING BEYOND TEMPORARY REGISTRATION OR OPERATING LIMITS
mo_ta: A traffic violation involving driving a temporarily registered vehicle, or operating a vehicle with restricted activity beyond its permitted area, route, or time. Under Article 13, Clause 7 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, this violation is punishable by a fine of 10,000,000 to 12,000,000 Vietnamese đồng.
A violation in which a driver of a commercial transport car drives longer than the time permitted under Clause 1 of Article 64 of the Road Traffic Order and Safety Law.

The **DRIVING EXAMINATION** is an assessment conducted by qualified examiners who must meet the required standards, hold an examiner card, and take responsibility for their examination results. The process includes theory examinations and traffic-situation simulations. During the examination, specified monitoring images and examination results must be displayed publicly on functioning screens.

Conduct by a driving-test candidate that can distort examination results, including bringing a mobile phone or image- or audio-capable telecommunications device into a theory-test room, a traffic-situation simulation test, or a test vehicle, or engaging in other deceptive conduct
A driving examiner conducts driving examinations, must meet the required conditions and standards, hold an examiner card, and is responsible for the examination results.
The process of issuing cards to qualified driving examiners, governed by requirements prescribed by the Minister of Public Security.
Training for driving examiners, which is among the matters governed by requirements prescribed by the Minister of Public Security.
People who conduct driving examinations and are subject to prescribed eligibility and qualification standards; they may receive training and be issued examiner cards.
Driving on roads in rain, fog, slippery or winding terrain, on steep slopes, or with limited visibility; drivers are required to increase the safe distance between vehicles in these conditions.

id: driving in an expressway emergency stopping lane or on its shoulder
ten: DRIVING IN AN EXPRESSWAY EMERGENCY STOPPING LANE OR ON ITS SHOULDER
mo_ta: A road-traffic violation consisting of driving in an expressway emergency stopping lane or on the expressway shoulder.

id: driving in an expressway emergency stopping lane or shoulder
ten: DRIVING IN AN EXPRESSWAY EMERGENCY STOPPING LANE OR SHOULDER
mo_ta: A traffic violation involving driving in an expressway emergency stopping lane or on its shoulder.

id: driving in an incorrect roadway or lane
ten: DRIVING IN AN INCORRECT ROADWAY OR LANE
mo_ta: “DRIVING IN AN INCORRECT ROADWAY OR LANE” is a road-traffic violation described in Article 8, Clause 6. It involves driving outside the prescribed roadway or lane, including a lane used for either the same or the opposite direction of travel, subject to any stated exception.

id: driving in the wrong roadway section or lane
ten: DRIVING IN THE WRONG ROADWAY SECTION OR LANE
mo_ta: A road traffic violation in which a motorcycle, moped, or similar vehicle is driven outside its prescribed section or lane, including in a lane for traffic traveling in the opposite direction.

A **DRIVING INSTRUCTOR** is a person who teaches practical driving and supervises learners. The instructor is required to meet applicable teaching standards and may sit beside a learner to supervise their steering. Practical driving instructors may also be subject to penalties for certain violations.
A certificate for a driving instructor, which may be issued, reissued, or revoked under rules set by the Government

A violation in which a driving instructor lacks the lesson plan for an assigned subject or uses a lesson plan that does not match that subject; the text specifies a fine of 2,000,000 to 3,000,000 Vietnamese dong.
Standards for driving instructors that the Government is tasked with specifying

Driving instructors are people who teach car driving and supervise learners or candidates during practical participation in road traffic. Practical instructors must follow the authorized training route and sit beside learners to assist them during driving practice. They are required to carry the documents specified in Article 56(1) and comply with applicable badge requirements. Under the cited provisions, Article 39, Clause 1 prescribes fines for certain violations by driving instructors, including teaching without wearing the required instructor badge or allowing a learner to practise without the required learner-driver badge.

A driving learner is a person practicing to drive under an instructor’s guidance. The instructor sits beside the learner and supervises their steering. The learner is described as committing a violation while practicing.
People who were trained to drive before Law 36/2024/QH15 takes effect, or are undergoing driver training on its effective date, and have not yet taken the driving test or received a driving license.
A person who has been issued a driving licence and whose licence may be revoked if they do not meet the health requirements for its class.

id: driving licence issuance, exchange, reissuance, and revocation
ten: DRIVING LICENCE ISSUANCE, EXCHANGE, REISSUANCE, AND REVOCATION
mo_ta: The legal procedures addressed by Article 62, including issuing, exchanging, reissuing, and revoking driving licences.

**DRIVING LICENCE POINT DEDUCTION** is an administrative penalty measure under Decree 168/2024/ND-CP (also cited as Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP). It applies to vehicle operators who commit violations covered by the Decree and involves deducting points from their driving licence. The deduction is carried out immediately after the related administrative penalty decision takes effect. The measure is referenced in the headings of Articles 12 and 21, while Article 50 addresses the deduction process. The descriptions provided do not specify how many points are deducted for any particular violation.
The principles governing the deduction of points from driving licences, referenced in the heading and text of Article 50
The restoration of points on a participant’s driving licence after they pass the legal knowledge test.
Training for people seeking to upgrade a driving licence from class C to class D1, D2, or D.
The issuance, exchange, or reissuance of a driving license, which may proceed according to the rules after the violation has been resolved and the relevant authority has been notified.
The procedures described in Article 62 for issuing, exchanging, reissuing, and revoking driving licenses.
The process of exchanging a driving license, one of the matters addressed in Article 62 of Law 36/2024/QH15.

**DRIVING LICENSE ISSUANCE** is the process by which the responsible driver training, examination, testing, and licensing authority grants a driving license to eligible learners. The license category granted is determined under the category rules specified in Clause 3 of Article 89. Driving license issuance is also one of the matters addressed in Article 62 of Law No. 36/2024/QH15.

id: driving license issuance, exchange, reissuance, and revocation
ten: DRIVING LICENSE ISSUANCE, EXCHANGE, REISSUANCE, AND REVOCATION
mo_ta: The administrative processes covered by Article 62 of Law 36/2024/QH15: issuing, exchanging, reissuing, and revoking driving licenses.
The agency responsible for issuing, exchanging, or reissuing driving licenses, which receives notice from the competent sanctioning official after the violation case is resolved.

**DRIVING LICENSE POINT DEDUCTION** is a traffic penalty involving the removal of points from a driver’s license for specified road traffic violations under Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. The consequence is referenced in the headings of Articles 7, 12, and 14. Article 35 also specifies point deduction as a penalty for people who illegally race, organize illegal races, or incite or cheer illegal racing.

Under the stated principle, points are not deducted while a license is suspended or from an international driving license.

DRIVING LICENSE POINT RESTORATION is the procedure for restoring points on a driving license under Article 51 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. Restoration occurs after the license holder passes the required test.
A test whose content, method, timing, and structure are specified in Article 6 of Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA. Passing the test restores points on a driving license.
The situation in which all points have been deducted from a driving license, for which the restoration procedure applies.
The process of reissuing a driving license, one of the matters addressed in Article 62 of Law 36/2024/QH15.
The process of revoking a driving license, one of the matters addressed in Article 62 of Law 36/2024/QH15.
A period during which the right to use a driving license is suspended; under the stated rule, points are not deducted from a license during this period.
The examination process for issuing driving licenses, including its form, content, and procedures.

id: driving more than 35 km/h above the speed limit
ten: DRIVING MORE THAN 35 KM/H ABOVE THE SPEED LIMIT
mo_ta: A road-traffic violation described in the decree; the text states that a driver committing it is subject to a fine of 12,000,000 to 14,000,000 Vietnamese dong.

id: driving on a road section reserved for pedestrians and other vehicles
ten: DRIVING ON A ROAD SECTION RESERVED FOR PEDESTRIANS AND OTHER VEHICLES
mo_ta: The prohibited act of driving a motorcycle or moped onto a section of road designated for pedestrians and other vehicles
A road-traffic violation involving driving a vehicle on a sidewalk, except when crossing the sidewalk to enter a house or agency.

id: driving on the wrong side of the road
ten: DRIVING ON THE WRONG SIDE OF THE ROAD
mo_ta: **DRIVING ON THE WRONG SIDE OF THE ROAD** is a road traffic violation in which a person drives without keeping to the right-hand side in the direction of travel. It applies to motorcycles, mopeds, and similar vehicles.

**DRIVING ONTO AN EXPRESSWAY** is a road-traffic violation under Article 7 involving driving a covered vehicle onto an expressway. The prohibition does not apply to vehicles used to manage or maintain the expressway. The stated fine is 4,000,000 to 6,000,000 Vietnamese đồng.

A road-traffic violation in which a driver operates a vehicle with a still-valid circulation permit on a route different from the one specified in that permit. Under Article 34 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP, this violation is subject to a fine of 13,000,000 to 15,000,000 Vietnamese dong.

id: driving oversized or overweight cargo off the permitted route
ten: DRIVING OVERSIZED OR OVERWEIGHT CARGO OFF THE PERMITTED ROUTE
mo_ta: A violation in which a vehicle carries oversized or overweight cargo with a valid circulation permit but travels on a route other than the one specified in that permit.
The activity of people practicing driving in a training vehicle, identified as a permitted circumstance for carrying them in a cargo truck bed.

DRIVING PRACTICE YARD is an area where learner drivers can practice driving exercises under an instructor’s supervision. It may also serve as a venue for driver examinations, including motorcycle driving tests, provided it meets the required facility and technical standards.
An additional penalty under which a driver may lose the right to use their driving license for 10 to 12 months for committing the violation specified in Clause 12.

A **DRIVING TEST** is an examination of a person’s driving ability and competence, with required content matched to the relevant driver’s-license class and driver-training curriculum. People who have completed the required training and meet prescribed age and health requirements may register; eligible learners may also take the test under applicable transitional rules. The test is governed by the regulations referenced in Article 39, which include requirements for records for each test session. The testing process is monitored, and its results and monitoring data are shared with the relevant authorities. A person who achieves a satisfactory result is eligible to receive a driver’s license. The regulations also identify transporting people who are taking a driving test in a test vehicle as a permitted circumstance for carrying people in a cargo truck bed.
People taking a driving test; the provision refers to publicly announcing their errors during the practical driving test.

A **DRIVING TEST CENTER** is an organization that conducts driving tests for road motor vehicle drivers. It must maintain the conditions prescribed by the applicable national technical regulation and retain the required records for each test session.

Under the applicable decree, a center may be fined for specified violations, including unauthorized relocation of functional rooms, changes to the test-course layout, allowing scoring equipment to operate inaccurately, permitting unauthorized signs or symbols during a test, or failing to retain—or incompletely retaining—records for two or more test sessions. Depending on the violation and the relevant provision, fines may range from **10,000,000 to 20,000,000 Vietnamese đồng** or **20,000,000 to 30,000,000 Vietnamese đồng**. A driving-test license may also be suspended for **one to three months** for specified violations.

Driving test centers are organizations and facilities that conduct automobile and motorcycle driving examinations. They must hold the required licenses or permits and comply with government-set conditions and procedures for carrying out testing activities. They are among the organizations covered by Clause 2 of Article 2 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP and are subject to the rules and penalties in Article 39, including provisions concerning driver training and testing.

Depending on the violation, a center may be fined:

- **VND 10 million to VND 20 million** for specified violations, including failing to provide enough functioning screens to publicly display required examination-monitoring images and results, and failures involving required monitoring equipment or the public audio announcement system during practical tests.
- **VND 20 million to VND 30 million** for specified violations, including when more than half of the center’s licensed theory-test computers fail to meet required testing conditions, or more than half of its licensed on-road test vehicles in a province fail to meet prescribed conditions.
- **VND 40 million to VND 50 million** for other specified violations under Article 39.

Article 39 also provides for fines under its relevant clauses, including Clause 4 for specified violations and Clause 7 for changing or using testing software, scoring equipment, or test vehicles without approval from the competent state management authority.

DRIVING TEST EXAMINERS are people who conduct car-driving tests and may supervise a vehicle’s steering while learners or candidates participate in road traffic. They must carry the documents specified in Article 56(1). The Minister of Transport prescribes their qualifications and standards, organizes their training, and provides for the issuance of examiner cards.

id: driving test in a test vehicle
ten: DRIVING TEST IN A TEST VEHICLE
mo_ta: The portion of a driving examination conducted in a test vehicle, where candidates are prohibited from bringing mobile phones or image- or audio-capable telecommunications devices
The administrative process of evaluating applications and issuing, reissuing, or revoking licenses for driving test activities.

A supplementary penalty under Article 39 that revokes a driving test center’s right to use its driving test license for two to four months when it commits the violations specified in Point k, Clause 5, or Clause 7.
A person who takes the driving test and, if successful, is eligible to receive a driver's license.

A **DRIVING TEST SESSION** is an occasion on which candidates take driving tests, during which specified equipment or signage violations may occur. Records may refer to two or more sessions; a separate requirement specifies retaining records for one session.

The DRIVING TEST YARD is the designated area where driving tests are conducted. It must have the prescribed surveillance cameras, and unauthorized signs or symbols are prohibited in the yard while a test is in progress.

DRIVING TESTING is the activity of examining people seeking to qualify as drivers, including assessing their driving knowledge or ability. It is regulated alongside driver training under Article 39 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP, which sets out sanctions for violations of the applicable regulations.

**Driving tests** are examinations and assessments used to determine whether people are qualified to operate vehicles, including motorcycles, and to support the issuance of driving licences. They encompass the tests’ forms, content, procedures, and technical arrangements addressed in Article 61 of Law 36/2024/QH15. Article 39 identifies driving-test activities as a regulated area, and related provisions address violations by driving-test centers and the qualification, issuance, renewal, or revocation of permits for those centers. The ministers of National Defense and Public Security may also regulate driver examinations for military and police personnel performing national-defense or security duties.

id: driving tests and driver’s license issuance
ten: DRIVING TESTS AND DRIVER’S LICENSE ISSUANCE
mo_ta: The testing of drivers and issuance of driver’s licenses, covered by a database managed by the Ministry of Public Security.
A theoretical knowledge examination for driver applicants, conducted using licensed computers at driving test centers and subject to the decree’s requirements.

id: driving three or more vehicles side by side
ten: DRIVING THREE OR MORE VEHICLES SIDE BY SIDE
mo_ta: A road-traffic violation described in the decree: operating a vehicle in a side-by-side formation of three or more vehicles. The stated fine is 600,000 to 800,000 Vietnamese đồng.

id: driving through a road tunnel without low-beam headlights
ten: DRIVING THROUGH A ROAD TUNNEL WITHOUT LOW-BEAM HEADLIGHTS
mo_ta: **DRIVING THROUGH A ROAD TUNNEL WITHOUT LOW-BEAM HEADLIGHTS** is a road traffic violation involving a driver who enters or travels through a road tunnel without using low-beam headlights. The stated penalty depends on the vehicle category and applicable provision: one description gives a fine of **800,000–1,000,000 Vietnamese đồng**, while **Article 7, Clause 3 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP** specifies a fine of **600,000–800,000 Vietnamese đồng** for a person operating a motorcycle, moped, or similar vehicle.

id: driving through a road tunnel without using low-beam headlights
ten: DRIVING THROUGH A ROAD TUNNEL WITHOUT USING LOW-BEAM HEADLIGHTS
mo_ta: A road traffic violation described in Article 8: operating a vehicle in a road tunnel without using the required low-beam headlights.

id: driving through an illuminated residential area
ten: DRIVING THROUGH AN ILLUMINATED RESIDENTIAL AREA
mo_ta: Driving along a section of road through a residential area while its lighting system is operating; using high beams in this situation is included among the prohibited conduct.
A course of driver training whose records must be stored by the driving training facility.

A **DRIVING TRAINING ESTABLISHMENT** is a driving school or other facility that provides driver training. It is required to arrange qualified instructors and ensure supervision during practical driving lessons, and it may provide instruction only for driver’s-license classes it is authorized to teach.

Under the applicable requirements, the establishment may be fined for specified violations, including using a practice vehicle without a valid practice-vehicle permit; failing to display the required “Tập lái” (“practice driving”) sign or the establishment’s name and phone number on the vehicle; using a training vehicle without an auxiliary brake or with an ineffective one; or enrolling students in or providing training for an unauthorized license class. For certain specified violations, the fine may range from 10,000,000 to 20,000,000 Vietnamese đồng.

DRIVING TRAINING ESTABLISHMENTS are organizations that provide driver training and are subject to sanctions under Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP for specified violations. Under Article 39, Clause 5, they may be fined VND 20 million to VND 30 million for failing to provide enough practice vehicles to meet actual training demand or for using vehicles of the wrong class for practical instruction.

Organizations that provide driver training. Under the cited provision, they may be fined for failing to have required equipment to monitor students’ theoretical study time and practical driving time and distance, or for having equipment that does not operate as required.
A generic driver-training establishment required to store the records for each training course in accordance with regulations.
Operating a vehicle while blindfolded, an act listed as grounds for vehicle confiscation.

id: driving while under the influence of prohibited substances
ten: DRIVING WHILE UNDER THE INFLUENCE OF PROHIBITED SUBSTANCES
mo_ta: A road-traffic violation consisting of operating a vehicle on a road while the driver has narcotics or another stimulant prohibited by law in their body.

id: driving while using a phone or other electronic device
ten: DRIVING WHILE USING A PHONE OR OTHER ELECTRONIC DEVICE
mo_ta: A driver holding and using a phone or another electronic device while operating a covered type of vehicle, listed as a road-traffic violation subject to the Article 7 fine.
A driver operating a covered type of vehicle while using an umbrella, listed as a road-traffic violation subject to the Article 7 fine.
A driver using an audio device while operating a covered type of vehicle; hearing aids are excluded. This conduct is listed as a road-traffic violation subject to the Article 7 fine.

id: driving with a low alcohol concentration
ten: DRIVING WITH A LOW ALCOHOL CONCENTRATION
mo_ta: A traffic violation described in the decree: operating a vehicle with alcohol in the blood or breath at a concentration not exceeding 50 milligrams per 100 milliliters of blood or 0.25 milligrams per liter of breath.

id: driving with a nonfunctioning image-recording device
ten: DRIVING WITH A NONFUNCTIONING IMAGE-RECORDING DEVICE
mo_ta: A violation consisting of driving a covered vehicle while its driver-image recording device does not work as required during traffic participation.

id: driving with alcohol above the specified threshold
ten: DRIVING WITH ALCOHOL ABOVE THE SPECIFIED THRESHOLD
mo_ta: A traffic violation under Article 6, Clause 11 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP: operating a vehicle with a blood alcohol concentration above 80 milligrams per 100 milliliters of blood or a breath alcohol concentration above 0.4 milligrams per liter. The stated fine is 30,000,000 to 40,000,000 Vietnamese dong.

id: driving with alcohol below the specified threshold
ten: DRIVING WITH ALCOHOL BELOW THE SPECIFIED THRESHOLD
mo_ta: The violation described in the text: driving with alcohol in the blood or breath, at a level not exceeding 50 milligrams per 100 milliliters of blood or 0.25 milligrams per liter of breath.

id: driving with alcohol in the blood or breath
ten: DRIVING WITH ALCOHOL IN THE BLOOD OR BREATH
mo_ta: A road traffic violation described in Article 6, Clause 6: driving on a road with alcohol in the blood or breath, at a concentration not exceeding 50 milligrams per 100 milliliters of blood or 0.25 milligrams per liter of breath.

id: driving with an alcohol concentration above the legal threshold
ten: DRIVING WITH AN ALCOHOL CONCENTRATION ABOVE THE LEGAL THRESHOLD
mo_ta: A road traffic violation described in Article 8, Clause 9 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP: operating a vehicle with blood alcohol above 80 milligrams per 100 milliliters or breath alcohol above 0.4 milligrams per liter.

id: driving with an alcohol concentration above the specified limit
ten: DRIVING WITH AN ALCOHOL CONCENTRATION ABOVE THE SPECIFIED LIMIT
mo_ta: A road traffic violation involving driving a vehicle while the driver’s blood alcohol concentration exceeds 50 mg and is up to 80 mg per 100 ml of blood, or the breath alcohol concentration exceeds 0.25 mg and is up to 0.4 mg per liter of breath. The stated fine is 18,000,000 to 20,000,000 Vietnamese dong.

id: driving with an expired inspection certificate or sticker
ten: DRIVING WITH AN EXPIRED INSPECTION CERTIFICATE OR STICKER
mo_ta: A traffic violation involving driving a specialized motorcycle or towed trailer with a technical safety and environmental protection inspection certificate or sticker that expired less than one month earlier.
Operating a vehicle while letting go of both hands, an act listed as grounds for vehicle confiscation.

**DRIVING WITH EXCESSIVE ALCOHOL CONCENTRATION** is a road-traffic violation under Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP involving operation of a vehicle when the driver’s blood alcohol concentration exceeds 80 milligrams per 100 milliliters of blood or their breath alcohol concentration exceeds 0.4 milligrams per liter of breath. The penalty depends on the vehicle: Article 9, Clause 4 sets a fine of 400,000 to 600,000 Vietnamese đồng for operating a bicycle, motorized bicycle, or other rudimentary vehicle, while Article 7, Clause 9 sets a fine of 8,000,000 to 10,000,000 Vietnamese đồng for operating a motorcycle, moped, or similar vehicle on a road.

id: driving with prohibited drugs or stimulants in the body
ten: DRIVING WITH PROHIBITED DRUGS OR STIMULANTS IN THE BODY
mo_ta: A road traffic violation described in Article 8, Clause 9 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP: operating a vehicle on a road while having narcotic substances or other stimulants prohibited by law in the body. The stated fine is 18,000,000 to 20,000,000 Vietnamese đồng.

id: driving with prohibited narcotics or stimulants in the body
ten: DRIVING WITH PROHIBITED NARCOTICS OR STIMULANTS IN THE BODY
mo_ta: A road traffic violation described as driving while having narcotics or other stimulants prohibited by law in the body.

id: driving without a valid control badge
ten: DRIVING WITHOUT A VALID CONTROL BADGE
mo_ta: A violation involving a driver operating a covered vehicle without the prescribed control badge or with a badge that has expired.

id: driving without a valid control insignia
ten: DRIVING WITHOUT A VALID CONTROL INSIGNIA
mo_ta: A violation consisting of driving a car or similar vehicle without the required control insignia, using an insignia that has expired, or using one not issued by a competent authority.

id: driving without a valid inspection certificate or sticker
ten: DRIVING WITHOUT A VALID INSPECTION CERTIFICATE OR STICKER
mo_ta: A traffic violation involving operating a vehicle that is required to undergo inspection without an inspection certificate or sticker, or with one that has been expired for at least one month. The provision sets a fine of 4,000,000 to 6,000,000 Vietnamese đồng and includes trailers and semi-trailers.

id: driving without a valid vehicle registration certificate
ten: DRIVING WITHOUT A VALID VEHICLE REGISTRATION CERTIFICATE
mo_ta: A traffic violation involving operating a motorcycle, moped, or similar vehicle without its vehicle registration certificate, or without the specified certified copy and original receipt when a credit institution or foreign bank branch holds the original certificate. The text states that this violation is punishable by a fine of 2,000,000 to 3,000,000 Vietnamese đồng.
A violation consisting of driving a covered vehicle without the required device for recording images of the driver.

id: driving without required approval or permit
ten: DRIVING WITHOUT REQUIRED APPROVAL OR PERMIT
mo_ta: The violation of driving a vehicle in traffic in Vietnam without written approval or a permit from the competent authority, when that vehicle type is subject to such a requirement.

id: driving without valid compulsory civil liability insurance
ten: DRIVING WITHOUT VALID COMPULSORY CIVIL LIABILITY INSURANCE
mo_ta: A violation involving a motorcycle, motorbike, or similar vehicle being driven without a valid compulsory civil liability insurance certificate for the vehicle owner. The stated fine is from 200,000 to 300,000 Vietnamese đồng.

id: driving without wearing a seat belt
ten: DRIVING WITHOUT WEARING A SEAT BELT
mo_ta: A road-traffic violation in which a person driving a car or similar vehicle on the road does not wear a seat belt.

**Driving-licence point deduction** is an administrative sanction for qualifying road-traffic violations. It involves subtracting points from the licence of the driver or vehicle operator and may be imposed alongside a fine or another penalty. The sanction is addressed in Articles 6, 17, 21, 27 and 32, including in connection with violations by cargo-vehicle drivers. The cited provisions do not specify the number of points deducted for the described overweight-towing conduct or for certain other violations.

When multiple qualifying violations are punished in the same case, only the point deduction for the violation carrying the highest deduction is applied. The authorized person must notify the affected licence holder of the deduction.
The deduction of points from driving licences provided for in the decree’s rules on violations by vehicle owners.

**DRIVING-LICENCE POINT RESTORATION** is the procedure for restoring points on a driving licence in cases covered by the relevant decree. It includes the applicable authority, the sequence of steps, and the procedures to be followed, and is carried out by the traffic-police officials authorized under the decree.

The procedure, described in Clause 3 of Article 51 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, for restoring points when a driving licence has lost all its points. It includes notifying the licence holder and updating the licence’s restored-point status.

The updating of information or status to show that driving-licence points have been restored, including publication on the Traffic Police Department’s website and, for licences represented as data messages, updates in the citizen’s electronic identification account.
People holding category A or B1 driving licences who are required to take the theoretical legal-knowledge test described in the circular.

A person who holds a driving license. If all points on the license are deducted, the holder may not drive a vehicle on roads under that license until the stated conditions for point restoration are met.

The agency responsible for issuing driving licenses. The authorized sanctioning official is to notify it if the violator has been identified and the relevant deadline has passed without resolution or compliance.
A test covering legal knowledge about road traffic order and safety. Its questions are based on the theoretical examination for the relevant driving-license class.

**DRIVING-LICENSE POINT DEDUCTION** is an administrative penalty measure under Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. It involves deducting points from a driving license for specified road-traffic violations and is addressed in provisions including Articles 6, 7, 12–14, 17, 20–22, 27, 32, and 34. These provisions cover various drivers and vehicle operators, including automobile and motorcycle operators, as well as vehicle owners; Article 27 concerns drivers transporting preschool children or students, while Article 32 addresses vehicle owners who violate road-traffic regulations.

The deduction may apply alongside other penalties. Some excerpts specify point amounts: a vehicle owner who directly operates the vehicle and commits a covered violation may lose four points; specified conduct under Clauses 3 or 3a of Article 29 results in a two-point deduction; and conduct described in points b and c of Clause 4 of Article 34 results in a three-point deduction. For many other violations, the cited descriptions identify point deduction as a possible or addressed consequence but do not state the amount—or establish that a deduction applies to the particular violation described. The applicable deduction therefore depends on the specific provision and conduct.

id: driving-license point deduction for a vehicle owner's violation
ten: DRIVING-LICENSE POINT DEDUCTION FOR A VEHICLE OWNER'S VIOLATION
mo_ta: The deduction of driving-license points as a consequence addressed by the decree for vehicle-owner violations.

id: driving-license point deduction for goods-vehicle violations
ten: DRIVING-LICENSE POINT DEDUCTION FOR GOODS-VEHICLE VIOLATIONS
mo_ta: A sanction addressed by Article 21 for certain violations involving goods-transport vehicles; the provided text does not specify the number of points deducted for the described overloading violation.

id: driving-license point deduction for vehicle-owner violations
ten: DRIVING-LICENSE POINT DEDUCTION FOR VEHICLE-OWNER VIOLATIONS
mo_ta: A penalty measure referenced in the title of Article 32 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, which concerns deducting points from driving licenses for vehicle owners who violate road-traffic regulations.
The deduction of points from the driving licenses of drivers who commit the specified road traffic violations, as provided for in Article 7 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP

**DRIVING-LICENSE POINT RESTORATION** is the process of restoring points to a driver’s license under the procedures and authority established by the decree. Eligibility and required examinations depend on the license category: a person whose motorcycle-license points have all been deducted may restore points by passing the required theoretical legal-knowledge test, while restoration of points on an automobile license requires passing both the theoretical legal-knowledge test and the simulated legal-knowledge test. In general, drivers may obtain point restoration after passing the examination or examinations specified for their circumstances.
Revocation of a driver's license when it was not issued by a competent authority or is invalid, in addition to other applicable penalties.

**DRIVING-LICENSE SUSPENSION** is an additional or supplementary penalty under Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP for specified road traffic violations. Depending on the violation and applicable provision—including Articles 7 and 35—the driver may lose the right to use their driving license for **10 to 12 months** or **22 to 24 months**. These ranges apply to different specified violations, rather than representing a single suspension period.
A supplementary penalty prescribed by Article 6, paragraph 15, of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP for the specified violations, involving withdrawal of the right to use a driving license for 22 to 24 months.

A violation committed by a practical driving instructor who either fails to carry a permit for a driving-practice vehicle or carries a permit that has expired. Article 39, Clause 1 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP prescribes a fine of 2,000,000 to 3,000,000 Vietnamese đồng for this violation.
A violation of the regulations referred to in Article 6 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP, committed by a learner during practical driving.

id: drying agricultural products on a roadway
ten: DRYING AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTS ON A ROADWAY
mo_ta: The act of drying rice, straw, agricultural, forestry, or seafood products on a roadway, listed as a punishable violation.

id: du lịch tại việt nam bằng xe cơ giới nước ngoài
ten: DU LỊCH TẠI VIỆT NAM BẰNG XE CƠ GIỚI NƯỚC NGOÀI
mo_ta: Tourism activity in which foreigners bring and use foreign motor vehicles in Vietnam, covered by the decree’s approval requirements.
The act of dumping chemicals in a way that endangers road traffic safety.
A duty to protect dykes, listed as a qualifying mission for an application to use a priority-vehicle signal device.

“DỪNG XE, ĐỖ XE” refers to stopping or parking a vehicle on a road, as regulated by Article 18 of Law 36/2024/QH15. Drivers must follow the applicable road-use rules. They may stop or park on a sufficiently wide roadside shoulder or on land outside the traveled portion of the road. If the shoulder is narrow or absent, they must stop or park close to the right edge of the road in their direction of travel.

An **economic organization** is a broad category that includes organizations established under either the Law on Cooperatives or the Law on Enterprises. Under the Law on Cooperatives, it includes cooperative groups, cooperatives, and cooperative unions. Under the Law on Enterprises, it includes the enterprise forms and dependent units covered by that law.

An educational institution is required to establish and communicate safe procedures for transporting its preschool children and students, and is responsible for ensuring road traffic order and safety during those transportation activities

Educational institutions are the settings in which legal knowledge and education about road traffic order and safety are provided. They include preschool institutions, schools, upper-secondary schools, vocational education institutions, and other educational establishments. The education may address children and students, with content suited to the relevant group. These institutions are also responsible for organizing legal awareness and information activities for people under their management. In schools and vocational institutions, instruction may additionally cover safe motorcycle riding and include assessment.

id: effective date for driver image-recording equipment penalties
ten: EFFECTIVE DATE FOR DRIVER IMAGE-RECORDING EQUIPMENT PENALTIES
mo_ta: The provisions on administrative penalties related to driver image-recording equipment for specified passenger and freight transport vehicles take effect on January 1, 2028.

id: effective date for passenger-cabin image-recording equipment penalties
ten: EFFECTIVE DATE FOR PASSENGER-CABIN IMAGE-RECORDING EQUIPMENT PENALTIES
mo_ta: The provisions on administrative penalties related to passenger-cabin image-recording equipment take effect on January 1, 2029, subject to the relevant law on such equipment in road vehicles.
The date on which Circular 13/2025/TT-BCA takes effect: March 1, 2025.
The event marking the date Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA takes effect, which is January 1, 2025.

id: effective date of clause 3 of article 10
ten: EFFECTIVE DATE OF CLAUSE 3 OF ARTICLE 10
mo_ta: The statutory commencement event for Clause 3 of Article 10 of Law No. 36/2024/QH15, set for July 1, 2026.
The date on which Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP came into force, used as the cutoff for the transitional rule in Article 54.
The date on which Decree 238/2026/NĐ-CP takes effect; the text uses this date to determine which rules apply to earlier administrative violations.

id: effective date of driver image-recording penalties
ten: EFFECTIVE DATE OF DRIVER IMAGE-RECORDING PENALTIES
mo_ta: The date on which the specified administrative-violation penalties concerning driver image-recording equipment take effect: January 1, 2028

The effective date of Law 36/2024/QH15 is January 1, 2025, except as otherwise provided in Clause 2 of Article 88. This date also marks the cutoff for transitional rules concerning driving licences issued before the law takes effect.
The event when Law No. 36/2024/QH15 takes effect; the text uses this date to distinguish previously issued driving licenses covered by the transitional rule.

id: effective date of point a, clause 20, article 7 of law 118/2025/qh15
ten: EFFECTIVE DATE OF POINT A, CLAUSE 20, ARTICLE 7 OF LAW 118/2025/QH15
mo_ta: The provision at point a, clause 20, Article 7 of Law 118/2025/QH15 takes effect on January 1, 2026.

id: effective date of the passenger-compartment image-recording provisions
ten: EFFECTIVE DATE OF THE PASSENGER-COMPARTMENT IMAGE-RECORDING PROVISIONS
mo_ta: The provisions on administrative penalties related to image-recording equipment in passenger compartments, referenced in Article 53 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, take effect on January 1, 2029.
The date on which the provisions concerning the specified motor-vehicle and transport-business databases take effect.
The circular is scheduled to take effect on July 1, 2026, except for cases specified in Clause 6 of Article 6.
The provision states that Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP takes effect on January 1, 2025, except for the provisions in Clauses 2, 3, and 4 of Article 53.

id: effectiveness of motorcycle and moped emissions inspection provisions
ten: EFFECTIVENESS OF MOTORCYCLE AND MOPED EMISSIONS INSPECTION PROVISIONS
mo_ta: The provision at point b, clause 1, Article 32 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP takes effect according to the environmental protection law provisions on inspection of motorcycle and moped emissions.

id: effectiveness of selected provisions on january 1, 2026
ten: EFFECTIVENESS OF SELECTED PROVISIONS ON JANUARY 1, 2026
mo_ta: The provisions at point m, clause 3, Article 6; point e, clause 4, Article 26; and point b, clause 1, Article 27 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP are to take effect on January 1, 2026.
The deduction of eight points from a driver's license, applied when a vehicle owner directly driving the vehicle commits the specified road traffic violation.
The deduction of eight points from a driver's license, imposed in addition to other penalties when the driver commits an act specified in Clause 7 of Article 21.
Elderly and frail people participating in road traffic are identified as a subject covered by Article 30 of Law 36/2024/QH15.
Elderly or frail people are recognized as a group participating in road traffic. Their participation is addressed under Article 30, including clause 2, and they should be helped when crossing a road.
Elderly people, including frail people, are identified in the heading of Article 30 as a group participating in road traffic.
The process of submitting the licensing dossier through the National Public Service Portal or the National Identity Application, with the application form completed electronically.

The ELECTRONIC IDENTIFICATION AND AUTHENTICATION SYSTEM is an electronic system used to access and verify a test participant’s identity information. It is accessed through the national identification application and may provide candidate identity details for comparison with the information in the participant’s examination application.

The **ELECTRONIC INFORMATION PORTAL** is an online portal managed within the competent authority’s scope. The authority uses it to publicly announce proposed examination dates and examination schedules, including the test’s date, time, and location. The portal also provides public access to study materials on road traffic order and safety laws.
Primary-level students who are to learn commonly encountered road traffic rules and why those rules must be followed.
Agencies and organizations that meet the requirements to use signal-emitting devices on priority vehicles and may apply for a new or replacement permit.
A person who has completed driver training and meets the age and health requirements specified in Article 59, and may register for a driving test

People from ethnic-minority groups who cannot read or write Vietnamese, previously held an A1 motorcycle driving license, and have had all its points deducted; they may take the separate road traffic legal-knowledge test)

**EMERGENCY DUTIES** are urgent assignments performed in emergency circumstances. Depending on the applicable legal provisions, they may justify allowing oversized or overweight vehicles to travel on roads. Duties carried out during a legally defined state of emergency may also qualify priority vehicles to use flashing blue lights, while urgent police duties may qualify police vehicles to use priority-vehicle signal equipment.

**EMERGENCY DUTY** is a legally defined urgent official mission carried out by vehicles of the military, police, or procuracy forces. Such missions may include arrests, searches, investigative activities, and other urgent assigned tasks. Vehicles performing emergency duty are treated as priority vehicles and are covered by rules on priority-signal devices, including the use of flashing blue and red lights where specified.

id: emergency duty by a priority vehicle
ten: EMERGENCY DUTY BY A PRIORITY VEHICLE
mo_ta: A priority vehicle traveling against the direction of traffic while carrying out an emergency duty is an exception to the wrong-way driving penalty described in the text.

EMERGENCY DUTY BY PRIORITY VEHICLES refers to the operation of priority vehicles while carrying out emergency duties. Such operation is excepted from the stated wrong-way driving penalty when conducted in accordance with applicable regulations, and is also identified as an exception to the prohibited-entry violation described in the text.

id: emergency duty of a priority vehicle
ten: EMERGENCY DUTY OF A PRIORITY VEHICLE
mo_ta: An urgent mission performed by a priority vehicle. The text specifies that priority vehicles on such missions are excepted from the described prohibition.
Urgent medical care provided to road traffic accident victims.
An emergency-response assignment for which an ambulance may use flashing red priority lights.

An emergency response mission in which an ambulance is dispatched to provide emergency medical assistance; the text refers to an ambulance performing this duty while using signaling equipment for priority vehicles.

EMERGENCY MEDICAL RESPONSE is an emergency medical assignment or mission carried out by an ambulance. During the response, the ambulance uses red flashing priority lights and is granted priority at intersections under Article 27, Clause 2 of Law 36/2024/QH15.
Urgent duties performed by military vehicles, including the operational, security, investigative, and counterterrorism missions specified in Article 18.
Emergency missions performed by military forces, for which their priority vehicles may be authorized to use signal-emitting devices.
An urgent duty performed by vehicles of the military forces, police, or procuracy; such vehicles receive priority under the cited provision.
An emergency process allowing an applicant to consult the competent authority in advance about obtaining a permit, followed by submission of the required application documents.

id: emergency signal to stop a train
ten: EMERGENCY SIGNAL TO STOP A TRAIN
mo_ta: The immediate signaling required when a road vehicle breakdown, road traffic accident, or cargo spill obstructs a railway crossing or shared railway bridge and cannot be cleared promptly.

An **EMERGENCY SITUATION** is a legally defined and declared emergency under the relevant decree. During it, vehicles assigned to serve the Steering Committee or mobilized functional forces may perform their duties, including qualifying missions using a priority-vehicle signal device under Article 17(3)(a). Applicants may communicate with the competent authority in advance about a permit, but must submit the required application documents immediately afterward. Under Article 22(2) of Decree No. 151/2024/NĐ-CP, the permit for the vehicle’s signal device expires immediately when the emergency condition referred to in Article 18(8) ends.

id: emergency stop in a road tunnel
ten: EMERGENCY STOP IN A ROAD TUNNEL
mo_ta: A stop in a road tunnel required by a technical failure or another force majeure circumstance; if the vehicle cannot be moved to an emergency stopping area, the driver must signal and promptly report the situation.

The **EMERGENCY STOPPING LANE** is the lane alongside an expressway, running in the direction of traffic, designated for vehicles that must stop because of a technical problem or another unavoidable circumstance. It is reserved for emergency stops, and driving in the lane is identified as a traffic violation.
A designated lane or area on a highway for emergency stops.
A designated position in a road tunnel where a vehicle must be moved if an emergency makes stopping necessary.
An exception to the helmet-related penalty applies when a driver is transporting a sick person for emergency care.

id: emergency transport of an injured person
ten: EMERGENCY TRANSPORT OF AN INJURED PERSON
mo_ta: Taking an injured person for emergency medical care, an exception that may justify leaving the accident scene.

id: emergency travel by a priority vehicle
ten: EMERGENCY TRAVEL BY A PRIORITY VEHICLE
mo_ta: A priority vehicle traveling while performing an urgent mission, an exception to the listed entry-prohibition violations.

An **EMPLOYEE** is a person who works for a vehicle owner. The owner may assign or permit the employee to operate the owner’s vehicle. If permitted to operate it, the employee may commit the violation described in point b, clause 4, Article 34 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP.
EMPLOYEES are people employed by a vehicle owner who may be permitted to drive or otherwise operate the vehicle and may commit a specified traffic violation referenced in the decree.

Conduct described in the decree in which a vehicle owner hands over a vehicle or allows an employee or representative to operate it and commit a violation specified in Article 21, Clause 8, points a or b.

id: encounter with a group of pedestrians
ten: ENCOUNTER WITH A GROUP OF PEDESTRIANS
mo_ta: A road-traffic situation in which a road user encounters a group of pedestrians; the cited provision requires the road user to observe, slow down, or stop as needed for safety.
A road-traffic situation in which a road user encounters a vehicle transporting hazardous goods; the cited provision requires the road user to observe, slow down, or stop as needed for safety.

id: encounter with oversized or overweight cargo vehicles
ten: ENCOUNTER WITH OVERSIZED OR OVERWEIGHT CARGO VEHICLES
mo_ta: A road-traffic situation in which a road user encounters a vehicle transporting oversized or overweight cargo; the cited provision requires the road user to observe, slow down, or stop as needed for safety.
A road situation in which a driver encounters pedestrians crossing the road; using high beams in this situation is included among the prohibited conduct.
Encouraging illegal road racing is prohibited under Article 9 of Law 36/2024/QH15.

id: end of a vehicle’s service life
ten: END OF A VEHICLE’S SERVICE LIFE
mo_ta: A circumstance specified in Article 25, Clause 5, that requires revocation of an intelligent transport vehicle’s operating license.

id: engine removal for registration on another vehicle
ten: ENGINE REMOVAL FOR REGISTRATION ON ANOTHER VEHICLE
mo_ta: The removal of an engine from a vehicle so it can be registered for use in another vehicle, a circumstance listed for revocation.

id: ensuring road traffic order and safety
ten: ENSURING ROAD TRAFFIC ORDER AND SAFETY
mo_ta: The activity of maintaining road traffic order and safety, including on the route or road section used by dangerous-goods transport vehicles.
The activity addressed by Article 51 of Law 36/2024/QH15: maintaining order and safety on roads in relation to road vehicles transporting dangerous goods.
Operating a motorcycle, moped, or similar vehicle by entering a highway, an act listed in the provision as a violation when it causes a traffic accident.

id: entering a main road from a side road without yielding
ten: ENTERING A MAIN ROAD FROM A SIDE ROAD WITHOUT YIELDING
mo_ta: A traffic violation involving failure to slow down or stop and yield when entering a main road from a side road.

id: entering a priority road from a non-priority road without yielding
ten: ENTERING A PRIORITY ROAD FROM A NON-PRIORITY ROAD WITHOUT YIELDING
mo_ta: A traffic violation involving failure to slow down or stop and yield when entering a priority road from a non-priority road.

A traffic violation described in Article 8, clause 6 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP: operating a vehicle into an area where entry is prohibited for that vehicle type, subject to a fine of 3,000,000 to 5,000,000 đồng, except for specified cases.

id: entering a prohibited area or road
ten: ENTERING A PROHIBITED AREA OR ROAD
mo_ta: **ENTERING A PROHIBITED AREA OR ROAD** is a road-traffic violation committed when a driver enters an area closed to traffic or drives onto a road where the vehicle type is prohibited, whether the restriction is imposed by a traffic sign or by a competent authority. The violation is subject to a fine of 2,000,000 to 3,000,000 Vietnamese đồng, subject to specified exceptions, including certain violations set out elsewhere in Article 8 and priority vehicles responding to an emergency.
A prohibited act of entering a hydraulic work, explicitly listed as an exception to the penalty provision for entering a prohibited area or road.

id: entering a prohibited road causing a traffic accident
ten: ENTERING A PROHIBITED ROAD CAUSING A TRAFFIC ACCIDENT
mo_ta: Driving onto a road marked as prohibited for the type of vehicle being driven and causing a traffic accident.

id: entering a road with a vehicle-specific no-entry sign
ten: ENTERING A ROAD WITH A VEHICLE-SPECIFIC NO-ENTRY SIGN
mo_ta: A traffic violation described in Article 8, clause 6 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP: operating a vehicle onto a road displaying a sign prohibiting entry for that vehicle type, subject to a fine of 3,000,000 to 5,000,000 đồng, except for specified cases.

id: entering an electronic toll lane without a vehicle tag
ten: ENTERING AN ELECTRONIC TOLL LANE WITHOUT A VEHICLE TAG
mo_ta: A road traffic violation in which a driver enters a lane reserved for automatic, non-stop electronic toll collection without the required onboard terminal tag.

id: entering an expressway with an animal or animal-drawn vehicle
ten: ENTERING AN EXPRESSWAY WITH AN ANIMAL OR ANIMAL-DRAWN VEHICLE
mo_ta: A road-traffic violation involving a person driving or leading an animal, or operating an animal-drawn vehicle, onto an expressway. The stated fine is 1,000,000 to 2,000,000 Vietnamese dong.

id: entering or exiting a stopping or parking position without signaling
ten: ENTERING OR EXITING A STOPPING OR PARKING POSITION WITHOUT SIGNALING
mo_ta: A road-traffic violation described in Article 6: a driver enters or exits a stopping or parking position without signaling to notify other drivers. The stated fine is 400,000 to 600,000 Vietnamese đồng.

id: entering or exiting an expressway without following the rules
ten: ENTERING OR EXITING AN EXPRESSWAY WITHOUT FOLLOWING THE RULES
mo_ta: A road-traffic violation consisting of failing to comply with regulations when entering or leaving an expressway.

id: entering or leaving a stopping or parking position
ten: ENTERING OR LEAVING A STOPPING OR PARKING POSITION
mo_ta: The vehicle maneuver for which Article 18, clause 3 requires the driver to signal to other road users.
A business entity to which dependent units belong; the text identifies branches and representative offices as dependent enterprise units.
Businesses asked to coordinate in researching and developing road-travel programs and routes for foreign tourists.
Enterprises assigned by the Vietnamese State to manage, operate, and maintain certain expressways.
Prohibited conduct under Article 9 of Law 36/2024/QH15, involving soliciting or enticing passengers.

id: entry and exit of foreign motor vehicles
ten: ENTRY AND EXIT OF FOREIGN MOTOR VEHICLES
mo_ta: ENTRY AND EXIT OF FOREIGN MOTOR VEHICLES refers to the regulated process of bringing foreign motor vehicles into traffic in Vietnamese territory and taking them out of the country. These movements must be organized and conducted in accordance with applicable regulations.
The subject addressed by Article 12 of Circular 38/2024/TT-BGTVT.

id: entry into force of circular no. 105/2026/tt-bca
ten: ENTRY INTO FORCE OF CIRCULAR NO. 105/2026/TT-BCA
mo_ta: The taking effect of Circular No. 105/2026/TT-BCA. The text does not specify its effective date; it states that the cited provisions of Circular No. 65/2024/TT-BCA cease to be effective from that date.

id: entry into force of clause 3 of article 10 of law 36/2024/qh15
ten: ENTRY INTO FORCE OF CLAUSE 3 OF ARTICLE 10 OF LAW 36/2024/QH15
mo_ta: Clause 3 of Article 10 of Law 36/2024/QH15 takes effect on January 1, 2026.
The decree's commencement, which Article 38 refers to as the point from which the stated repeals apply; no specific date is provided.
The provisions of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP take effect on January 1, 2025, except for the provision specified in Clause 2 of Article 53.
The event of the decree taking legal effect, referenced by the heading of Article 28

ENTRY INTO VIETNAM refers to the process by which foreign nationals enter the country. Their entry is governed by applicable immigration rules, which determine the relevant visa period and the period during which they may participate in traffic. Required customs procedures must also be completed as part of the entry process.
Procedures that foreigners must complete under the laws governing entry into Vietnam.

id: entry, exit, transit, and residence of foreign nationals
ten: ENTRY, EXIT, TRANSIT, AND RESIDENCE OF FOREIGN NATIONALS
mo_ta: The immigration and residence activities in Vietnam that are subject to applicable legal requirements.
Environmental pollution that may result from the specified administrative violations.

id: environmental pollution caused by an administrative violation
ten: ENVIRONMENTAL POLLUTION CAUSED BY AN ADMINISTRATIVE VIOLATION
mo_ta: Environmental pollution resulting from an administrative violation; the text says the responsible party may be compelled to take measures to remedy it.
Protection of the environment, which the road traffic principles are intended to support

The **Environmental Protection Law** is the body of legislation governing environmental protection. Its provisions determine when the motorcycle and moped emissions-inspection rule takes effect, including the provision in point b, clause 1 of Article 32 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP.
An **ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION VIOLATION** is a violation of regulations concerning environmental protection, including violations covered by the cited road-traffic penalty provisions.
Violations of environmental protection regulations committed while participating in traffic, as described in Article 17.
Corrective measures requiring the person responsible to remedy environmental pollution caused by an administrative violation.
A violation of environmental-protection regulations covered by the cited road-traffic sanctioning provisions.
An act by a driver of a car, tractor, or similar vehicle that violates environmental-protection regulations while participating in traffic.

id: environmental-protection violation by a vehicle driver
ten: ENVIRONMENTAL-PROTECTION VIOLATION BY A VEHICLE DRIVER
mo_ta: A violation covered by Article 17, involving a driver of a car, tractor, or similar vehicle breaching environmental-protection rules while participating in traffic.

A violation of environmental-protection requirements committed by a driver while participating in traffic; Article 17 addresses penalties for such violations by drivers of cars, tractors, and similar vehicles.
A violation of environmental-protection regulations committed by a driver of an automobile, tractor, or similar vehicle while participating in traffic.
Violations of regulations concerning environmental protection, listed among the conduct subject to the measures in the text.

Violations described in Article 17, including transporting soil, rocks, waste, or loose goods without adequate covering, allowing cargo to spill onto a road, or carrying goods or waste so that water runs onto the road and creates a traffic-safety hazard.
An epidemic-related incident referenced as a situation requiring vehicles to carry out emergency response and remediation duties.
Activities to prevent or control epidemics, listed as a circumstance permitting the transport of people in a goods-truck cargo bed.

EPIDEMIC RESPONSE refers to duties and operations carried out to address epidemics, disease outbreaks, and related incidents. Vehicles assigned to this work may be designated as priority vehicles and are eligible to use priority-vehicle signalling equipment, including flashing blue lights, as provided for under the applicable decree.
Epidemics are among the public emergencies traffic police participate in preventing.
The erasure or alteration of a technical-safety and environmental-protection inspection certificate or inspection sticker, which the text identifies as subject to surrender.

id: escort of suspects, defendants, and prisoners
ten: ESCORT OF SUSPECTS, DEFENDANTS, AND PRISONERS
mo_ta: Police escort duties involving suspects, defendants, or prisoners.

id: escorting a person accused of a legal violation
ten: ESCORTING A PERSON ACCUSED OF A LEGAL VIOLATION
mo_ta: An exception to the helmet-related penalty applies when the passenger is being escorted for having committed a legal violation.
The duty of escorting suspects, defendants, or prisoners.
A member of an ethnic minority taking the road traffic legal knowledge examination; if accompanied by an interpreter, the examinee and interpreter sign or fingerprint the examination record

id: ethnic-minority test participants unable to read or write vietnamese
ten: ETHNIC-MINORITY TEST PARTICIPANTS UNABLE TO READ OR WRITE VIETNAMESE
mo_ta: Ethnic-minority test participants who cannot read or write Vietnamese. When taking the test, they use an interpreter hired by the competent testing authority.

id: evacuating people from a dangerous area
ten: EVACUATING PEOPLE FROM A DANGEROUS AREA
mo_ta: Moving people out of a dangerous area, a circumstance permitting their transport in a goods-truck cargo bed.

id: evading detection of an oversized or overweight vehicle
ten: EVADING DETECTION OF AN OVERSIZED OR OVERWEIGHT VEHICLE
mo_ta: A violation under Article 34, Clause 5, involving transferring cargo or using other tactics to avoid detection of an oversized or overweight vehicle.

id: evading detection of vehicle overloading or overcapacity
ten: EVADING DETECTION OF VEHICLE OVERLOADING OR OVERCAPACITY
mo_ta: Conduct intended to prevent authorities from detecting a vehicle carrying more load or passengers than legally permitted.

id: evading responsibility through false or inaccurate reporting
ten: EVADING RESPONSIBILITY THROUGH FALSE OR INACCURATE REPORTING
mo_ta: The violation of failing to report, reporting falsely, or providing inaccurate information or documents to evade responsibility after being found to have violated road traffic order and safety laws.
Intentional evasion of or obstruction to the sanctioning process; when it ends, the period for using collected results is recalculated.

id: events organized by the party and state
ten: EVENTS ORGANIZED BY THE PARTY AND STATE
mo_ta: The provision allows temporary registration and license plates for vehicles serving events organized by the Party and the State.
People generally, who have a responsibility to help the specified groups when they cross a road.
A person registering to take the examination on legal knowledge concerning road traffic order and safety. The registrant must submit a valid health certificate issued by a competent medical facility.
The process by which people register to take the road traffic law knowledge examination and provide contact details in an application.
A notice sent to people who previously registered when the examination’s announced time or location changes; it is sent by email or text message using contact details provided in the application.
The activity of examining and overseeing matters related to road traffic order and safety.
Examination of road-traffic law knowledge for people seeking to operate specialized motorcycles.
An examination of road-traffic legal knowledge for operators of specialized motorcycles, as described in Article 63 of Law 36/2024/QH15.

id: examination of road traffic law knowledge
ten: EXAMINATION OF ROAD TRAFFIC LAW KNOWLEDGE
mo_ta: An examination of knowledge of laws concerning road traffic order and safety, whose responsibilities are addressed in Article 8.
The procedure at the end of an examination in which the candidate signs or fingerprints the examination record; an interpreter also signs or fingerprints it when applicable.
People who register to take the legal-knowledge examination; they may choose and register for an examination date using Form No. 01 in the circular’s appendix.

EXAMINATION REGISTRATION is the process of applying to take the road traffic law knowledge examination by submitting the required registration dossier, including an application and health certificate. When registering online, applicants also select a testing authority and choose an examination date.

The process of registering for and arranging the road traffic law-knowledge examination, including submitting a dossier in advance, selecting an examination date and competent authority, and arranging the examination’s time and location.

id: examination result update and data synchronization
ten: EXAMINATION RESULT UPDATE AND DATA SYNCHRONIZATION
mo_ta: The process in which examination results are entered into the road traffic law knowledge examination software and synchronized with the administrative violation handling database for road traffic order and safety.
The prompt notice sent to registered examinees when a previously announced examination time or location changes. It gives the updated time and location.

The competent authority’s notice to registered examinees stating the examination’s time and location. It must be sent at least two working days before the examination, once a complete and valid application has been received.
The notification of a person’s road-traffic-law examination results to the relevant driver’s-license authorities.

An EXAMINEE is a person taking an examination on knowledge of laws concerning road traffic order and safety. The examinee may be a foreign national or a member of an ethnic minority and may have an interpreter.
An official who instructs test participants on how to complete the test and whose instructions they are required to follow.
Training for driving-test examiners, which the Minister of Transport regulates as part of examiner qualification and certification requirements.
The training of officials and issuance of examiner cards by the Traffic Police Department, as required for officials assigned to conduct the legal knowledge tests.
Officials certified to conduct legal knowledge tests on road traffic order and safety.
The violation of using a road traffic rescue vehicle to carry a rescued vehicle whose weight exceeds the rescue vehicle’s permitted carrying capacity.
Transporting cargo that exceeds the prescribed dimensional limits.
**EXCEEDING PERMITTED PASSENGER CAPACITY** is a violation that occurs when a vehicle carries or transports more people than it is permitted or authorized to carry.

id: exceeding permitted passenger capacity by more than 100%
ten: EXCEEDING PERMITTED PASSENGER CAPACITY BY MORE THAN 100%
mo_ta: A traffic violation by a driver of a passenger car or similar vehicle, involving carrying more than twice the number of passengers the vehicle is permitted to carry.
The violation of towing a rescued vehicle whose weight exceeds the rescue vehicle’s permitted towing capacity as recorded in its technical safety and environmental protection inspection certificate.
