Oversized Vehicle Operation refers to operating a vehicle on public roads when it exceeds the permitted size or dimensional limits. It is a road traffic violation addressed by Articles 31 and 34. Specified violations in this category may result in points being deducted from the driver’s licence.
A traffic violation involving a vehicle whose dimensions exceed the permitted limits while it is operating on a road.

**OVERTAKING** is the traffic maneuver in which a vehicle passes a vehicle traveling ahead. On a road with one motor-vehicle lane in each direction, it is defined as the vehicle behind moving left to pass; on roads with multiple lanes in the same direction, moving ahead is governed by lane-use rules.

Under Article 14 of Law 36/2024/QH15, overtaking is permitted only when the road ahead is safe. The overtaking driver must signal and maintain a safe distance from vehicles ahead and behind, while the vehicle being passed must not obstruct the maneuver. Overtaking is prohibited in specified circumstances, including when weather or road conditions make it unsafe, where visibility is restricted at a hill crest on a two-way road or on a curve, and in specified road-crossing situations.

**OVERTAKING A VEHICLE** is the act of passing another vehicle, as addressed in Article 14 of Law 36/2024/QH15. The article prohibits overtaking when the conditions set out in Clause 3 are not met and in locations specified under the article, including those covered by Clause 6.

id: overtaking and yielding to a vehicle requesting to pass
ten: OVERTAKING AND YIELDING TO A VEHICLE REQUESTING TO PASS
mo_ta: The traffic maneuvers identified as the subject of Article 14 of Law 36/2024/QH15.

id: overtaking and yielding to overtaking vehicles
ten: OVERTAKING AND YIELDING TO OVERTAKING VEHICLES
mo_ta: A traffic situation addressed in Article 14 of Law 36/2024/QH15. A vehicle may overtake only when the road ahead is unobstructed, there is no oncoming traffic in the intended overtaking section, and the vehicle ahead is not itself signaling to overtake another vehicle; the vehicle ahead must signal a right turn and move to the right to allow passing.
A road traffic violation involving overtaking on a road section marked with a sign prohibiting overtaking for the vehicle being driven.

id: overtaking where a no-overtaking sign applies
ten: OVERTAKING WHERE A NO-OVERTAKING SIGN APPLIES
mo_ta: A road traffic violation in which a driver overtakes on a section displaying a sign prohibiting overtaking for the type of vehicle being driven, subject to the exception cited in Article 7, Clause 4.
A road traffic violation involving overtaking without signaling beforehand.

**OVERWEIGHT TRAILER-TOWING VIOLATION** refers to towing a trailer or semi-trailer whose total mass exceeds the permitted towing mass recorded in the vehicle’s technical-safety and environmental-protection inspection certificate by more than 100%. Under Article 21 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, the applicable fine depends on the degree of excess: exceeding the permitted mass by more than 100% and up to 150% carries a fine of 7,000,000 to 8,000,000 Vietnamese đồng under Clause 7; exceeding it by more than 150% carries a fine of 8,000,000 to 12,000,000 Vietnamese đồng under Clause 8.

OVERWEIGHT VEHICLE OPERATION refers to operating a vehicle on a public road when it exceeds the permitted weight limit. It is addressed as a vehicle category under Article 31, and specified violations may result in a deduction of driving-licence points under the cited decree.

id: owner directly operating a vehicle in violation
ten: OWNER DIRECTLY OPERATING A VEHICLE IN VIOLATION
mo_ta: “OWNER DIRECTLY OPERATING A VEHICLE IN VIOLATION” refers to a vehicle owner who personally operates the vehicle while committing a violation under Article 34, Clause 2, or the violation specified in Article 20, Clause 4.

The OWNER’S REPRESENTATIVE is a person who represents a vehicle owner and may be assigned or permitted to operate the vehicle. If operating it, the representative may commit the violation described in point b, clause 4, Article 34 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP.

People who own motor vehicles. Under Article 43, clause 2, they must maintain and repair vehicles to preserve their technical condition and are legally responsible for putting vehicles that do not meet technical-safety and environmental-protection requirements into road traffic.

id: owners of motor vehicles and specialized-use vehicles
ten: OWNERS OF MOTOR VEHICLES AND SPECIALIZED-USE VEHICLES
mo_ta: People who own motor vehicles or specialized-use vehicles. The excerpt requires them to maintain and repair their vehicles to preserve their technical condition and makes them legally responsible for putting vehicles that fail technical-safety or environmental-protection requirements into road traffic.

People who own specialized-use vehicles. Under Article 43, clause 2, they must maintain and repair vehicles to preserve their technical condition and are legally responsible for putting vehicles that do not meet technical-safety and environmental-protection requirements into road traffic.

id: paid cargo transport in a non-commercial vehicle
ten: PAID CARGO TRANSPORT IN A NON-COMMERCIAL VEHICLE
mo_ta: The violation of driving a car that is not used for commercial goods transport while carrying goods for payment; Article 21 of the decree specifies a fine of 8,000,000 to 12,000,000 Vietnamese dong for this conduct.
A procession involving people carried in the bed of a cargo truck; the text states this is allowed when authorized by a competent authority
A paragraph listing remedial measures for administrative violations involving road traffic order and safety, including requiring the removal of objects obscuring road signs or traffic lights.
The paragraph specifying fines of 1,000,000 to 2,000,000 Vietnamese đồng for the listed violations involving contract-based passenger transport.
The paragraph of Article 32 that sets fines for vehicle owners who allow vehicles with required inspection certificates or stickers expired by less than one month to participate in traffic.

The act of leaving a vehicle stationary for an unlimited period; the text requires use of the parking brake or another safety measure before leaving the vehicle, and additional precautions when parking on a slope
“PARKING A VEHICLE” refers to the act of leaving a vehicle stationary. Article 18, Clause 3 of Law 36/2024/QH15 addresses this conduct and prohibits parking on the left side of a one-way road.
PARKING AREAS are facilities where road inspectors may conduct inspections and checks under the cited provisions.

id: parking at a firefighting water access point
ten: PARKING AT A FIREFIGHTING WATER ACCESS POINT
mo_ta: A violation in which a driver parks at a place reserved for fire engines to draw water.
Applying the parking brake is a safety measure required when the driver leaves the driving position for specified tasks while the vehicle is stopped.

id: parking more than 0.25 meters from the right-hand road edge
ten: PARKING MORE THAN 0.25 METERS FROM THE RIGHT-HAND ROAD EDGE
mo_ta: A violation in which a driver parks without positioning the vehicle close to the right-hand road edge or sidewalk, leaving the nearest wheel more than 0.25 meters away.
A violation in which a driver parks on a road reserved for buses.

id: parking on a slope without wheel chocks
ten: PARKING ON A SLOPE WITHOUT WHEEL CHOCKS
mo_ta: PARKING ON A SLOPE WITHOUT WHEEL CHOCKS is a traffic violation in which a vehicle is parked on a slope without securing its wheels with chocks.

id: parking over a sewer drain opening
ten: PARKING OVER A SEWER DRAIN OPENING
mo_ta: A violation in which a driver parks over the mouth of a sewer drain.

id: parking over a telephone or high-voltage electricity manhole
ten: PARKING OVER A TELEPHONE OR HIGH-VOLTAGE ELECTRICITY MANHOLE
mo_ta: A violation in which a driver parks over a manhole associated with telephone lines or high-voltage electricity.

id: parking vehicles on the central median strip
ten: PARKING VEHICLES ON THE CENTRAL MEDIAN STRIP
mo_ta: A violation consisting of occupying the central median strip to park vehicles.
A traffic violation consisting of parking where a no-parking sign is posted, subject to the exception referenced in point b, Clause 6 of Article 8.
A violation in which a driver parks where a sign prohibits parking, or where a sign prohibits both stopping and parking, subject to the exceptions referenced in the decree.

id: parking where stopping and parking are prohibited
ten: PARKING WHERE STOPPING AND PARKING ARE PROHIBITED
mo_ta: A traffic violation consisting of parking where a sign prohibits both stopping and parking, subject to the exception referenced in point b, Clause 6 of Article 8.

id: participating in road traffic with a vehicle lacking valid inspection
ten: PARTICIPATING IN ROAD TRAFFIC WITH A VEHICLE LACKING VALID INSPECTION
mo_ta: The road-traffic violation of using a motor vehicle, specialized motor vehicle, or related trailer that is required to undergo inspection but lacks an inspection certificate or environmental-protection inspection label, or has one that expired at least one month earlier.

“Participation in Traffic in Vietnam” refers to driving or operating vehicles on Vietnam’s roads. It includes foreign nationals and foreign motor vehicles, whose participation is subject to written approval. Foreign vehicles may use Vietnam’s roads for no longer than the applicable visa or visa-exemption period, except where an additional-stay circumstance applies. Violations, accidents, and other related incidents may occur during such participation.
A type of economic organization established under the Law on Enterprises.
Agencies of the Party whose vehicles are eligible to receive license plates with a blue background and white letters and numbers under the stated provision.

id: passage on a road section with obstructed visibility
ten: PASSAGE ON A ROAD SECTION WITH OBSTRUCTED VISIBILITY
mo_ta: The passage of a vehicle covered by the regulation on a road section where visibility is obstructed

id: passage on a single-lane one-way road
ten: PASSAGE ON A SINGLE-LANE ONE-WAY ROAD
mo_ta: The passage of a vehicle covered by the regulation on a one-way road with one lane, where other vehicles have difficulty avoiding or overtaking it

id: passage on a two-way road with one lane in each direction
ten: PASSAGE ON A TWO-WAY ROAD WITH ONE LANE IN EACH DIRECTION
mo_ta: The passage of a vehicle covered by the regulation on a two-way road with only one traffic lane in each direction

id: passage over a road structure requiring reinforcement
ten: PASSAGE OVER A ROAD STRUCTURE REQUIRING REINFORCEMENT
mo_ta: The passage of a vehicle covered by the regulation over a road structure that needs reinforcement

id: passage through road sections requiring safety measures
ten: PASSAGE THROUGH ROAD SECTIONS REQUIRING SAFETY MEASURES
mo_ta: The operation of the specified vehicles on roads when passing a road structure that needs reinforcement, a section with obstructed visibility, a two-way road with only one lane in each direction, or a one-way road with a single lane where other vehicles have difficulty avoiding or passing them

A **PASSENGER** is a person being carried in a vehicle, including a motorcycle, motorbike, moped, or similar two- or three-wheeled vehicle. Passengers must follow instructions intended to maintain traffic order and safety. Under Article 33, prohibited conduct includes standing on a motorcycle or its cargo rack, sitting on the handlebars, and clinging to, towing, or pushing another vehicle while participating in road traffic. A passenger who commits a violation specified in the relevant provision may be fined 400,000 to 600,000 Vietnamese dong. The rules also address passengers boarding or leaving a passenger vehicle: allowing someone to do so while the vehicle is moving is a violation.
The activity of a passenger getting out of a vehicle, identified as a reason for temporarily stopping it.

id: passenger and goods transport by motorcycles, mopeds, and rudimentary vehicles
ten: PASSENGER AND GOODS TRANSPORT BY MOTORCYCLES, MOPEDS, AND RUDIMENTARY VEHICLES
mo_ta: PASSENGER AND GOODS TRANSPORT BY MOTORCYCLES, MOPEDS, AND RUDIMENTARY VEHICLES refers to the road-transport activity covered by Article 47 of Law 36/2024/QH15. It involves using motorcycles, mopeds, or rudimentary vehicles to carry passengers or goods and is subject to the article’s specified road-safety requirements.

id: passenger and goods transport by road
ten: PASSENGER AND GOODS TRANSPORT BY ROAD
mo_ta: The activity of transporting passengers and goods using motorcycles, motorbikes, and rudimentary vehicles, subject to the requirements stated in Article 47 of Law 36/2024/QH15.

id: passenger and goods transport by two-wheeled and rudimentary vehicles
ten: PASSENGER AND GOODS TRANSPORT BY TWO-WHEELED AND RUDIMENTARY VEHICLES
mo_ta: The regulated activity of transporting passengers and goods using motorcycles, mopeds, or rudimentary vehicles, subject to requirements for safe loading and limits on passengers, cargo weight, and vehicle dimensions.
The activity of a passenger getting into a vehicle, identified as a reason for temporarily stopping it.
The activity of passengers getting on or off vehicles at a road stopping or parking point

id: passenger failure to follow onboard instructions
ten: PASSENGER FAILURE TO FOLLOW ONBOARD INSTRUCTIONS
mo_ta: A traffic-order and safety violation in which a passenger traveling in a vehicle does not comply with instructions from the driver or onboard service staff. The text states that this conduct is punishable by a fine of 100,000 to 200,000 Vietnamese dong under Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, Article 33, Clause 1.
The violation of carrying more than 50% above the number of people a vehicle is permitted to carry; the text says this can result in suspension of the vehicle’s operating insignia.
Road locations designated for picking up or dropping off passengers.
A violation involving the pickup or dropoff of passengers, referenced in Article 20(8), Article 21(9), and Article 26(8)(c) of the decree.
Organizations engaged in commercial road transport of passengers, subject to the penalties described in Article 26 when they commit the specified violations.

id: passenger stop exceeding the permitted time
ten: PASSENGER STOP EXCEEDING THE PERMITTED TIME
mo_ta: A traffic violation involving stopping to pick up or drop off passengers for longer than the permitted duration.
The category of passenger conduct covered by Article 33, Clause 2 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP, punishable by a fine of 1,000,000 to 2,000,000 Vietnamese đồng.
A transport business operator that provides equipment for accessing electronic contracts and passenger lists.

PASSENGER TRANSPORT BY AUTOMOBILE is the activity addressed by Article 45(1). It must comply with applicable legal requirements and limits, including rules for road-traffic order and safety. Transport must follow the registered schedule and route, except in cases of force majeure.

Violations involving contract-based passenger transport, including failing to carry or provide a passenger list or transport contract, carrying people not listed, or transporting people outside the permitted categories. These violations are subject to the fine stated in Article 20, khoản 5.

Violations under Article 26, Clause 7 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP involving passenger-transport cars with at least eight passenger seats (excluding the driver’s seat): operating without the required equipment to record images of the passenger compartment, having equipment that fails to record or store data while the vehicle is in traffic, or falsifying the equipment’s data. The provision sets fines of 5,000,000–6,000,000 Vietnamese đồng for individuals and 10,000,000–12,000,000 Vietnamese đồng for transport businesses or transport-support service organizations.

id: passenger transport vehicle operation without required onboard service staff
ten: PASSENGER TRANSPORT VEHICLE OPERATION WITHOUT REQUIRED ONBOARD SERVICE STAFF
mo_ta: A traffic violation in which a passenger transport vehicle is operated without an onboard service employee when one is legally required.
The activity of transporting passengers in cars, which the text says must comply with the applicable rules.
A passenger carried on a motorcycle, moped, or similar vehicle while using an umbrella.

id: passenger using an umbrella on a bicycle
ten: PASSENGER USING AN UMBRELLA ON A BICYCLE
mo_ta: A traffic violation in which a passenger being carried on a bicycle or electric bicycle uses an umbrella. Article 12 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP prescribes a fine of 100,000 to 200,000 Vietnamese đồng for this conduct.
A person driving a passenger car or a similar passenger-carrying vehicle; under the cited provision, a driver who commits the specified violation is subject to a driving-license point deduction.
Drivers of passenger cars and similar vehicles, including drivers operating passenger transport services on fixed routes or under contract.
Operation of a passenger-carrying motor vehicle, which is explicitly included among the vehicles covered by Article 34.

The violation of carrying more passengers than a passenger vehicle is permitted to carry on a route longer than 300 km. The stated fine is 1,000,000 to 2,000,000 Vietnamese dong for each excess passenger, capped at 75,000,000 dong in total.
Administrative penalty provisions for violations involving equipment that records images of passenger compartments in road-transport vehicles.
Violations involving carrying more passengers than a vehicle is permitted to carry.
A driver of a passenger car or a similar vehicle, the class of road user whose violations are addressed by Article 20.

A violation involving a passenger-transport car with at least eight passenger seats, excluding the driver’s seat, that lacks a passenger-compartment image-recording device, has an inoperative device while in traffic, or has altered device data. The stated fine is 1,000,000 to 2,000,000 Vietnamese đồng.

id: passenger-compartment recording requirements take effect on 1 january 2029
ten: PASSENGER-COMPARTMENT RECORDING REQUIREMENTS TAKE EFFECT ON 1 JANUARY 2029
mo_ta: The effective date under Law 36/2024/QH15 for requirements to install image-recording equipment in passenger compartments of passenger transport vehicles with at least eight passenger seats; implementation follows a roadmap prescribed by the Government.
The prohibited conduct described in Article 12, Clause 2: a person being carried on a bicycle or electric bicycle clings to, tows, or pushes another vehicle or object, or carries a bulky object.
Drivers of automobiles used to transport passengers. Under Article 45, Clause 2 of Law No. 36/2024/QH15, they are responsible for checking that luggage and goods are arranged and secured safely.

A violation involving a passenger-transport car fitted with added or removed seats or berths, or with a luggage-compartment size that does not match the technical specifications recorded in its inspection certificate.
Operating a passenger vehicle without the required badge, without displaying it, with an expired badge, or with a badge not issued by a competent authority.
The person operating a passenger car, a vehicle carrying people, or a similar vehicle; Article 20 addresses violations committed by such operators.
Drivers of passenger cars, vehicles carrying people, and similar vehicles are the people subject to the penalties described in the text.

PASSENGERS are people carried or transported in vehicles, including passenger-transport vehicles and two- or three-wheeled motorcycles or motorbikes. When transported under a passenger-transport contract, they must be identified on the passenger list associated with the signed contract, and the vehicle may not carry anyone who is not listed. In passenger-transport cars, they must receive road-safety and emergency-evacuation instructions before departure and be guided to sit, stand, or lie in the positions prescribed for the vehicle. Motorcycle and motorbike passengers are required to wear helmets that meet national technical standards and fasten them correctly. Passengers also include people getting on or off vehicles at a stopping or parking point on a road.
People being transported in cars who, under the stated rule, must wear seat belts where belts are fitted while participating in road traffic.

id: passengers remaining in a vehicle during ferry transit
ten: PASSENGERS REMAINING IN A VEHICLE DURING FERRY TRANSIT
mo_ta: A traffic-safety violation described in Article 20, Clause 3 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP: allowing passengers to remain in a passenger vehicle while it is going onto a ferry, on the ferry, or leaving the ferry at the landing. Exceptions include the driver, children, pregnant women, elderly or frail people, sick people, and people with disabilities.
A result recognized as passing for a driver-license category when its score equals the required passing score for the corresponding theoretical driving test.
A designated place on a narrow road where a vehicle can move aside to let an oncoming vehicle pass.
Drivers of other road vehicles who pass the location of an accident. They are responsible for transporting injured people to receive emergency care.
The successful completion of the road traffic order and safety legal-knowledge examination, which qualifies a license holder to have the full 12 points restored.
Activities carried out to patrol and control road traffic order and safety, as addressed in Article 65.

The PATROL AND CONTROL FORCE consists of the personnel responsible for carrying out patrol and control duties, including road traffic order and safety patrols. In performing these duties, the force is required to follow the principles stated in the text.

PATROL AND CONTROL FORCES are responsible for patrolling and controlling road traffic order and safety. They are authorized to issue vehicle stop orders and make inspection or control requests while carrying out these duties. They must comply with applicable laws and with patrol and control orders and plans issued by competent authorities, follow the principles governing their work, and accept legal responsibility for their decisions and actions.

id: patrol and control of road traffic order and safety
ten: PATROL AND CONTROL OF ROAD TRAFFIC ORDER AND SAFETY
mo_ta: The activity of patrolling and controlling road traffic order and safety, identified in Article 65 of Law 36/2024/QH15. The text introduces this activity but does not provide further details.)

id: patrol and control orders and plans
ten: PATROL AND CONTROL ORDERS AND PLANS
mo_ta: Orders and plans issued by a competent authority to conduct patrol and control activities on roads
An activity carried out by the traffic police to maintain road traffic order and safety, including identifying deficiencies in roads and traffic organization and reporting causes of traffic disorder.

id: payment of the auction amount to the heir
ten: PAYMENT OF THE AUCTION AMOUNT TO THE HEIR
mo_ta: The heir receives the full amount the winning bidder paid for the auction after the qualifying death and cancellation.

id: payment of the winning bid to the heir
ten: PAYMENT OF THE WINNING BID TO THE HEIR
mo_ta: The payment to the winner’s heir of the full amount the winner paid, when the winner dies under the conditions stated in the text.
The required payment of costs for moving a violating vehicle or hiring someone to move it.

A pedestrian is a person crossing the road. Drivers must yield to pedestrians at marked pedestrian crossings and also at locations where no crossing markings are present. When turning, a driver must yield to a pedestrian crossing at a marked pedestrian crossing.

A **PEDESTRIAN CROSSING** is a marked or designated portion of the road for pedestrians to cross. Under the stated traffic rules, vehicles may not reverse on a pedestrian crossing (Article 16) or make a U-turn there (Article 15).

A PEDESTRIAN CROSSING AREA is a section of roadway marked or otherwise signposted for pedestrians to cross, or a place where pedestrians and wheelchair users are crossing. Overtaking is prohibited in this area.
A person walking across the road; encountering such a pedestrian is the circumstance that triggers the lighting requirements in the cited provision.
Parts of a road designated for pedestrians to cross.
The traffic-rule violation described in the text: a pedestrian entering an expressway, except a person serving in its management or maintenance.
A structure for pedestrians to cross above a road, identified as a designated crossing option.

PEDESTRIAN ROAD CROSSING refers to the circumstance in which a pedestrian or pedestrians are crossing the road. Under the decree, overtaking and the use of high-beam headlights are prohibited in this situation.
Violations of road traffic rules committed by pedestrians; the text states that these violations are subject to a fine of 400,000 to 600,000 Vietnamese đồng.

A penalty provision in Article 10 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. It imposes a fine of 150,000 to 250,000 Vietnamese dong on pedestrians who fail to obey traffic signals, signs, or road markings, except for violations covered by a separate provision.
A monetary penalty of 150,000 to 250,000 Vietnamese đồng imposed on pedestrians for committing one of the specified road-traffic violations.
A pedestrian's violation of road traffic rules, including carrying or transporting bulky objects that obstruct traffic.
A tunnel provided for pedestrians to cross beneath a road, identified as a designated crossing option.
A road or path designated for pedestrians, which pedestrians must use where available

**PEDESTRIANS** are people travelling on foot and participating in road traffic. They are addressed as a road-user category in Article 30 of Vietnamese Law No. 36/2024/QH15, and specified violations of pedestrian traffic rules may incur fines under Article 10.

Pedestrians must follow road-traffic rules and, where available, use sidewalks, road shoulders, pedestrian-only roads, and designated crossings or crossing structures. They must obey traffic signals; where no designated crossing is available, they must check for approaching vehicles and signal by hand when crossing. They must not cross a road divider or cling to a moving vehicle, and must carry bulky items safely without obstructing other people or vehicles.

Pedestrian crossings and designated pedestrian areas are situations in which vehicle operators must take safety precautions. Drivers must yield when required, including at a flashing yellow signal, and pedestrians are entitled to priority when crossing at a marked crossing. Overtaking is prohibited in the designated roadway area used for pedestrian crossing. When the specified signal is given, pedestrians must cross behind the traffic controller. Sections of road reserved for pedestrians are not for motorcycles or mopeds to enter.

id: penalties and driver's license point deductions
ten: PENALTIES AND DRIVER'S LICENSE POINT DEDUCTIONS
mo_ta: Penalties and deduction of driving-license points imposed on drivers who commit vehicle-condition violations in traffic

id: penalties and driver’s license point deduction under article 24
ten: PENALTIES AND DRIVER’S LICENSE POINT DEDUCTION UNDER ARTICLE 24
mo_ta: The penalties and deduction of driver’s license points provided for automobile drivers who violate regulations on transporting live animals or fresh food.

id: penalties and driver’s license point deductions
ten: PENALTIES AND DRIVER’S LICENSE POINT DEDUCTIONS
mo_ta: Administrative penalties and deductions from a driver’s license points are applied to drivers who commit violations while operating motorized four-wheel passenger or goods vehicles.

**PENALTIES AND DRIVING-LICENSE POINT DEDUCTIONS** refers to the enforcement measures specified for vehicle operators covered by Article 34. These measures include penalties for the covered traffic violations and deductions from the driver’s license point balance.

id: penalties and driving-license point deductions under article 25
ten: PENALTIES AND DRIVING-LICENSE POINT DEDUCTIONS UNDER ARTICLE 25
mo_ta: The enforcement measures described in Article 25 for drivers of environmental sanitation vehicles and waste-carrying cars who violate urban transport regulations.

id: penalties and driving-license point deductions under article 32
ten: PENALTIES AND DRIVING-LICENSE POINT DEDUCTIONS UNDER ARTICLE 32
mo_ta: The enforcement measures described in Article 32 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP for specified road traffic violations by vehicle owners. The excerpt gives monetary fine ranges for individual and organizational owners; its heading also refers to driving-license point deductions.
Administrative penalties and corrective measures applied to drivers who commit the specified vehicle-condition traffic violations.
The penalties addressed by Article 40 for violations of regulations governing motor vehicle inspection activities.

id: penalties for motor vehicle traffic violations
ten: PENALTIES FOR MOTOR VEHICLE TRAFFIC VIOLATIONS
mo_ta: The imposition of penalties on drivers who violate road traffic rules while operating motorcycles, motorbikes, or similar vehicles, as provided for in Article 7 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP

id: penalties for passengers violating traffic order and safety regulations
ten: PENALTIES FOR PASSENGERS VIOLATING TRAFFIC ORDER AND SAFETY REGULATIONS
mo_ta: The subject of Article 33 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, which concerns penalties for passengers who violate regulations on traffic order and safety.
The imposition of penalties for violations of road traffic order and safety regulations in road transport and related support services.
The penalties addressed by Article 31 for unlawful vehicle manufacture or assembly and unlawful production, purchase, or sale of vehicle license plates.

id: penalties for vehicle emissions and noise violations
ten: PENALTIES FOR VEHICLE EMISSIONS AND NOISE VIOLATIONS
mo_ta: A provision in Article 13 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP imposing a fine of 400,000 to 600,000 Vietnamese đồng for driving a covered vehicle without an effective muffler or smoke-reduction component, or with one that fails to meet environmental standards for emissions or noise

id: penalties for vehicle owners’ road traffic violations
ten: PENALTIES FOR VEHICLE OWNERS’ ROAD TRAFFIC VIOLATIONS
mo_ta: Article 32 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP provides for fines and driving-license point deductions for vehicle owners who violate road traffic regulations. The excerpt specifies fines of 10,000,000–12,000,000 VND for individuals and 20,000,000–24,000,000 VND for organizations owning automobiles, motorized four-wheel passenger or cargo vehicles, specialized motorcycles, or similar vehicles, when they commit one of the listed violations.

A PENALTY is a sanction imposed on a driver or vehicle operator for committing a specified violation. It may apply to violations involving the transportation of dangerous goods and, where applicable, be imposed in addition to a deduction of points from the driver’s license.

**Penalty and Driving-License Point Deduction** is an enforcement measure provided for in Articles 17 and 32. It involves penalties or fines and the deduction of driving-license points for covered road-traffic violations, including violations by vehicle owners under Article 32.
The penalties and subsequent remedial measures applied to drivers who commit the vehicle-condition violations described in Article 16.

A PENALTY DECISION is a decision imposing an administrative penalty for a violation. The violator must comply with the decision by the specified deadline. It may be issued after a vehicle and related documents have been temporarily seized.
The process of carrying out an administrative penalty decision by the deadline specified in that decision.

id: penalty fine of 10,000,000 to 20,000,000 vietnamese dong
ten: PENALTY FINE OF 10,000,000 TO 20,000,000 VIETNAMESE DONG
mo_ta: The monetary penalty prescribed in Clause 4 for the listed violations by driver-training establishments and driving-test centers.

id: penalty for a vehicle owner’s road-traffic violation
ten: PENALTY FOR A VEHICLE OWNER’S ROAD-TRAFFIC VIOLATION
mo_ta: The imposition of penalties on vehicle owners for violations of regulations related to road traffic, as described in Article 32.

id: penalty for driver-training and testing violations
ten: PENALTY FOR DRIVER-TRAINING AND TESTING VIOLATIONS
mo_ta: The administrative penalty specified in Clause 5 of Article 39 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP: a fine of VND 20 million to VND 30 million for covered violations, including camera-related violations at driver testing centers.

id: penalty for driving without a suitable or valid license
ten: PENALTY FOR DRIVING WITHOUT A SUITABLE OR VALID LICENSE
mo_ta: A legal penalty provision imposing a fine of 18,000,000 to 20,000,000 Vietnamese dong on drivers of cars and specified four-wheeled motor vehicles who drive a vehicle for which their license is unsuitable, or whose license has been expired for at least one year.

id: penalty for failing to carry required documents
ten: PENALTY FOR FAILING TO CARRY REQUIRED DOCUMENTS
mo_ta: An administrative enforcement action described in the decree: a driver may be penalized for not carrying required documents, while the vehicle owner is not penalized if the driver presents the documents or their qualifying electronic information within the stated resolution period.

An administrative fine of 10,000,000 to 15,000,000 Vietnamese dong imposed on a covered testing or certification facility for specified violations, including when at least two inspectors have been penalized under Clause 1 within 12 months of the first penalty.
The penalty imposed on drivers who commit violations identified in Article 7, including the applicable four-point deduction.
The sanction imposed on the instructor according to the rules applicable to the violation committed by the learner.

id: penalty for unauthorized towing by a road rescue vehicle
ten: PENALTY FOR UNAUTHORIZED TOWING BY A ROAD RESCUE VEHICLE
mo_ta: An administrative penalty rule for driving a road rescue vehicle while towing a vehicle that is not eligible for rescue under Clause 1, Article 54 of the Law on Road Traffic Order and Safety. The stated fine is 5,000,000 to 10,000,000 Vietnamese dong

id: penalty for underage motor vehicle operation
ten: PENALTY FOR UNDERAGE MOTOR VEHICLE OPERATION
mo_ta: A penalty specified in Article 18 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP: a fine of 4,000,000 to 6,000,000 Vietnamese dong for a person aged 16 to under 18 who operates a car, a motorized four-wheeled passenger or cargo vehicle, or a similar vehicle.

The sanction applied when an individual or organization continues activities covered by a license or professional practice certificate while deprived of the right to use it; the conduct is treated as if performed without the required license or certificate.

A fine of 2,000,000 to 3,000,000 Vietnamese đồng for specified violations, including using an erased vehicle registration certificate, one with incorrect chassis or engine numbers, or one not issued by a competent authority.

The enforcement action described in Clause 7 of Article 32 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP: vehicle owners are fined for specified road-traffic violations. The stated fines differ for individual and organizational owners and apply to cars, trailers and semi-trailers, certain four-wheeled motor vehicles, specialized motorcycles, and similar vehicles.

PENALTY IMPOSITION is the imposition of an applicable penalty on an individual or organization for committing a specified violation. It also covers cases in which the same person commits a violation addressed by provisions in different articles of Chapter II and penalties are imposed.
The application of a penalty to a driver who commits a covered cargo-vehicle traffic violation; the text says this penalty applies in addition to the driver's license point deduction.
PENALTY PRINCIPLES are the rules governing the imposition of penalties on vehicle owners, drivers, and operators for specified road traffic violations.

**PENALTY PROCEDURE** refers to the procedure for imposing penalties on vehicle owners, drivers, and operators for violations of road traffic order and safety regulations. The procedure for relevant traffic violations is addressed in Article 47 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP.
The procedure and principles for penalizing vehicle owners, including people or organizations treated as owners under the decree.
The specified administrative penalty under Article 26, clause 7, point i, which applies when a transport-business individual directly drives the vehicle.
People aboard passenger-transport vehicles who are required to comply with the rules in Clause 2 of Article 10
A category of people legally permitted under the cited provision to operate mopeds.
People Lacking Civil Act Capacity are individuals who lack or have lost civil act capacity and participate in road traffic. Their participation is addressed in Article 30, including clause 2.
People lacking civil act capacity, identified as people who should be helped when crossing a road.

id: people present at the accident scene
ten: PEOPLE PRESENT AT THE ACCIDENT SCENE
mo_ta: People Present at the Accident Scene are those who are at the location of a road traffic accident. Under Article 80, they have responsibilities that include promptly reporting the accident to the nearest relevant authority or facility and helping protect the injured person’s property.

People with disabilities are among the groups whose participation in road traffic is addressed by Article 30 of Law 36/2024/QH15, including clause 2. Their needs are to be accommodated while they use the road, and they should be assisted when crossing. The text specifically refers to wheelchair users crossing the road and provides that they are given the right of way when required.
The People's Armed Forces are the personnel group whose members may be transported in the bed of a cargo truck when carrying out an urgent duty, as described in the text.
Units belonging to the people's armed forces that are responsible for organizing legal propaganda and dissemination for people under their management.

The PEOPLE’S COMMITTEE is a Vietnamese local government body, with committees operating at multiple administrative levels, including the district level. In the road-traffic accident provisions, the nearest relevant PEOPLE’S COMMITTEE is identified as an authority to notify: drivers or others involved in an accident, people present at the scene, and anyone who discovers an accident may be required or expected to report it promptly to that committee when it is the nearest relevant authority.
A district-level local government body. The text identifies its chairperson as having authority to impose specified administrative sanctions.

id: people's committee chairpersons at all levels
ten: PEOPLE'S COMMITTEE CHAIRPERSONS AT ALL LEVELS
mo_ta: The public officials whose penalty authority is addressed in Article 42 of the decree.
Vietnamese local government bodies whose chairpersons' sanctioning authority is addressed in Article 42.

People’s Committees at all levels are Vietnamese local government bodies responsible, within their respective duties, powers, and jurisdictions, for state management of road traffic order and safety in their localities and for organizing communication and dissemination of related laws. Under Article 42 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, the chairpersons of these committees are assigned administrative sanctioning authority within their respective jurisdictions. The provision addresses the authority of chairpersons at different administrative levels, including provincial- and district-level chairpersons.

id: people's committees of provinces and centrally governed cities
ten: PEOPLE'S COMMITTEES OF PROVINCES AND CENTRALLY GOVERNED CITIES
mo_ta: The People's Committees of relevant provinces and centrally governed cities are local government bodies designated to receive copies of approvals for coordination in management.

id: people's committees of provinces and centrally run cities
ten: PEOPLE'S COMMITTEES OF PROVINCES AND CENTRALLY RUN CITIES
mo_ta: The PEOPLE'S COMMITTEES OF PROVINCES AND CENTRALLY RUN CITIES are local government bodies in the relevant provinces and centrally run cities. They are notified of approvals to coordinate management, and their chairpersons are responsible for implementing the decree.

Vietnam’s People’s Public Security (Công an nhân dân) is the country’s public security and law-enforcement force. It is responsible for, among other functions, driver-training and testing databases and related licensing and certification activities, including records concerning people who operate specialized vehicles within its system.

Article 43 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP sets out the administrative-penalty authority of designated People’s Public Security personnel and units. Depending on their position and the limits specified in the decree, they may issue warnings and fines, confiscate exhibits or vehicles involved in administrative violations, suspend or revoke certain permissions, and apply remedial measures. The provisions identify authorities including officers performing official duties, commune-level police chiefs, police-station chiefs, provincial-level directors, department directors, the Mobile Police commander, and other designated officials. They include a fine limit of 500,000 đồng for specified on-duty officers and allow certain officers to confiscate exhibits or vehicles valued at no more than 15,000,000 đồng.

The force also carries out road-traffic enforcement. Traffic Police may coordinate patrol and control operations with other People’s Public Security units, which can be mobilized and equipped according to their assigned tasks. The governing law for the People’s Public Security provides a basis for additional Traffic Police duties.
Commissioned officers of the People's Public Security who are included among the personnel covered by the circular and are assigned to check legal knowledge concerning road-traffic order and safety.
The PEOPLE'S PUBLIC SECURITY FORCE is Vietnam’s public security force. Applications through the force are listed as one channel for submitting examination applications and registration.

Noncommissioned officers of the People's Public Security who are included among the personnel covered by the circular and are assigned to check legal knowledge concerning road-traffic order and safety.
The People's Public Security of Vietnam is the law-enforcement organization whose authority to impose penalties is addressed in Article 43 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP.

id: people's public security officer on duty
ten: PEOPLE'S PUBLIC SECURITY OFFICER ON DUTY
mo_ta: A PEOPLE’S PUBLIC SECURITY OFFICER ON DUTY is a serving officer performing official duties and authorized to impose administrative sanctions. Depending on the applicable limits, the officer may issue warnings, impose fines of up to 7,500,000 đồng, and confiscate violating items or vehicles up to the prescribed value limit.
Officers of the People's Public Security who are performing official duties; the text states they may impose fines of up to 7,500,000 Vietnamese dong.
The nearest local People’s Committee, identified as an authority to which a driver must promptly report the accident.

id: people’s committee chairpersons at all levels
ten: PEOPLE’S COMMITTEE CHAIRPERSONS AT ALL LEVELS
mo_ta: The officeholders whose sanctioning authority is addressed in Article 42 of the decree.

id: people’s committees at all administrative levels
ten: PEOPLE’S COMMITTEES AT ALL ADMINISTRATIVE LEVELS
mo_ta: Vietnamese local government bodies at different administrative levels; the decree’s Article 42 sets out the sanctioning authority of their chairpersons.

People’s Committees at all levels are Vietnamese local-government bodies whose chairpersons’ authority to impose administrative penalties is addressed by Article 42 of Decree No. 168/2024/ND-CP. The article sets out sanctioning powers for chairpersons at different administrative levels, specifically including commune-level and provincial-level chairpersons.

id: people’s committees of centrally governed cities
ten: PEOPLE’S COMMITTEES OF CENTRALLY GOVERNED CITIES
mo_ta: Government bodies of centrally governed cities responsible, within their assigned duties and authority, for state management of the road traffic order and safety database.
Provincial government bodies responsible, within their assigned duties and authority, for state management of the road traffic order and safety database.

id: people’s committees of provinces and centrally governed cities
ten: PEOPLE’S COMMITTEES OF PROVINCES AND CENTRALLY GOVERNED CITIES
mo_ta: Local government bodies responsible, within their assigned duties and authority, for state management of the road traffic order and safety database.

id: people’s committees of relevant provinces and centrally run cities
ten: PEOPLE’S COMMITTEES OF RELEVANT PROVINCES AND CENTRALLY RUN CITIES
mo_ta: The local government bodies of relevant Vietnamese provinces and centrally run cities. They are to receive approval documents for coordination in managing the approved vehicle activities.

The People’s Public Security of Vietnam is a law-enforcement force whose designated officials and units have enforcement and sanctioning powers under Article 43 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. These powers include imposing fines and other penalties for administrative violations. The force is also referenced in connection with databases relating to vehicle inspection and driver training.

The People’s Public Security is the public security force referenced in the text. The listed databases include information about vehicle inspections and legal-knowledge training certificates within this force.
An emergency-duty activity performed by a priority vehicle; vehicles engaged in this activity are excepted from the specified penalties under the provision.
Health examinations that must be organized for drivers regularly and must cover all content required by regulations.
PERIODIC HEALTH EXAMINATIONS are a required remedial measure under which an organization must arrange regular health examinations for its drivers and employees who serve on vehicles.

The **PERMIT ISSUANCE AND REISSUANCE PROCEDURE**, described in Article 21, governs applications to issue or reissue permits for using signal devices on priority vehicles. Once a complete and valid application is received, it is reviewed within two working days. When an application is handled directly, the permit information must be entered into a database for management.
The process for granting or renewing a permit to use a signal-emitting device on a priority vehicle, including an emergency provision allowing advance communication with the competent authority.

The **Permit Reissuance Procedure** is the administrative process for applying for and receiving a reissued permit to use a signal-emitting device on a priority vehicle. It is the procedure identified as the subject of the text.

id: permit reissuance procedure for priority vehicle signaling equipment
ten: PERMIT REISSUANCE PROCEDURE FOR PRIORITY VEHICLE SIGNALING EQUIPMENT
mo_ta: The procedure described in Article 21, clause 2 of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP for reissuing a permit to use signaling equipment on a priority vehicle. It includes receiving and checking the application, notifying the applicant of deficiencies or refusal, and accepting a qualifying in-person submission with a receipt and scheduled result date.

The administrative procedure required when an existing permit to use a signal device on a military-force priority vehicle does not comply with the decree: the permit holder withdraws the existing permit and requests a new one.

A required corrective measure under Clause 19: revise the permitted cargo weight recorded on the vehicle’s technical safety and environmental protection inspection certificate to comply with current regulations.
The required correction of the vehicle’s permitted cargo weight in its technical safety and environmental protection inspection certificate before the vehicle is used on the road.

id: permitted operating speed determination and speed-sign installation
ten: PERMITTED OPERATING SPEED DETERMINATION AND SPEED-SIGN INSTALLATION
mo_ta: The process of considering and deciding the permitted operating speed for a road section and organizing the installation of corresponding speed signs.
Transport of oversized machinery on a specialized vehicle with a road-use permit, which is explicitly excepted from the described cargo-restraint violation.

The participation in Vietnamese road traffic of foreign-registered right-hand-drive cars and foreign motor vehicles brought into Vietnam for tourism, subject to the scope, routes, and times authorized by competent Vietnamese authorities.

id: permitting an employee or representative to commit a vehicle violation
ten: PERMITTING AN EMPLOYEE OR REPRESENTATIVE TO COMMIT A VEHICLE VIOLATION
mo_ta: The act of assigning a vehicle to, or allowing, an employee or representative to operate it while committing the violation specified in point a, clause 4, Article 34.

id: person assigned to guide road traffic
ten: PERSON ASSIGNED TO GUIDE ROAD TRAFFIC
mo_ta: A person assigned the duty of guiding traffic on roads, identified as one category of road traffic controller.

id: person authorized to impose administrative sanctions
ten: PERSON AUTHORIZED TO IMPOSE ADMINISTRATIVE SANCTIONS
mo_ta: An unspecified person with legal authority to impose administrative sanctions and deduct points from driving licenses

id: person causing a road traffic accident
ten: PERSON CAUSING A ROAD TRAFFIC ACCIDENT
mo_ta: A person who caused a road traffic accident and is identified as someone whose life, health, or property may be infringed.

A person whose violation is recorded in an administrative violation record and who must comply with the penalty decision if required documents or their electronic information are not provided by the stated deadline.
A person present at the scene of a road traffic accident. The text requires the scene to be preserved when someone has died.

id: person present at the accident scene
ten: PERSON PRESENT AT THE ACCIDENT SCENE
mo_ta: A **PERSON PRESENT AT THE ACCIDENT SCENE** is a person who is at the location of a road traffic accident and is covered by the responsibilities set out in Article 80. These responsibilities include providing relevant information about the accident when requested by a competent authority.
A person who helps, provides emergency care to, or transports an injured person for emergency treatment, and whose life, health, or property may be infringed.

A **PERSON RELATED TO THE ACCIDENT** is someone involved in or otherwise connected with a road traffic accident and subject to responsibilities under Article 80. The provision addresses this person alongside the vehicle operator and others present at the scene. Their responsibilities include stopping, warning others of danger, preserving the scene, assisting injured people, and notifying the nearest relevant authority or facility. They must provide identifying and accident-related information to the competent authority and remain at the scene until the police arrive, except where a specified exception applies; in such cases, they must report promptly as required.
A person penalized for an administrative violation whose driving-licence points are deducted and who must be informed of the deduction.

id: person with a disability using a wheelchair
ten: PERSON WITH A DISABILITY USING A WHEELCHAIR
mo_ta: A person with a disability using a wheelchair while crossing at a marked pedestrian crossing; the text identifies their wheelchair as among those to whom a turning driver must yield.
A person identified in the traffic-accident records as having rights or obligations related to the accident.

id: personally operating a vehicle during a violation
ten: PERSONALLY OPERATING A VEHICLE DURING A VIOLATION
mo_ta: A vehicle owner personally operates a vehicle while committing the violation specified in Article 22, clause 3, point a, of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP.
People assigned to carry out specialized inspection duties who, while on official duty, may impose fines of up to 500,000 Vietnamese đồng under Article 44, clause 1.
The age group specified in the provision as being subject to the rule on operating motorcycles and similar vehicles.

id: persons assigned to specialized inspection duties
ten: PERSONS ASSIGNED TO SPECIALIZED INSPECTION DUTIES
mo_ta: **Persons Assigned to Specialized Inspection Duties** are individuals assigned to conduct specialized inspections. While performing their official duties, they are authorized to impose sanctions and apply the specified remedial measures.

id: persons assigned to specialized road inspection duties
ten: PERSONS ASSIGNED TO SPECIALIZED ROAD INSPECTION DUTIES
mo_ta: People assigned to perform specialized road inspection tasks who may impose administrative penalties within the scope of their assigned functions and duties.
Individuals who bring right-hand-drive cars into Vietnam to participate in traffic for purposes other than tourism.

Persons lacking civil act capacity are identified in the heading of Article 30 as a group participating in road traffic. When travelling on a road, they must be accompanied by someone who can guide them.

**PERSONS PERFORMING OFFICIAL DUTIES** are officials carrying out public duties who are authorized to inspect and control, make requests to road users, and pursue operators of road vehicles who flee. When road users fail to comply with their requests or obstruct their work, these officials may take legally prescribed preventive measures and are protected against obstruction or resistance.

id: persons present at the accident scene
ten: PERSONS PRESENT AT THE ACCIDENT SCENE
mo_ta: People present where a road traffic accident occurs; the provision states that they are responsible for participating in protecting the scene.

People who fall under the management authority of the armed forces units, agencies, organizations, or educational institutions and are the intended audience for the legal information and dissemination.
People with disabilities are listed among the groups participating in road traffic in the heading of Article 30.
Individuals who submitted a petition about road traffic order or safety and are to be notified of the results of corrective action.
Organizations that submitted a petition about road traffic order or safety and are to be notified of the results of corrective action.

id: phòng cảnh sát giao thông công an tỉnh, thành phố trực thuộc trung ương
ten: PHÒNG CẢNH SÁT GIAO THÔNG CÔNG AN TỈNH, THÀNH PHỐ TRỰC THUỘC TRUNG ƯƠNG
mo_ta: Traffic Police Divisions of provincial and centrally governed municipal police. Under the decree, they issue, reissue, and revoke permits for eligible priority vehicles belonging to agencies and organizations, except those covered by Clause 1 and emergency-duty military vehicles.

id: phòng hướng dẫn tuyên truyền, điều tra, giải quyết tai nạn giao thông
ten: PHÒNG HƯỚNG DẪN TUYÊN TRUYỀN, ĐIỀU TRA, GIẢI QUYẾT TAI NẠN GIAO THÔNG
mo_ta: A professional division of the Traffic Police Department responsible for guidance on communications, investigation, and resolution of traffic accidents.

id: phòng hướng dẫn, đào tạo, sát hạch, quản lý giấy phép của người điều khiển phương tiện giao thông
ten: PHÒNG HƯỚNG DẪN, ĐÀO TẠO, SÁT HẠCH, QUẢN LÝ GIẤY PHÉP CỦA NGƯỜI ĐIỀU KHIỂN PHƯƠNG TIỆN GIAO THÔNG
mo_ta: A professional division of the Traffic Police Department responsible for guidance on training, testing, and management of vehicle operators’ licenses.

id: phòng hướng dẫn, đăng ký và kiểm định phương tiện
ten: PHÒNG HƯỚNG DẪN, ĐĂNG KÝ VÀ KIỂM ĐỊNH PHƯƠNG TIỆN
mo_ta: A professional division of the Traffic Police Department responsible for guidance on vehicle registration and inspection.

id: phạt tiền từ 2.000.000 đồng đến 3.000.000 đồng
ten: PHẠT TIỀN TỪ 2.000.000 ĐỒNG ĐẾN 3.000.000 ĐỒNG
mo_ta: The imposition of a fine ranging from 2,000,000 to 3,000,000 Vietnamese dong on a driver who commits the specified priority-signal-device violation.
The administrative penalty action authorized by the cited provision, allowing the specified officials to impose a fine of up to 75,000,000 đồng

id: phục hồi điểm giấy phép lái xe
ten: PHỤC HỒI ĐIỂM GIẤY PHÉP LÁI XE
mo_ta: PHỤC HỒI ĐIỂM GIẤY PHÉP LÁI XE là thủ tục khôi phục điểm trên giấy phép lái xe. Theo quy trình được mô tả, người lái xe phải chưa bị trừ hết điểm và không bị trừ điểm trong 12 tháng kể từ lần bị trừ điểm gần nhất; đồng thời phải vượt qua kỳ kiểm tra kiến thức pháp luật về trật tự, an toàn giao thông. Sau khi đạt yêu cầu, điểm giấy phép lái xe được khôi phục lên 12 điểm và cập nhật tự động.

id: picking up and dropping off passengers at designated places
ten: PICKING UP AND DROPPING OFF PASSENGERS AT DESIGNATED PLACES
mo_ta: A required passenger-transport practice specifying that passengers must be picked up and dropped off only at designated locations.

id: picking up or dropping off passengers at prohibited locations
ten: PICKING UP OR DROPPING OFF PASSENGERS AT PROHIBITED LOCATIONS
mo_ta: A violation involving passenger pickup or drop-off on a street at a transport business's headquarters, branch, representative office, or another fixed location rented or used for business cooperation by the transport business.

id: picking up or dropping off passengers on a curve with obstructed visibility
ten: PICKING UP OR DROPPING OFF PASSENGERS ON A CURVE WITH OBSTRUCTED VISIBILITY
mo_ta: A traffic violation involving picking up or dropping off passengers on a curve where visibility is obstructed, except for the conduct separately specified in clause 8 of Article 20.

id: picking up or dropping off passengers on an expressway
ten: PICKING UP OR DROPPING OFF PASSENGERS ON AN EXPRESSWAY
mo_ta: A traffic violation described in Article 20 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP: a driver picking up or dropping off passengers on an expressway. The stated fine is 10,000,000 to 12,000,000 Vietnamese đồng.

id: picking up or dropping off passengers where stopping or parking is prohibited
ten: PICKING UP OR DROPPING OFF PASSENGERS WHERE STOPPING OR PARKING IS PROHIBITED
mo_ta: A traffic violation involving picking up or dropping off passengers at a place where stopping or parking is prohibited.

id: pickup or dropoff at a location not specified in the transport contract
ten: PICKUP OR DROPOFF AT A LOCATION NOT SPECIFIED IN THE TRANSPORT CONTRACT
mo_ta: A violation involving the pickup or drop-off of passengers or specified groups of people at a location different from the one stated in the signed transport contract, except for conduct covered by Article 20, Clause 8.

id: pickup or dropoff at a transport operator's premises or other fixed street location
ten: PICKUP OR DROPOFF AT A TRANSPORT OPERATOR'S PREMISES OR OTHER FIXED STREET LOCATION
mo_ta: A violation involving a contract passenger-transport vehicle picking up or dropping off passengers on a street at the operator's headquarters, branch, representative office, or another fixed location leased or used under a business cooperation arrangement.

id: pilot auction of automobile license plates
ten: PILOT AUCTION OF AUTOMOBILE LICENSE PLATES
mo_ta: The pilot auction of automobile license plates is the activity addressed by Resolution No. 73/2022/QH15.
The destination to which certain vehicles may be transported from production, transport, import, repair, or maintenance locations.
The act of placing signs indicating the maximum operating speed for a period of the day, using supplementary or electronic signs.

The activity of installing signs that indicate the operating speed on a road segment or route. The placement must follow road-signaling laws and account for actual conditions, including road infrastructure, traffic volume, vehicle types, and time of day.

**Placement of Operational Speed Signs** is a regulatory activity in which a competent authority determines where to place signs indicating the operational speed limit on specified roads. It applies to the cases specified in Clause 4 of Article 10.

id: placing a rice threshing machine on a roadway
ten: PLACING A RICE THRESHING MACHINE ON A ROADWAY
mo_ta: The act of placing a rice threshing machine on a roadway, listed as a punishable violation.

id: point a of clause 2 of article 39 of decree 168/2024/nđ-cp
ten: POINT A OF CLAUSE 2 OF ARTICLE 39 OF DECREE 168/2024/NĐ-CP
mo_ta: The provision of Article 39 that is included among those for which traffic police may impose administrative penalties under Clause 2 of Article 41.
A provision referenced in Article 13, Clause 11, as a violation that requires corrective measures.

id: point a of clause 3 of article 34
ten: POINT A OF CLAUSE 3 OF ARTICLE 34
mo_ta: Point a of clause 3 of Article 34, cited as a provision whose violations require excess or oversized cargo to be removed.

id: point a of clause 7 of article 26
ten: POINT A OF CLAUSE 7 OF ARTICLE 26
mo_ta: A referenced category of violation that triggers the corrective measures described in Clause 13.
The referenced provision identifying a violation that results in confiscation of the vehicle’s license plate.

id: point a, clause 1, article 6 of circular 65/2024/tt-bca
ten: POINT A, CLAUSE 1, ARTICLE 6 OF CIRCULAR 65/2024/TT-BCA
mo_ta: A specific provision amended and supplemented by Article 6 of Circular 13/2025/TT-BCA.
A specific provision of Article 6 cited as covering an administrative violation for which a vehicle may be temporarily seized.

id: point a, clause 2 of article 6 of circular 65/2024/tt-bca
ten: POINT A, CLAUSE 2 OF ARTICLE 6 OF CIRCULAR 65/2024/TT-BCA
mo_ta: A specific provision of Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA whose test requirements continue to apply under Circular 105/2026/TT-BCA.

mo_ta: A specific provision of Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA whose test requirements continue to apply under Circular 105/2026/TT-BCA.
The provision referenced in Article 13 as the conduct that triggers a 10-point driver’s-license deduction.
A specific provision of Article 6 cited as covering an administrative violation for which a vehicle may be temporarily seized.
A cited violation provision in Article 32 that, when committed by a vehicle owner directly operating the vehicle, results in a six-point driver's-license deduction.

mo_ta: A provision referenced by Article 7 whose specified traffic violations result in a 10-point deduction from the driver’s license.
A cited legal provision identifying a violation that may result in withdrawal of a vehicle badge.
A specific provision of Article 6 cited as covering an administrative violation for which a vehicle may be temporarily seized.

A cited legal provision identifying a violation that may result in withdrawal of a vehicle badge.

A specific provision of Article 6 cited as covering an administrative violation for which a vehicle may be temporarily seized.
A provision referenced in Article 13, Clause 11, as a violation that requires corrective measures.

mo_ta: Point d of clause 3 of Article 34, cited as a provision whose violations require excess or oversized cargo to be removed.

mo_ta: A provision referenced as an exception to the violations covered by Clause 4 of Article 6.
A specific provision of Article 6 cited as covering an administrative violation for which a vehicle may be temporarily seized.
A provision referenced in Clause 19 of Article 32 as covering conduct that requires restoration of the vehicle to its original condition and re-inspection.
A legal provision of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP cited as an exception to the violations described in Article 32, Clause 9.
The cited provision identifies the violation that results in confiscation of priority-signal equipment installed or used contrary to regulations.

ten: POINT H OF CLAUSE 7 OF ARTICLE 26
mo_ta: A referenced category of violation that triggers the corrective measures described in Clause 13.

The specific provision referenced in Article 39 as the basis for applying a remedial measure to an individual who commits the violation described there.
A provision identifying a violation that triggers the corrective measures specified in Clause 19 of Article 32.
A referenced provision of Article 14 that identifies a vehicle-condition violation requiring corrective action.

mo_ta: The specified points of Article 32 cited as provisions describing violations subject to the sanctioning authority in Article 41.

mo_ta: The specified points of Article 32 cited as provisions describing violations subject to the sanctioning authority in Article 41.

id: points đ, e, g, h, i, and k of clause 5 of article 39 of decree 168/2024/nđ-cp
ten: POINTS Đ, E, G, H, I, AND K OF CLAUSE 5 OF ARTICLE 39 OF DECREE 168/2024/NĐ-CP
mo_ta: The provisions of Article 39 that are included among those for which traffic police may impose administrative penalties under Clause 2 of Article 41.

The police are an organization whose vehicles may receive priority when performing emergency missions or other urgent duties, and may be equipped with priority signal lights as provided by the cited regulation. Under Clause 3 of Article 40 of Law 36/2024/QH15, police motor vehicles used for security purposes are exempt from the service-life limit.

**POLICE AGENCY** is a government authority that performs duties related to road traffic order and safety, national security, and public order. Within its assigned functions and duties, it is responsible for acting when it detects or receives information about an unexpected road-traffic situation that disrupts order or safety, including situations covered by Article 76, Clause 1. It must promptly organize personnel to go to the scene, take prescribed measures, and help restore or maintain traffic order and safety.

In a road traffic accident, the POLICE AGENCY is among the authorities that must be notified. People present at the scene are required to notify it promptly, and a driver or another person involved may be required to report promptly to the nearest police authority in specified circumstances. Police personnel are expected to respond to the scene, carry out measures required by law, and help resolve the accident. The POLICE AGENCY leads the accident response, coordinates with relevant agencies, organizations, and individuals, and organizes personnel and equipment for rescue and relief. When needed, it reports the accident to the competent authority to mobilize additional resources and coordinates with insurance enterprises to arrange rescue vehicles.

For an accident involving a vehicle carrying dangerous goods, the POLICE AGENCY leads the response. It must promptly notify the relevant functional unit, secure the scene, direct traffic, and prevent people and vehicles from entering the area.

The POLICE AGENCY also manages auctioned vehicle license plates and may be a place where a winning bidder registers a plate. In addition, it may request drivers and onboard service staff to cooperate in duties related to national security and public order.

id: police arrival at the accident scene
ten: POLICE ARRIVAL AT THE ACCIDENT SCENE
mo_ta: The arrival of police personnel at the accident scene, which marks the point until which the driver and people related to the accident are generally required to remain there.

The Police Authority is one of the nearest authorities to which a driver or operator must promptly report the described accident. Within its functions and duties, it is also responsible for responding when it detects or receives information about an unexpected situation that causes disorder or threatens traffic safety on roads.

id: police department for administrative management of social order
ten: POLICE DEPARTMENT FOR ADMINISTRATIVE MANAGEMENT OF SOCIAL ORDER
mo_ta: The **Police Department for Administrative Management of Social Order** is a department of the People’s Public Security. Under the applicable decree, its director is authorized to apply specified remedial measures and, under Article 43, Clause 6, to impose fines of up to 75,000,000 Vietnamese đồng.
Drivers serving in the police forces while performing security duties; their age requirements are prescribed by the Minister of Public Security.

id: police for administrative management of social order
ten: POLICE FOR ADMINISTRATIVE MANAGEMENT OF SOCIAL ORDER
mo_ta: The Police for Administrative Management of Social Order (Vietnamese: *Cảnh sát quản lý hành chính về trật tự xã hội*) are authorized under Article 41 to penalize specified administrative violations concerning road-traffic order and safety, within their assigned functions and duties.

id: police for fire prevention, fire fighting and rescue
ten: POLICE FOR FIRE PREVENTION, FIRE FIGHTING AND RESCUE
mo_ta: The police force responsible for fire prevention, firefighting, and rescue; its fire engines are designated priority vehicles when carrying out firefighting duties.

The POLICE FORCE operates priority vehicles on urgent or emergency missions. When performing these duties, its vehicles are subject to rules governing the installation and use of legally prescribed priority-vehicle signals, including flashing blue and red lights and a priority siren.

**Police Forces** are Vietnamese forces performing national security, national defence, and security duties. Their members’ driving licences—including licence formats, issuance, and use—are governed by regulations prescribed by the Minister of Public Security and, where applicable, the relevant ministers. The Minister of Public Security also prescribes applicable driver-age requirements.

Police members performing these duties are covered by provisions on driver training, driving tests, and certification, including specialized training, testing, and certification for motorcycle operators. A driver examination centre may organize examinations under the stated exception.

Police vehicles are designated priority vehicles when used for urgent duties and may use priority signal devices when responding to emergencies. Police-force vehicle-inspection data, and data relating to driver training, licensing, road-traffic-law certificates, and vehicle operators, are excluded from the specified databases and responsibilities assigned to the Ministries of Transport and Construction.
The police forces or agencies serving the relevant units and localities; they are identified as parties to whom the circular applies.
Personnel from a police agency who are expected to arrive at the accident scene.

A **POLICE POST** is a police unit whose chief or head is authorized under the decree, within the scope of assigned duties, to impose administrative penalties for specified road-traffic violations. The chief is named in Article 41 as having authority to sanction those violations and is also listed in Article 43, including Clause 3, among officials empowered to impose administrative penalties. Under Article 43, Clause 3, the chief may impose fines of up to 2,500,000 Vietnamese dong and apply specified remedial measures.

The **POLICE POST CHIEF** is the official who heads a police post. Within the official’s assigned functions and duties, the chief is authorized under Articles 41 and 43 to impose administrative penalties for specified road-traffic and other administrative violations and to apply specified remedial measures. Under Article 43, Clause 3, the chief may also seize objects and vehicles used in administrative violations when their value does not exceed 5,000,000 đồng.
A generic official heading a police post, listed in Article 43 as having authority to impose sanctions.
POLICE POSTS are police units whose chiefs are granted authority under the decree to impose administrative penalties, within their assigned duties, for specified road traffic violations.

The police agency’s required response upon receiving an accident report: promptly dispatching personnel to the accident scene and carrying out legally prescribed and other measures to resolve the accident.

A **POLICE STATION** is an authorized enforcement body whose chief may impose specified administrative penalties under Articles 41 and 43 of the decree. These powers include sanctions for certain violations involving road traffic order and safety, within the chief’s assigned functions and duties. At a border gate or in an export processing zone, the station chief may, under Article 43, Clause 3, impose fines of up to 2,500,000 Vietnamese dong.

The **POLICE STATION CHIEF** is the head of a police station within the People’s Public Security. The role is held by an unnamed official and carries authority, within assigned functions, duties, and responsibilities, to impose administrative sanctions for specified violations of road traffic order and safety and to apply specified remedial measures. Under the cited provisions of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, this authority is described in Articles 41 and 43; Article 43, clause 3, authorizes fines of up to **2,500,000 Vietnamese dong**. The chief’s powers are limited to the violations and measures specified in the applicable provisions and to the scope of the chief’s assigned responsibilities.
A generic official heading a police station, listed in Article 43 as having authority to impose sanctions.

Police stations are entities whose chiefs are granted authority under the decree to impose administrative sanctions for specified road-traffic violations, within the scope of their assigned functions and duties.
A police team whose leader is among the officials granted administrative penalty powers under Article 43.
A police team leader, authorized alongside specified other officials to impose administrative penalties and apply remedial measures under Article 43.
Police teams whose leaders are among the officials granted the stated authority under the decree.
Police units and localities responsible for reporting difficulties or obstacles encountered while implementing the circular.
Political events are among the activities for which temporary use of a roadway or sidewalk may be permitted, subject to an approved plan.
Political and social organizations whose vehicles are eligible to receive license plates with a blue background and white letters and numbers under the stated provision.
A pontoon bridge is a type of bridge referenced as a route for vehicles crossing)

PONTOON BRIDGE CROSSING is covered by Article 23. Road users must follow the traffic controller’s instructions. Under Clause 4, motor vehicles and motorcycles intended for specialized use must cross in a single line in their direction of travel and must not obstruct people or vehicles moving in the opposite direction.

Populated areas are densely inhabited geographic zones that serve as reference points for distinguishing road segments located outside them. In these areas, horn use is restricted between 10 p.m. and 5 a.m., except by priority vehicles.
A port is a location that may serve as either the origin or destination for transporting certain vehicles to their place of use under the conditions of the applicable permit and law.

The violation of failing to stop the vehicle immediately, preserve the scene, or assist injured people after a vehicle is directly involved in a traffic accident. The text states that this conduct is punishable by a fine of 2,000,000 to 3,000,000 Vietnamese đồng, subject to the stated exception.

The **POSTAL SERVICE** is a permitted mail-delivery channel through which applicants may send prescribed written notices, applications, dossiers, requests, and supporting or follow-up documents to the competent authority. Submissions may relate to intelligent transport vehicle operating permits, approvals, road traffic law examination registration, permit reissuance, or other required procedures.
A situation that may compromise road traffic safety; the text says vehicle horns may be used to warn road traffic participants when such a situation arises
The act of pouring substances that make a roadway slippery.
The practical instruction required as part of driver training for people seeking a driver’s license.
The activity of an instructor teaching a learner to practice driving.
A person who teaches practical driving. Under the text, an instructor who allows a learner to commit a specified driving-related violation is subject to the penalty applicable to that violation.

PRACTICAL DRIVING INSTRUCTORS teach learners to drive vehicles in different categories. The cited provisions address two related requirements: an instructor may violate the rules by failing to carry a valid permit for a vehicle used for driving practice, and a driver-training facility must have enough practical driving instructors to support its planned use of training vehicles.
A driving lesson in which a learner practices driving and an instructor is required to sit beside the learner to supervise steering.
The in-course driving test referenced in the provision, during which a center must publicly announce candidates’ errors through an audio system.

id: practice driving without the required badge
ten: PRACTICE DRIVING WITHOUT THE REQUIRED BADGE
mo_ta: A violation in which an instructor allows a learner to drive a practice vehicle without a learner-driver badge or without wearing the badge.
The required check of a vehicle’s safety condition before it participates in road traffic.

Pregnant women are identified in Article 30 of Law 36/2024/QH15 as a group participating in road traffic. Their participation is addressed under Article 30, including clause 2, and the text says they should be accommodated and helped when crossing a road.
The official act of preparing records for administrative violations, whose authority in the road-traffic field is specified in Article 46.
The act of preparing official records documenting administrative violations.
The event of a vehicle preparing to pass another vehicle on the road.

Educational establishments, including preschool and general education institutions, where activities teaching legal knowledge about road traffic order and safety are to be organized and compliance with traffic laws is to be managed.

Preschool children are young passengers whose transportation is addressed by road-traffic safety provisions, including Articles 27 and 46 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP. The provisions cover children carried in commercial transport vehicles and in vehicles used by educational institutions for preschool pickup and drop-off. They address vehicle identification requirements, including required paint coloring, and require educational institutions to ensure children’s safety during pickup and drop-off. Preschool children are also identified as recipients of instruction on laws concerning road-traffic order and safety.

Preschool Educational Institutions are establishments serving preschool-age children. Their teaching programs and activities are to provide age-appropriate education on road traffic laws, traffic order, and road safety. This education includes safety while walking and while travelling in road vehicles, as well as awareness of the dangers and consequences of failing to follow traffic safety rules. These institutions are also settings in which instruction on traffic-law compliance is organized and compliance with relevant road traffic laws is managed.
